rows.title: So tired…
rows.titleText:
You slope off to bed, to sleep. You just need to sleep. 


For the past few weeks, it feels that goal has eluded you. Each night, you lie down and close your eyes and wake in the morning feeling more tired than when you went to sleep in the first place. You wake up confused and disorientated and don’t know why. You don’t dream. At least…you don’t think you do.


You look at your treacherous bed, narrowing your already narrowed eyes. Perhaps this time…


You refuse to jinx yourself, lying on the bed, letting exhaustion take you.

objects.title: Sleep
objects.text:
You close your eyes, your mind drifting to mush.

Perhaps this time… Perhaps this time…

rows.title: You Run…
rows.titleText:
Your old school whips by. A blur; a building; a remembrance. It has a different purpose now. An office? A business of some kind? It’s not your school any more: like a familiar actor donning another role. Its halls are twisted, its purpose unknown. All you know is that you’re going to be late. So very very late.

You’re going to be late and…

objects.title: You Don’t Care
objects.text: Why are you running? You laugh instead. It doesn’t matter; it never did! You don’t know what you were worried about. Turning a corner, you decide to get out of here. You never liked it much in the first place.

objects.title: You’re Lost
objects.text: If you could just find the right room! The familiar doors open into unfamiliar ways as stairs spiral up without handrails and cupboards lead into crawlspaces. If you can just keep moving forward, you should get there, in the end.

objects.title: Late Late Late!
objects.text: You’re late. You know it. They’re going to know it as well! A hot sweat of shame floods your skin, your disorientation made worse by your roving eyes. Others see. Mocking laughter chases. You’re desperate to get there yet hate the thought of arriving.

rows.titleText: The outside beckons. Nature and the sliding open spaces and their unknown strangenesses. You go forwards, walking on grass, through fields and fresh places, searching, finding, and searching again. You’re looking for…

objects.title: Nature?
objects.text: The air feels fresh, like a blanket. Nature is kind and welcoming and you walk where no bad things wait, wondering with legs and without words, what is over the hill. Past the trees and bushes and living things.

objects.title: People
objects.text: There are children here, from that school place. They watch and you don’t like it. They’re wrong. You know that they are and that they shouldn’t be. You pick up your pace, feeling their eyes. They’ll chase you if they can.

rows.titleText: Around and around and around. Maybe this way? You don’t know. You do know. It’s all so familiar to you. You were going…where? This way. No… The scene changes, having always been different, the halls leading to places unfamiliar.

objects.title: It’s all so fascinating
objects.text: You sometimes walk and sometimes crawl, following a path that is always branching yet always simple, going exactly where you’re going. It loops and climbs and ends and begins, leaving you where you know where you are before you go back to where you know you’re not.

objects.title: You Shouldn’t Be Here
objects.text: The rooms are broken now. Less habitable. The more you look around, the more you see. Ceilings gone. Walls gone. The floors creak, sounding like falling. Breaking. The old place becomes a condemned place. It’s not safe. You need to get out. Which way was it?

rows.titleText: This door? No. This door? No. This door? No. This door? You don’t know which way anymore and it’s getting really really urgent! You have to- What was that? This door? No. If you don’t find a way soon then... bad things will happen. You know it!

objects.title: This Door.
objects.text: The room is different. Not where you were going, but a way there? It is safe and nice, though odd. Friendly. It makes you curious. Who is in here? You know them. This place at least. If you can find them, they’ll help.

objects.title: It’ll Get You!
objects.text: You saw it. It was, behind you. Back there. You need to keep running. You escape through a door, then another door, and crawl through a hole, and keep going. It’s dangerous. High. Sharp. The thing behind is more dangerous. You keep moving.

rows.titleText: You move and view, going somewhere and yet going nowhere. There is a path. It changes when you look at it, in direction and makeup, so you don’t, simply following it with a mild curiosity. There is no wind. No air. The trees stop it.

objects.title: Keep Walking
objects.text: The path hasn’t lead you astray so far. You follow it. Have followed it. For hours and hours now. It irritates. Why haven’t you gotten there yet? Grass turns to mud turns to stone turns to grass. The canopy thickens. It’s darker now. Where are you?

objects.title: There Is Beauty
objects.text: You’re not alone. They are here. You’ve finally found what you were looking for and go to them, sinking into each other. Their desire. Their soft lips. Passion fires between you, strangers, willing, open, warm. They tingle against your skin.

rows.titleText: You walk, keeping your head down, so they don’t see. You feel their eyes on you and know that they are watching, like birds of prey, searching for weakness. Your shoulders hunch, feeling soft scratches at your senses.

objects.title: Climb to Escape
objects.text: There is a tree, with steps. A treehouse up above, like a cartoon shanty town floating in the canopy. You begin to climb, wooden steps and wooden branches propelling you up and away, into house and through, up ladders and hand holds and ropes.

objects.title: Chase!
objects.text: You run. They run. Feet beat the ground like heavy rain, a herd, a many legged thing. You don’t look back. You don’t dare to. You run past the unimportant, turning, climbing, hiding, and running when it catches up.

rows.titleText: You go down, into a tunnel. Narrow. You need to crawl. Corners ahead take your sight away, leaving you feeling your way forward with instinct and knowing. There was…a place. If you could just get back to it…

objects.title: A Door
objects.text: This one looks older, overgrown, leading into nature. There are woods through it, the wide open space looking fresh and new, the narrow squeeze before already left behind. Looking at it from the other side, you can’t go back. You’d never find your way.

objects.title: A Sound
objects.text: Something is in here with you. It’s coming for you. You shouldn’t have come this far. Scurrying on, you look for somewhere to hide. If you can hide, it will go. You’re in the guts of somewhere. Pipes guide your way, through backrooms and service passages.

rows.titleText: There is a hole in the wall. Old. It’s been here a long time, caused by neglect, though the rest of the room looks fine. You climb through, looking around at the place you’ve taken yourself to and finding…

objects.title: An Old Friend
objects.text: Of course! It’s… From… The details are slippery. Irrelevant. They have a face you know, and a smile, and a hug. Oh but you’re glad to see them! They’ll know. They’ll help. Together, you go in a new direction, with a new purpose.

objects.title: A Way Up
objects.text: Up is out. This is a truth you know: the path you need to take to get out of here. The steps look old and tired, and steep, like a ladder, but they lead to a place you’d rather be. The place you’re going. You put a foot on the first, and your hand on the fourth.

rows.titleText: You mess with the trinkets of someone else. Small things. Odd things. You know you can. They won’t mind. They’re here, watching over your shoulder, and as you turn to greet them, you find yourself face to face with…someone…

objects.title: A Friend
objects.text: Oh, it’s…yes, you remember. Where were they from again? They’re here now, smiling. You smile back, and arm in arm, you walk together in lively debate, erudite and brilliant, making plans of generous scope. It’s so obvious. Why has no one thought of it?

objects.title: A Stranger
objects.text: They’re unfamiliar. Strange, which make sense. They should be as odd as the room. They’re no threat to you, and lean close. They have a secret to tell, to take with you, to place in your hand. Are you sure you don’t know them? You’ve seen that face before.

rows.titleText:
There is no hiding. It’s here. Ugh. Cornered. You can’t escape, and you don’t want to be here. Why can’t it just leave you alone! If you could stop it, you could leave. Got to stop it. You don’t want it. Got to…

Got to…

objects.title: Freeze
objects.text: It looks at you. You look at it. You don’t move. It doesn’t move. What is it? What… does it want? You ask, your words strong and fierce and friendly. Maybe it’s friendly? It could be. It approaches you to reach out. You watch it, curious.

objects.title: Fight
objects.text: Punches land through water. Weak sluggish splashes that don’t do anything. You’re frantic. Desperate. Frightened. You can’t do anything, flailing like a child against a titan. You’re going to die. You’re going to die.

rows.titleText:
The pleasant woods never were, old dead trees all around, and the sun has set on life. You’ve walked too far. The forest is a cold place now, filled with eyes and hidden paths and old dead branches. Wherever the woods go, they go badly. You should leave…
You should…

objects.title: Find a Tavern
objects.text: There’s one. You walk to it. There is light and sound and laughter. Celebration. Joy. Warmth. Like a fantasy. It stands in a void, and you’re through the door, welcomed by those inside. The coat hooks are broken. You don’t need them.

objects.title: Run to the Shack
objects.text: The woods are cold and uninviting, but there is a house. Run down. Drafty. I looks the kind of place bad things happen in, but it’s exposed out here. Inside is better. You hope the door doesn’t make noise. You hope no one is home.

rows.titleText: Passionate arms entangle you, stroke you, hold you, want you. Lips come to yours and libido runs wild, giving in. You want this. There is a bed. You fall to it, landing atop your partner, rolling, engaging. You want this. You want this.

objects.title: Passion
objects.text: Your wildest and weirdest wants finally satisfied. The strangeness of it an irrelevance. You push yourself against them, melding and merging with moans of passionate embrace. Let this go on forever, and ever, and ever.

objects.title: Horror
objects.text: A second look gives a second face, horrific, familiar, familial, monstrous. You keep going, half on autopilot, driven by passions inertia, you other half -your lesser half- a horrified spectator, twisting and begging for the fantasy to end.

rows.titleText: You climb and climb and climb, one hand before the other, as though crawling upward. You climb up long winding tunnels, ladders in wide open space, through rooms filled with oblivious people, and across gnarled and twisted passageways.

objects.title: Fall
objects.text: Your hands slip, flailing in air, scrabbling for purchase and finding only dust and grit, sloughing away as your body contorts to keep from falling. The rung you stand upon wavers, weak and crumbling and unable to hold for long. It doesn’t.

objects.title: Reach the Top
objects.text: You climb until there is nothing left to climb, crawling up to the top of the highest point. So high there are clouds. The top of a tower or mountain; you can’t decide. It looks cold. You crawl forward so you are not near the hole and its fathomless drop.

rows.titleText: Hand in hand, arm in arm, you go out to fight them! To organise! Together, you’re plans will overthrow all others and finally fix the problems of the world. You and they huddle around a table and plot in the dark. The plan nears completion. Viva la revolución!

objects.title: Victory!
objects.text: Victory is inevitable. It always was and always will be. You go with your friend to celebrate. Tyrants are quashed, hero’s made, there should be festivals! Days named after this day. Your friend takes you some place; a place where good people are welcome.

objects.title: Failure!
objects.text: How? How could it all go so badly? You ask your friend, beg them to know, but they are fading. Dying in your arms. You weep for them as you beg, leaning close as they try to speak, to answer your desperate question. You listen for the secret. Listen till it hurts.

rows.titleText: You listen, ready to hear what is given, but the stringer does not speak. Not yet. You have to ask. They are close, ready, their face a moment from your own face, so familiar yet so unknown, smiling. You have not asked yet. They’re so close. Do you dare to?

objects.title: No
objects.text: As soon as you think the possibility their closeness brings, they know. Their smile widens, their distance shortening. They begin to sink, sliding from your view, smile still wide. You place your hands in their hair, letting them communicate without words.

objects.title: Yes
objects.text: They lean to your ear, their press and closeness palpable, their lips loud before even speaking. The roar of a whisper comes, like the churn of the ocean, washing into your ear something true. Something profound. You listen. You can’t not.

rows.titleText: You run and run. Crawl and crawl. Get away. Hide. Escape. An endless maze complete with a chasing monster you can no longer see. You climb, up and out and in and through, until you’re sure it cannot find you. You huddle, quiet as a mouse.

objects.title: Until You Don’t Need To
objects.text: Safe now, reality shifts. A warm place beckons, safer even than hiding, light and laughter that could keep any monster away. You hear it and know it, and soon, by crawling, you see it, welcoming you like an old familiar friend.

objects.title: Digging Deeper Into Dark
objects.text: The feeling doesn’t leave you, predator eyes still searching. You crawl into dark spaces, squeezed under great weights, a cave or crawlspace, old and callous. The hunted feeling doesn’t go, driving you on, into worse terrain.

rows.titleText: With an arched back and empty arms, you plunge down, screaming, flailing, the ground racing toward you, so far becoming so terrifyingly near, until the hard ground-

objects.title: You Jump Awake
objects.text:
You were…You…

Fuck. Your heart pounds in your chest, your body breathing in your bed. What a…dream? Was that a… So tired. And you have work tomorrow as well. Crazy. You’ll have to tell someone about this, sometime. Tomorrow.

You’ll remember this in the morning.

You’ll…

You let your heavy eyes close, slipping away. You don’t dream for the rest of the night. Maybe tomorrow you’ll get some rest.

rows.titleText: The room has a narrow entrance, but is bright and cosy and welcoming inside, filled with voices that carry good cheer, even if you don’t see any people specifically. This looks like the place that adventures start in, or relaxed conversations between effortlessly cool people. That makes you cool, you think.

objects.title: Relax
objects.text: You’re sitting in a chair, out of the hubbub, but near enough to enjoy it all. A wallflower, relaxing after a hard day. You need this. You’ve had such trouble relaxing lately. Can’t seem to get a moments rest. You deserve this.

objects.title: Poison!
objects.text: You clutch your throat. You must have drunk it? You know it’s inside, burning a path through you. Betrayal! Deception! The kindly pub takes on a sinister tone. Who did it? You? You? Wherever you point, likely suspects are laid bare.

rows.titleText: You’re in a brothel, tired and satisfied, and alone. Where did they go? It doesn’t matter. The place at first glance looks exactly like what you’d expect: seedy and vulgar. On a second, it possesses oddities. Why is there a toilet in the hallway? Why are the walls carpeted?

objects.title: It Doesn’t Matter
objects.text: The places strangeness doesn’t distract from its purpose. This is a place to relax, and you do so need to relax. Picking a bed, you lie down upon it, reclining, the comfiest chair, where you can watch the empty world go by in post coital bliss.

objects.title: Better Find Someone
objects.text: There should be someone around here. This is a brothel. Do you have to pay? You’ve never… You begin to look, exploring with muted curiosity. It’s warm and nice, but where are the people? The backrooms? Someone should really find them.

rows.titleText: The words buzz and burn in your head. Why would they say that? What possible reason? Could it even be true? The revelation changes everything…somehow. People should know; you shouldn’t carry this knowledge alone. You think for a moment.

objects.title: Wallowing In Confusion
objects.text: Of course! It can’t be? You pour the truths between your hands, loosing precious reason as you do. The more you think on it, the less it makes sense, yet it is true, you’re sure: the fault must lie with you.

objects.title: And Start To Worry
objects.text: It cannot be. The implications if it were… You’re pacing, trying to disprove, yet only proving it truer. What should you do? What can you do? It’s not here that you can do it, whatever it is. You’ll need to prepare. Everyone will.

rows.titleText: You move inside the cold house, old stone on the walls. A tall place, like an old castle inside. Each step is loud enough to let everyone know, but it’s not the kind of place where you want people to know. You go forward, searching, stepping lightly.

objects.title: You Find The Owner
objects.text: A woman, who you know is the snow queen, waits for you, sitting atop her throne. She doesn’t smile. It’s her job not to. But she looks mighty and kind and beautiful. In a moments fluster, you don’t know what to say. Hopefully, she won’t take offence.

objects.title: You Find The Residents
objects.text: They’re dead. Everyone. The whole castle has been left a cold culling ground. They’re piled up, frozen and withered, and it feels wrong, like there is a space left for you. The bodies watch with eyeless sockets, and a knowing pain grips your chest.

rows.titleText: Hands grab you, hauling you deep and screaming, sliding, until slamming into the pit of some cold place. It’s a lair for something. Bones jut from the ground like grass, skulls like river stones. Your heart hammers, your hands searching everywhere but where you know it waits. Searching, and finding…

objects.title: Your Courage
objects.text: Anger flairs, and action with it. From the bones you pull just what you need: a sword. A thing of beauty. It shines with its internal magic, and levelling it at the monster is enough to lessen it. To make a coward of it. You charge, victorious!

objects.title: Nothing
objects.text: Just bones. Your bones. The thing pounces and rakes a claw upon you. You fall back. There is no blood, but you are injured. No pain, but the knowledge it will come. You hold your belly, whimpering, keeping things inside as you try to get away.

rows.titleText: You walk and think for hours. Days. The churn of your thoughts boiling over, philosophy mixing with history mixing with thaumaturgy, all bolstered with knowing and random epiphany. It feels more like falling than walking. Sinking than thinking. A sudden question rings out, like a fresh note.

objects.title: Are Demons Real?
objects.text: A disquieting notion. You know that they are, and that it fits with the evil in the world and the world to come. Wait…you’ve realised this before, haven’t you? For a sudden moments déjà vu, you are certain of it, but it slips away before you can grasp it. You walk on, pondering the rest.

rows.titleText: A knocking breaks you reprieve. Hand on wood. It silences everything, though everything has always been silent, and it draws you up and on, to find its source. If someone is at the door, it makes sense to let them in. Charitable, even.

objects.title: The Source Eludes
objects.text: It had happened once, with each after being an echo of recollection. Perhaps it wasn’t human; just a banging of something in the wind? You travel onward anyway, drawn to the memory of it. Could it have been your imagination? You open a door.

rows.titleText: You slide across the ground, pulling yourself in dragging heaves. You’re too weak to stand. To exhausted. Your core burns with heat. Agony is sure to follow. Nothing else does. You’ve crawled for hours now. Can’t sleep. You’ll die if you sleep.

objects.title: Outcrawled Your Injury
objects.text: You stand. Now that you’re far enough away, they won’t notice. They can’t see that it was all nothing. Of course it was. You outsmarted them. A nervous laugh barks out your throat and you pickup the pace, jogging now. You don’t stop holding your belly though.

rows.titleText: Forearmed, you step out, walking, searching for somewhere defensible. You will not fall or falter; this challenge is yours to overcome. You just need somewhere you can defend, or an enemy you can face. You just need a chance!

objects.title: There Is No Good Ground
objects.text: Beasts are coming. Creatures of overwhelming number, or mythical prowess, and you have nowhere to stand to face them. You search about, looking for something. Looking for… Whatever it is, it’s not here. It must be in this direction!

rows.titleText: Wondering and wondering, your legs take you to a place. It’s cold here. And empty. Like an old abandoned castle, floating in the sky. The place looks odd. You look out from a balcony and see nothing but mist. Where to now?

objects.title: The Last Door
objects.text: There is one more way to go. A door your fingers tremble to touch. No, you’ve… You’ve opened it before. Some time ago. Unlike the door, you can’t quite put your fingers on it. Well, you walk through, going forward to the last stop on your journey.

rows.titleText: The pain stops. Or it never started. You know you’re cold. Cold enough to shatter if you’re not careful. The dead remain, but the wrongness doesn’t, bleached bone skulls now smiling with warm welcome. You smile back.

objects.title: I’m I Dead?
objects.text: The question should be frightening, but it isn’t. If this is death, it is nothing to be afraid of. You walk past piles of bodies, onwards. You don’t know where, but you go there without fear. Perhaps a warm place. Or…a familiar place. Odd. There should be one in this direction, but you don’t know how you could know that.

rows.titleText: You move forward, towards something in the distance. Something strange. Something familiar. You’ve seen it before, yet have no clue what it is. You’re holding your breath. Squeezed tight by the sight. You don’t want to see it. But you NEED to see it.

objects.title: Approach
objects.text: You walk the distance, tentatively, the thing more real than you are. The light, the long reach, narrows, as you close, focusing, revealing, changing. Each step you take makes it what it is; what it chooses to be. You force yourself to take each and every one.

rows.title: To Dream Perchance To Sleep
rows.titleText:
Finally, you stand before it, as you never have before, and as you have so many times already. Each step has left fatigue in you, and knowledge as well: the understanding that you have done this before and failed before, countless times, and every time here. This light. This thing. The end of your road. The last and ever offered chance.

You reach out, examining, thinking, with hands and eyes. Deciding and being decided upon. The last distance gives the last clarity.

objects.title: Awaken Tired
objects.text:
You stand before a pole of light, beautiful in design and tied with intricate mesmerising ribbons, rising and waving like the flames of a fire. It’s breath-taking to see, but, it hovers above the ground, as though too good for it, and you know with a crushing despair that one breeze will blow it away. 

As though summoned by the thought, you watch as the pole flies away, twisting and writhing before landing high up in the sky, punching it, as though a great weight upon a spread sheet, tearing it all from the grip of the horizon. Sky wrapped and fleeing from you, the dream falls into darkness. 

As the light goes out, the last remnant of the dream is your sadness, pouring forth, and the knowledge that perhaps you’ll have this dream again, though perhaps not. Knowing now, in a flash of certainty and revelation, that this is a dream, and one you’ve had before, you realise with all your fading faculties that you didn’t get it right, and what’s more…

You’ll be tired again tomorrow.

objects.title: Sleep Onward
objects.text:
You stand before a strange pole, intricate in design, fixed firmly into the earth. The mast of a sailing ship, cutting the waves! No, an old weapon -a spear!- rammed into the breast of a vast dragon! No…

No.

You take a moment to focus and clear your mind so that you might see and understand. So much fuzz and confusion. Thinking now, it’s obvious. It’s a marker. It marks a path that you can take. That you can journey without walking, to a place you’ve never been, yet you know by heart. You just…can’t remember the details.

You setoff, and as you do, you realise you never setoff at all. You were already on this journey. You have been for a long time now.

It feels good to start making progress again.

objects.title: Awaken Screaming
objects.text:
The light is buried, in the earth. You fall and sink your hands into thick mud, up to your elbows, your shoulders, flailing through, searching desperately, pushing by thick inches. It’s hopeless. You try to pull free, feeling only your knees sink, the mud and filth swallowing your legs greedily. 

The thing you search for, that you weep for the absence of, is not here, but something has found you, not letting go of even a single scrap of your flesh, pulling you in, the mud now black like tar. You scream and thrash, your body weak, your purchase absent, until the filth finds your jaw, pulling it and your face into darkness. You cannot scream. You cannot breathe. Crushed. Pressed through everything, until you lie on the underside of reality, knowing that you are dead, and will be forever.

When you wake up, you are breathless, panting, sweating, with tears in your eyes and loss in your heart. Your throat is sore, 

and you are so very very tired.

rows.title: More Than Lucid
rows.titleText:
You fly, free and formless, skirting between the sky and the stars as you race toward your goal. Looking ahead, you cannot see your destination, but you can see the lands below, each a world, each a reality. One has lands that flow like water, and another no land at all, but thousands of balloons instead, sailing over a vast stormy sky. One green, one blue, one an angry red. You see them and they’re gone. Your prize is greater.

Thinking for a moment, you know some things. They seem obvious to you, but you don’t know how you know them. There are general things, like how you know this is a Dream. How you know the worlds below you are real, filled with waking people living waking lives. You know more specific things, like the dreamers trophies: great prizes, whose form and function are specific to the individual that claims them, if they can. They, you know, are your destination: heavy things you sink towards. You’ll need to make what choices you can before you arrive: use the dream that brought you here as fuel for the journey and the changes you will make along the way.

These trophies will not be handed to you. You will have to suffer for them and thus the chance to claim them is bought with suffering. The trials for you to overcome will require a change to yourself: they are not for the normal, and thus your hopes must be spent to even the odds.

Or, you suppose, you could avoid the trial. The through brings loss, as though giving up a sin, but the world you go to now may be fair enough on its own, with a little changing.

You think on your wants, travelling onwards towards the reality of your testing.

rows.title: Point Exchange
rows.titleText: First, you consider that you will need to balance your reserves, working with what you have as best you can. You already know their purpose, like you know a glass of water will quench thirst.

objects.title: Dream to Nightmare
objects.text: Nightmares are what you will need to purchase the chance of a trophy. Thinking on it, you need not claim such a prize at all; you could live a full life in your new world without. But to give up the chance…

objects.title: Dream to Change
objects.text: Change is the power to alter reality from the dream. You will need it to change yourself and the world, and give yourself an edge to survive, or better yet, succeed. You could get these through other sacrifices later, but the more wealth you begin with…

objects.title: Nightmare to Dream
objects.text: Dream is a raw positive power. It has no worth outside of here, to be soured into nightmare, or refined into change. Giving up excess terror to gain goodness is fine, but to not spend it then on Change would be to throw it away.

objects.title: Change to Nightmare
objects.text: Sacrifice the ability to smooth your path now, for the chance to get so much more at journeys end. Beginning in debt is never good, though you’ll have the chance to pay it off later. Beware that you don’t leave yourself so in debt that successes and trophies will be forever out of your reach.

rows.title: The Dreamers Trophies
rows.titleText: The great prizes. You are traveling to a word with these at its centre, like the pupil of a watchful eye, yet you are sure you are the first in over a thousand years to do so by dream itself. Much sought after, their power is tremendous, and while the denizens of the world may fight for but the smallest scrap of a chance, they have not the rich seam of nightmare that you carry with you: their greatest kings achieved but the smallest splinter of but one of these.

objects.title: True Immortality
objects.text:
Your soul is etched permanently into existence. When you die, you can choose what happens: undo the event, reappear elsewhere, even be reincarnated into another wold, which opens up a way of travel. Ageing can be stopped, but not reversed, and it does not spare you from pain, physical, mental, or spiritual, nor from the attentions of those who would do you wrong, but it is your soul, and you can leave this gift behind when existence wears thin. 

Without this, you will be subject to the reincarnation/afterlives/oblivions of whatever reality you die in, though your other prizes can never be taken from you. Incidentally, the world you’re heading towards has reincarnation as the default, with no memory retention, and a body/power level fitting to the average.

objects.title: The Open Door
objects.text:
Worlds beyond counting are open to you, some great and some small. Some are empty and ready to be claimed, some are the halls of gods before which you will be cowed. With this you can travel between them all, slipping between with no more effort than a thought and a step. Be careful where you travel though: in the grand scheme you are nothing, but there are attentions of being you do not wish to attract.

Without this, or another means of travel, you will be stuck in the world you’re heading to.

objects.title: Your Other Half
objects.text: Your true soulmate. To encounter them is to be joined in fate forever, your soul instinctively bonding with them and the both of you together becoming far greater than the sum apart. They will be perfect for you beyond anything physical or mental that can compare, leaving your life before them a hollow nightmare in comparison. objects.text: To have someone’s face in your crotch, your hands on their head, working. Heaven.

objects.title: Their Pussy
objects.text: The womanly moans. The soft, the wet, the warm. As it was meant to be.

objects.title: Your Pussy
objects.text: The special pleasure, the risk, the reward. You have it, and you want to use it.

objects.title: Natural Talent
objects.text: When it comes to sex, you just know what to do, thrilling others by instinct.

objects.title: Self Control
objects.text: A desire for sex is natural, but you refuse to let your urges control your actions.

objects.title: Less Control
objects.text: You’re more often lead by your loins, at the protest of your brains.

objects.title: Virgin Hunter
objects.text: You’re drawn to the innocent and prefer to bed the unbedded.

objects.title: Mature Lover
objects.text: You prefer the seasoned over the juvenile. Mature instead of unripened.

addons.text: Virgin Hunter: Your dating pool may be very small.

objects.title: Violence Seeker
objects.text: Sex should be wild. Frantic. Bloody. Consensual or not is up to you, except when it isn’t.

objects.title: Sadistic
objects.text: To hurt your partner is to pleasure yourself. Tears or blood: theirs to lose, yours to gain.

addons.text: Violence Seeker: A draw to violence and the suffering of others leaves you with the fantasies of a rapist.

objects.title: Masochistic
objects.text: Sex should hurt you. It’s what you deserve. What you crave. What you need.

addons.text: Violence Seeker: A draw to violence and your own suffering leaves you with fantasies of being raped

rows.title: The Races of Your Affections
rows.titleText:
Which races are you naturally drawn toward? If they are not your own, the respectability of such practices vary by race: a noble elf slumming it with a savage orc would bring shame on his elven blood, while a human and a dwarf may have the families of both simply viewing the union with confusion.

Xenophobia does exist though, and as half breeds are only possible between some lesser or invasive races, unions between most are considered wasteful hedonism. Yet still, the heart wants what the heart wants.

You may leave this section blank to be open to all, regardless of race. Also note that not selecting a race does not preclude them from romance; it’s just that their race will not be considered a plus should they court you, as may be the case for you courting others.

objects.title: Human Preference
objects.text: The dynamic race, plentiful, strong, and civilised, but somewhat basic, don’t you think?

addons.text: Your Race: As it should be

objects.title: Elven Preference
objects.text: The fairest race. There are few who would not agree with your assessment.

addons.text: Your Race: As it should be

objects.title: Dwarven Preference
objects.text: Hardy and strong, but often ornery and standoffish. Still, some like them thick.

addons.text: Your Race: As it should be

objects.title: Orcish Preference
objects.text: Savage, wild, thrilling, and free. People will think less of you, or assume the worst of them.

addons.text: Your Race: As it should be

objects.title: Drow Preference
objects.text: The beauty of elves with a dark side. People will be sceptical, assuming you a duped fool.

addons.text: Your Race: As it should be

objects.title: Celestial Touched Preference
objects.text: Everyone wishes to be closer to the heavens. If you succeed, expect a round of drinks and jealousy.

addons.text: Celestial: Keep the blood pure

objects.title: Demon Touched Preference
objects.text: A fiery passion that grows in the dark. Few wish demon blood to propagate, but forbidden fruit is sweet.

addons.text: Demon: They should only breed with themselves.

objects.title: Harpy Preference
objects.text: The wild flying savages. Beasts on high. Beautiful plumage doesn’t make them welcome in society.

addons.text: Your Race: As it should be

objects.title: Construct Preference
objects.text: The magical golems come in all shapes, sizes, and functions, and work with unlimited stamina. Some will think you odd.

addons.text: Your Race: A golem that can love at all is strange. To love what cannot love it back is pitiful.

objects.title: Greenkin Preference
objects.text: Ogres and Goblins: brutes and rapists by nature, utterly unfit for the world. If this gets out, it could ruin you.

objects.title: Monster Preference
objects.text: A catch all term. Minotaurs, merfolk, fairies, centaurs, dragons etc. Most have sentience, but not as you could relate to. Feel free to pick and choose. Includes vampires and werewolves too.

objects.title: Beast Preference
objects.text: These are just animals. No sentience. Most just want to kill you. Bestiality is illegal, but what happens in the wild often stays in the wild.

objects.title: Demon Preference
objects.text: Some fiends can be strangely alluring, yet all they desire of you is your suffering, violation, and any power you have. Many will think you traitor, or mad.

objects.title: Strong Affection
objects.text: You lose your inhibitions and judgment when surrounded by the races of your affections. Not recommended if combined with your own race, or the more common races.

objects.title: Xenophobic Balance
objects.text: The races not selected here will sexually repulse you. You can overcome it, for someone special, but it will be hard to get aroused unless the room is dark, or a bag is involved.

rows.title: A Moment to Reflect
rows.titleText:
You think for a moment. Have you made all your choices before you move on? You’ll be able to think back and make more changes to yourself before you arrive, but once you get there, you’ll be stuck with what you have.

A sudden dreadful thought of arriving without eyes, or a chest, or a face creeps in. Better to check before moving on. You’ll need something selected for your Race, Gender, Age, Height, Build, Skin Colour, Eyes, Hair Colour, Rear, Dick, Pussy, Chest, Attractiveness, and Sexuality…you think.

objects.title: Continue On
objects.text: It looks like you have everything you need.

rows.title: A World in Sight
rows.titleText:
With eyes to see and a body to know, the world of your destinations comes quickly into view, clouds shifting to reveal it has always been before you. To see a thing is to invite information about it into your mind, and so you look about with greedy hunger, at deserts and forests, mountains and cities, even through the ground, at mining dwarves and scheming darkness. There are wars and wonders, magic and mercenaries, honour and horrors, and through it all, eyes turned to the same prize you seek.

It’s dizzying. The world is vast, and your destination is vast, yet such a small part of the whole. Your journey's end is but a single country, surrounded by other countries, yet how long would it take to walk from one end to the other? How many months? As you try and judge the distance, you find that you can’t; the land changes before your eyes, unsettled by your gaze. The country, lit by a glowing light at its centre, the beacon you have followed, that only you can see, is shadowed by dream, and perhaps for the first time, observed by a dreamer. Before you arrive, you can change it, as you have changed yourself.

The closer to the light, the more you can change, but first you must know and understand. The fabric of the world is too strong to change greatly, but if you take your time, perhaps…

objects.title: The World
objects.text: You look upon the world, your new eyes watering at the sight of the horizon.

objects.title: The Countries
objects.text: You look upon the lands below, each containing a piece of the puzzle.

objects.title: Dormientes
objects.text: You look where power lies, the changeable landscape of the central kingdom.

objects.title: Your Arrival
objects.text: You look to the task of ingress, a thief breaking into the rest of your life.

objects.title: Your Boons
objects.text: You consider the dream, the fantasy. How can you best be served, and prepared?

objects.title: Your Banes
objects.text: You consider the darkness, the nightmare. How does reality balance the good with the bad?

objects.title: Your Beginning
objects.text: All dreams must end. It’s time for you to wake up and see the dawn of a new day.

rows.title: Worldly Knowledge
rows.titleText: As you look upon the world, the knowing of its ways blossoms in your mind, not in detail, but certainly in scope. Thinking upon it is to think on the challenge ahead and your place within in. The obstacles you will face and the peoples you will meet.

objects.title: The Challenge as Known
objects.text:
You look to the light. To the trophies you seek. They are housed in a great and impenetrable fortress: the tower of Dormientes. It existed long before the city that surrounded it and took its name, and it’s neither the high walls of black crystal nor the impossibly thick gates that make it so unassailable: to walk there is to fall into a deep slumber.

The towers guardians, ancient golems of incredible construction, walk in an unending patrol. For the sleepers they find, they check, and those without the keys of passage are taken to the temple of waking, where the fortunate shake off the spell, and the unfortunate are buried after passing. What is checked for are the six keys of entry, painted gently onto the soul, each findable in the six cardinal directions.

Fulfil the challenges and unlock the keys, each a quest of many years. Walk into the citadel and sleep, waking before the final door. There you can claim all that has been set aside for you. The trophies that are yours.

objects.title: The Six Points of the Compass
objects.text:
Highmarch, far to the North, where mountains rise and temperatures fall, Dwarven hammers ring and cultish practices whisper.

Nellacomb, to the distant South, where a baking desert houses empires both ruined and new. The dried dead sleep with ready vigilance.

Melliomer, the great Eastern forest, where old elves look young beside great trees and sordid histories long since forgotten. 

Eardheart, Westward, where eyes watch and battle rages. Demons ply their evil craft, and many suffer under the spilling of the outer worlds.

Upward fly the floating castles; ancient fortresses of old empires that sail upon the clouds. Secrets and trinkets entice all.

And far far below, the rivers of the deep, where Drow, dark skinned, dark hearted, move through darker channels, where secret wars are ever waged.

Each hold a key. Each must be mantled by a champion.

objects.title: The Unchangeable Change
objects.text:
The seventh point of the compass: its middle. Dormientes. A country named for its city names for its divine centre. The tower holds a world of pure dreams, able to contain the power of the trophies, and the result is that the land of the country is far more open to change by one such as yourself. It stands now as a simplistic place: an impression of a place, more so than the lands around it, and they more so than the world beyond them.

There is no reason to fear though. It is changeable to you now, but no others will come while you are there; no dreamer will change your fate before it is carried out, one way or the other. When you claim what prize you can, it will wait patiently for your passing before another might claim some part of what is left, changing the same part of the world as you did, and such a thing will be a thousand year occasion in its rarity.

Once dreamed, the dream will remain, a heaven or a nightmare. You will not be able to change it once you step out into the world. Beware of death as well, for here your soul will remain, reincarnated as blank as the rest, again and again.

objects.title: There is a History
objects.text:
Many in this world have tried to seize some shred of the power within the tower of Dormientes. Empires have risen and fallen in its pursuit. Very few have succeeded, but enough to keep old legends alive and attracting many to walk a hopeless path. It is said that all who live in Dormientes either are, or are descended from, someone who sought the great power at its heart.

The result is a country of dreamers. Some may join you on your quest, but they will become rivals in time, as is usually the case when power is involved. Worse, there are many in the world who may not want anyone to succeed as they may disrupt the order of things; tradition may have disinterested kings offering you quests, but the closer you get, the more your efforts will be sabotaged by those who see a threat to their power.

No one has managed to get more than the slimmest sliver of the great power, but those who did now have their decedents ruling nations, jealously guarding their fading inheritance and the distant prestige of their ancestors. None are as you, able to claim full trophies, but all with think they could be.

objects.title: The Cult of the Dream
objects.text:
The world has many religions, gods, spirits, and saints, and many ways that one should live. Some start cults that sacrifice the innocent, and some start the orders that stand against them. You need only deal with one at most if you wish to claim your prize.

The Soporatus Cult is the principal religion of Dormientes and is woven throughout society there. They host the knowledge and ritual required to gain access to the grand sanctum of Dormientes, to gain the power of the trophies within. Outside of that country, in the six other countries, their presence is far less, yet there is still a shrine in each, and within that shrine you may pledge to take up the challenges there. Fulfilling them will allow you to be bestowed with a key, painted onto your soul and pressed to permanence in Dormientes itself. All six will be required to enter the great sanctuary.

This is a cult of hierarchy. To advance within its ranks and be granted the challenges of the six points, you will have to be recognised by them. For their duty, they, more than anyone, are subject to your change.

objects.title: The Strangeness of Magic
objects.text:
This new reality works on a new foundation, woven through with magic threads both within and without. Priests prey to gods who listen and respond with miracles. Mages construct and cast spells, built with knowledge and understanding. Even warriors and common men look inward, towards their own glowing souls, channelling and cultivating their own inner strengths towards miraculous abilities. Each type has its advantages and its limitations, requiring effort, talent, and practice to achieve, and thus out of reach to a sad many. 

Those who rely on the gods so often submit thought to faith, becoming complacent vessels to the drives of external forces. The few who resist engage in a battle of Will with the heavens, negotiating or strong-arming miracles from them, powerful, but often lacking subtlety. Masters of mind and magic cast with complex sigils, words, thoughts, and gestures. It requires an educated mind to work, and a strong mind to resist the mental fatigue that follows. Finally, for those who better themselves, it requires the teachings of time, or of another on the same path, and the wisdom within yourself to tell a fool and a wiseman apart.

rows.title: Worldly Changes
rows.titleText:
The world is a vast place and your destination only a small part that feels soft to the touch of your mind. Despite this, you have some influence here, both to know and to alter. Like dropped ink, your changes will be concentrated by the trophies you seek. Some may not reach any further than the countries linked to the dreamers trophies. Others may stain even the furthest corners of this world.

You need not select a single change, leaving the world to be a simple generic fantasy, conforming to the expected, yet still rich with the flavours of surprise. If you wish to make changes though, use the options below to show and hide them.

objects.title: The Style
objects.text: Up to and beyond the six points; how the reachable world looks and operates.

objects.title: The Races
objects.text: Those you will be and those you will encounter, including all the forces beyond.

objects.title: The Religion
objects.text: Anyone questing for power will deal with the Soporatus Cult extensively.

rows.title: The Aesthetics of the World
rows.titleText:
Cultures, ideas, fashions, technologies; these things know no boarder and may spill out far beyond the six pointed boarder you’ll land in. The operation of the world though can be much more far reaching, acting as the style of the world and the direction its fates fall toward.

You’d think you could combine three or so at most, letting the colours mix as they may into something unique.

objects.title: Western
objects.text: Practical armour. Hardy robes. Styles that wouldn’t look out of place in your own world’s western medieval history. Social mobility is just as low, but the presence of magic can soften some edges. Expect polearms and crossbows and stout brigandine. The default option, here only for mixing.

objects.title: Ancient
objects.text: Realistic, but of an older style. Spears and shields and houses more commonly made of wood and mud than stone. They can still have fine cities, with fine entertainment, but the wild is wilder, the people more ignorant, and some concepts you take for granted are but glints in civilisations eye.

objects.title: RPG
objects.text: A world with great adventures and pointier hats. Individuals can rise and fall more easily as power can be cultivated and status grows with it. It can lead to a more chaotic space, and more threats, keeping people in cities and villages, but guilds are more relevant and can be hired to help.

objects.title: JRPG
objects.text: Similar to RPG, but with less practical fashions and more child soldiers. While there will still be adventures, expect more apocalyptic threats and powerful adversaries. You’ll need those giant swords, though power will be closer tied to their wielder than the items themselves.

objects.title: Eastern
objects.text: Rather than a medieval look, with strange lands far away, the lands you arrive in will have a more eastern flavour. They will be akin to a mix of ancient japan, china, and Korea, and the magic, gods, myths, and legends will match as well, different, but similar.

objects.title: Dark
objects.text: The world will be grim and harsh, always feeling as though the life you know is not welcome within it. That existence is a constant struggle for all, even the powerful, as beasts and fate gnash their teeth at the throats of the good. People fight it. So far, they’ve been winning.

objects.title: Storied
objects.text: The world is far more steeped in history. The cities of the day are built upon ancient ruins, themselves built upon even more ancient remains. Grand indomitable structures still stand, weathered by time, and labyrinths stretch unmapped, their purpose lost for good.

objects.title: High Fantasy
objects.text: Why build a city when you can build a grand tower? Why slay a dragon when you can tame it? And what kind of wizard lives in a house that isn’t at least a little bigger on the inside? With this, the world moves away from the practical and towards the fantastical.

objects.title: Close The Style
objects.text: Return to the Worldly Choices.

rows.title: The Races of the World
rows.titleText: There are many beings in this world. Some remain in dark places, unseen and unheard. Some lurk outside of the world, bleeding in through the seams. Many are hard to categorise and impossible to understand, and while there will always be scholars who will attempt to try, they will near always fail. Nevertheless, here are some categories of what you can expect to find.

objects.title: The Civilised Races
objects.text: Humans, Elves, Dwarves, Drow, and Orcs. The latter is an often debated topic as some wish them categorised as Green Kin. There are other races in the world that lie outside of the six points, like the serpent peoples or deep merfolk societies, but until more migrate to the six points, they will not be considered civilised by its denizens.

objects.title: The Bestial Races
objects.text: Races that have some degree of intelligence, but not enough for civilisation. Miniatures, beastfolk, harpies, centaurs, giants, lizardmen, even rarer creatures like fairies or dragons fall into this category. All are rarely seen in the six points, often being hunted. Miniatures and beast folk are not considered Green Kin, despite the predilections of their males.

objects.title: The Green Kin Races
objects.text: Ogres, Trolls, and Goblins mostly, but any species whose life cycle near totally relies on the rape of anther species. Goblins are all male, and while a female elk captured in the woods would do, more intelligent mates result in more capable offspring. Ogres and Trolls have females, but even they consider them too ugly. Anything in this category are truly despised by all.

objects.title: The Animal Races
objects.text: Creatures with only animal intelligence and cunning. Covers everything from the great scorpions of the Nellacomb Desert to the star birds of the floating islands. Each land has a rich array of such life, from big to small, and when considering how dangerous some are, the civilised races can never consider themselves the top of the food chain.

objects.title: The Cursed
objects.text: Those stricken with a transformative curse, either spreadable, like werewolves, vampires, and some stranger monsters, or that are unique to them, delivered by gods or wizards playing such. Magic underlies the malady, so in theory they can be cured, though few dare to try. Those who drag others down with them are sometimes organised, forming cults or hidden societies for protection.

objects.title: The Undead
objects.text: Often considered cursed, but as they can be raised and enslaved by the necromancer cults and usually cannot transfer it, they have their own category. Skeletons, zombies, dullahans, ghosts, and yes, vampires, are all counted among them. The result of cursed ground, sour magic, or life hating influences. Unified by a shared weakness to holy magic.

objects.title: The Divine Sphere
objects.text: Covers the gods and their servants: powerful beings in the infinite beyond who reach in to influence the world for their unknown reasons. Some pray to these being to be noticed and influenced. Others to spite and curse. The beings can have good motives and ill, but are always holy, and limited in what they can do in the material world, despite their power.

objects.title: The Infernal Kind
objects.text: Demons. Some great, some small, all malicious and cruel. A kind of metaphysical consumption; a mould that feeds on suffering and the decaying of the spirit. Far from holy, these beings stew in the lowest pits of dark reality, tempting power in exchange for hooks and favours, wishing to spread, so all things become like they are.

objects.title: The Others
objects.text: This is the category for everything else, though it mostly covers the creatures from dark other worlds, like mind flayers, tentacled horrors, and things without names. Most lurk below in the deep river regions. It is said that in the deepest darkest depths, there is a hole to another world so small, only things without bones can squeeze through.

rows.title: Modifying the Races
rows.titleText: Race is rarely a fixed thing. It can adapt in one place and stay the same in another. This world is large enough in total that the races of the six points being different from the norm in some way would not greatly raise attentions.

objects.title: Power Hungry Humans
objects.text: Even the poorest, most oppressed and downtrodden person can be happy with their station if they think there are those lesser than themselves. This option makes humans more power hungry, oppressive and cruel, both unable and unwilling to play nice with anyone outside of their race.

addons.text: Your Race: Affects you a little. Changes how you’re perceived a lot.

objects.title: Weak Humans
objects.text: Jack of all trades, master of none. The sentiment works on an individual level. Outclassed in magic, production, military strength, and technology, the only advantage humans have is their numbers. In a battle between races, fighting, trading, or any competition, expect humans to lose, or barely hold on.

addons.text: Your Race: Your abilities will be somewhat reduced; you’ll stand out among humans far more.

objects.title: Arrogant Elves
objects.text: They carry themselves with extreme haughtiness, viewing all other races as fundamentally lesser than they. It is a belief that will manifest in blatant xenophobia, leaving them as isolationist or militant or both.

addons.text: Your Race: You can fight against it, but your underlying prejudices will increase.

objects.title: Elven Banishment
objects.text: Elven societies are stricter with their rules. If an elf breaks them, they will be banished. Means that the elves you meet outside of their countries will either be slaves captured when vulnerable, or simply more integrated and friendly, having being rejected from their old lives.

addons.text: Your Race: Breaking the rules can have you chased like a fugitive in places like Melliomer.

objects.title: Greedy Dwarves
objects.text: Driven by lust for gold and valuables of all kinds, these dwarves build subterranean fortresses, kidnap other races for slaves, waging wars of aggression for territory, and generally treating the world like a corpse ripe for looting. What’s yours is theirs. You just don’t know it yet.

addons.text: Your Race: Increases your kleptocratic tendencies, though you won’t be as ‘gold mad’ as other dwarves.

objects.title: Sly Dwarves
objects.text: Usually known for their strength and straight forward attitude, Dwarves are now known for their underhanded ways, similar to Drow. Their society is rife with politics and intrigue and honour is an unknown concept. Dealing with them becomes fraught. Living among them, a nightmare.

addons.text: Your Race: Makes dealing with the other races more of a challenge as they view you with suspicion.

objects.title: War Loving Orcs
objects.text: Their civilisation now resembles a war band, broken into anything between a small group of raiders to a vast sweeping army. The weak among them die, and the weak among their enemies become sport: merely playthings to keep them entertained in the nights between battle. Near considered Green Kin.

addons.text: Your Race: Being one of the enemy of all other races will make your challenge much harder.

objects.title: More Accepted Orcs
objects.text: While still stronger than humans, they are not considered simpler or more brutish. Rather than tribes or slums, they’ll be more integrated into societies. That said, they are risen, not elevated: any hardship that can beset a human can beset an Orc, just not because they are an Orc.

addons.text: Your Race: This will certainly remove the stigma you may face otherwise.

War Loving Orcs: Celebrating martial prowess and victory, they are seen as making fine soldiers and mercenaries, with whole clans even being contracted to fight demons and undead. The bad is mostly balanced by the good.

objects.title: Domineering Drow
objects.text: The Drow are now committed to world domination, their number the only thing holding them back.  The subversion, enslavement, and domestication of other races keeps them busy in the meantime. Their use of sex as a weapon, reward, and sign of submission, is far more common place.

addons.text: Your Race: On the downside, you’re more distrusted than ever and your people have expectations of you. The upside? You can tell people you’re of the master race.

objects.title: Drow are Submissive
objects.text: The matriarchal and cut throat nature of the Drow is changed to a pacifistic and placating policy of non-aggression. This makes their society quite pleasant, as without the violence they have to rely on their charms to survive.

addons.text: Your Race: Instead of being seen as a spy taking advantage, people are more likely to take advantage of you instead.

objects.title: Man-Eating Harpies
objects.text: The unreasonable become far less reasonable. These birds prey upon many meat filled creatures, dragging them back to their great nests and consuming them alive. They play cruel games with their food, and such games can include a pre, post, and concurrent meal gang rape.

addons.text: Your Race: The stories are horrifying. Expect revulsion, even hunting parties, in the world below.

objects.title: More Organised Harpies
objects.text: Their mock parliaments and savage courts become more civilised, among themselves at least. Their roosts in the floating fortresses become their domains, and instead of a bandit gang, dealing with them is akin to dealing with any state, with laws, traditions, and even taxes.

addons.text: Your Race: While weary, people will at least think you less capricious in your dealings.
Man-Eating: The savagery of beasts made organised and efficient. This is something to fear.

objects.title: Corruption of Celestials
objects.text: It is seen by all that godly being are sent to battle the demonic threat. Even the demons believe this. That is why the forces of evil will track down and capture celestial blooded, corrupting them to their evil cause. Demons can use them to gain more power, and a corrupted celestial is no small threat.

addons.text: Your Race: You will be hunted by demons, and if they catch you, your fate will be horrific.

objects.title: Hot-Blooded Celestials
objects.text: The celestials that breed with lower races either have a plan or are closely linked with breeding itself. Cherubs, fertility goddesses, nymphs etc. Such are naturally the kind to pass on that attraction to carnal acts, and so their children have both the libido of their race and the libido of the divine.

addons.text: Your Race: You will have a harder time keeping your mind off sex, and be more open to it with anyone.

objects.title: Demon Touched Charm
objects.text: Demon Touched often have the blood of seducers running through their veins, giving them the ability to charm, through magic or looks, far more easily. Expect more demon touched prostitutes and courtesans as their reputation for allure increases their allure.

addons.text: Your Race: Rather than disgust, people are more likely to view you with sexual interest, but not more respect. You’ll also be more sexually motivated, but can resist it more than most if you choose to.

objects.title: Demon Touched Evil
objects.text: All Demon Touched are some part demon: Evil is a part of them, and they are far more likely to succumb to its charms. Expect them to be more criminal and amoral in their actions; more deserving of the poor reputation that lingers about them.

addons.text: Your Race: Reduces your own morality by only a little, but others will think you have none at all.
Demon Touched Charm: Increases sexual desire and reduced morality is a poisonous mix. Expect a reputation for less consensual sex to be well earned.

objects.title: Built with Horror
objects.text: Rather than just stone or metal or wood, these golems often have people mixed in, body and soul. Expect them to scream an apology when they attack, and moan with despair and horror when left broken and unable to die. Knowing this, are the ones who have fallen silent worse?

addons.text: Your Race: Being an ex-human with a soul, you are already such and have accepted it. It won’t affect you much. Expect more sympathy or pity from others, though fear and revulsion can also be found.

objects.title: More Human
objects.text: Modern constructs can be made to mimic real beings, in both appearance and manner, as long as one doesn’t look too closely. They will appear as dolls, made of wood or porcelain, with the cracks of damage and their too precise movements the only things giving them away.

addons.text: Your Race: Despite the uncanny valley, it’s easier to respect something that looks more like ones self. You can be made in the image of any race.
Built with Horror: Homunculi, seen as little different from undead by some, yet a new and distinct entity.

objects.title: Many Beasts
objects.text: Beastfolk are far more common in the six points, and far more of a threat. Before, a wild raging minotaur may have been a difficult quest. Now, a full tribe sensing a cities weakness and descending upon it is not an impossibility. Covers Beastmen, Minotaurs, and Lizardmen.

objects.title: Civilised Beasts
objects.text: Renewed in number, they are also renewed in control. Leaders keep tribes in line. Territories are drawn and defended. Even alliances are formed in their own way. This keeps the chaos low, but when it does happen, it happens hard.

objects.title: Female Goblins
objects.text: The female touch can have quite the civilising effect, as it happens. This effectively turns goblins into a kind of Beastkin, no longer needing other races to pro-create (though that is still an option). You may even see some in cities now, without the guards trying to kill them outright.

objects.title: Evil Goblins
objects.text: Before there was a twisted nature to them, simply following their instinct to breed. Now there is an evil in them, not just kidnapping to breed, but to let loose their sick urges and perverse pleasures. They are akin to demons, where the cruelty is the point.

objects.title: Organised Goblins
objects.text: Tribes can now work together to form bigger threats, and even small scale, their tactics are more dangerous. Ambushes now use traps, kidnappings now use poisons and spells, captives rarely die from mistreatment. Even their scrap weapons, tarnished armour, and fighting styles improve.

addons.text: Female Goblins: While generally becoming more intelligent, it is not something focused on evil. Their tribes and societies can build complex machines, and they’re more likely to be accepted in civilised society.

Evil Goblins: Their tactics become truly diabolical. Human shields, traumatic displays, brutal warnings, tactical torture and the breaking of wills. Their understanding of how to hurt others will be used to maximum effect.

objects.title: Green Tide
objects.text: The number of goblins, trolls, and ogres increases significantly, to the point that they are considered a plague and the first thing on the minds of any travellers moving through their territory. Numbers bring a greater hierarchy, so expect fearsome leaders keeping their lesser in line.

addons.text: Female Goblins: Increased numbers and civility leads to towns, villages, and even cities for the greenkin as they carve a place for themselves, same as any race.
Evil Goblins: Truly a tide of terror, turning atrocity into normality. You may think you can beat them, but the suffering they will cause will be immense regardless.

objects.title: Powerful Cursed
objects.text: Many cursed are extremely powerful: terrifying forces that even orders of experienced hunters often fare poorly against. Their abilities vary, their weaknesses are specific; slaying one will surely be a quest at some point, and many will not take it, scared of becoming a thrall or dinner.

objects.title: In Control
objects.text: The cults and cabals that werewolves and vampires form become far more refined, their reach expanding with subtle ease to effect society around them. From warrior clans with a bestial secret, to blood sucking nobles, they are no more loved, but they are far more protected.

addons.text: Powerful Cursed: Now the de facto rulers, whose power and positions are open secrets that few dare whisper, and none dare challenge.

objects.title: Willing Transmission
objects.text: The cursed seek out the powerful with the intent of transmission, to bring the strong to their side and under their control. Expect them to seek you out when you gain notoriety, and beware, removing a curse will be near impossible, and you cannot obtain the trophies while you have it.

addons.text: Powerful Cursed: It will be very hard not to become a subjugated thrall of the cursed; it’s not like they will wait until you can challenge them.

objects.title: Cursed at War
objects.text: Vampire clans and werewolf broods may be hunted by man, but it is each other that they find most repulsive. Perhaps it is the competition for food, or a hatred of themselves: a beast, reflected back at them. This will save mortal lives, if only by ending cursed ones.

addons.text: In Control: The hidden war between clans is brutal, playing their servants, their mortals, their food, against each other. Can lead to unexpected massacres, their cause attributed to crime or animal attacks.
Powerful Cursed: The only think keeping the mortal races free, though they will inevitably be cause in the cross fire.

objects.title: Terrifying Undead
objects.text: Usually, undead are foul, rotting, tragedies, to be destroyed before they destroy others. Now they will be the stuff of nightmares, requiring the strongest will and a stronger stomach just to face without breaking, and always returning unless specialised methods are used.

objects.title: Sexual Undead
objects.text: With the exception of the vampire, undead do not lust like the living do. Now they will, and seek to satisfy it upon the living, the dead, and undead. This can lead to some most horrifying things, not the least of which being the added maddening denial felt by the more fleshless of the dead.

addons.text: Terrifying Undead: The horrific hoard becomes that much worse. If a group of undead are coming and word gets out, expect some suicides if running isn’t an option.

objects.title: Ghost World
objects.text: The recently deceased could become ghosts before reincarnation: brief confused spirits struggling to move on. Now they can become trapped as such, growing in spiritual power and influence until becoming legends that dominate an area. Difficult to deal with as they can now possess the living.

addons.text: Terrifying Undead: Lingering ghosts are already hard to disperse, but they will be more terrifying, taking on horrific forms and drawing the living into their despairing hateful confusion.
Sexual Undead: Bereft of a body, they will possess the living to satisfy their fleshly urges, leaving their victim trapped and aware throughout the process

objects.title: Organised Undead
objects.text: Already a misanthropic bunch, even under a necromancers sway, the ‘naturally’ occurring undead take their task to heart, becoming a force organised by those who retain some sanity, campaigning for the end of life. Expect wars of aggression if not kept in check.

addons.text: Terrifying Undead: Regarded as what will inevitably be the apocalypse, numerous orders hunt the undead with extreme prejudice and zealotry, knowing that should the war begin, the living will undoubtedly lose.

Sexual Undead: Armies rape. This is a tragic reality. The undead would usually kill with cold unfeeling mercy, but now the people of conquered kingdoms will suffer a far worse, yet just as fatal, fate.
Ghost World: While ghosts match with the horde, the powerful kind rarely leave the ground or item their spirit is snagged on.

objects.title: Dutiful Divinity
objects.text: The celestial beings now send their servants to aid the civilised races against demons and corruption. Beware though: such powers will have a vested interest in keeping you from your prize, and in bringing you to judgment should you get in their way. They’ll be friend and enemy both.

objects.title: Wild Divinity
objects.text: When the outer worlds touch upon the mortal one, it is the rash whose influence can be felt most. Calm gods of peace and wisdom stay quiet, while wrathful beings of lofty understanding try to ‘fix’ things their way. Expect capriciousness wherever godly dealings happen.

addons.text: Dutiful Divinity: With more direct influence comes more direct ambitions. Undead and demons still die, but crime and injustice must be fixed with a firm hand, and worship enforced by the sword. Their forces will jump quicker to the ‘enemy’ stage.

objects.title: Godly Hedonism
objects.text: The gods and their servants now all share the lusts of base creatures, and encourage such excesses among their followers. Unless you plan on visiting the divine realms, this will mostly be seen in the rituals and iconography of all god fearing religions, which take on a decidedly sexual tone.

addons.text: Dutiful Divinity: There will be more Celestial Touched born, for obvious reasons.

Wild Divinity: Before, the gods demanded piety to receive their blessings. Now they’ll want a show, as what was once appreciation of beauty and pleasure takes on a decidedly lecherous air. One they expect you to be thankful for.

objects.title: They Walk Among Us.
objects.text: The gods are no longer restricted to the outer spheres, stepping into the mortal realm in mortal bodies forged by their own power. Should such bodies die, they will return to their godhood, diminished. Can be VERY dangerous for you, or beneficial, if you can get on their good side.

addons.text: Dutiful Divinity: They may lead their forces or leave them to it.
Wild Divinity: Young gods with wild hearts. They’ll go where they please and do as they please. If you get in their way, what happens to you will be up to them.
Godly Hedonism: They’ll just be here to have fun. Play your cards right and you can have fun with them. Just avoid the obsessive ones.

objects.title: Demon Prevalence
objects.text: While still pouring in to the west, the nascent cause is felt everywhere else. The summoning and binding of demons is all too common, and with all the deals brokered, the cost for civilisation may be its undoing. Such deals are illegal, and risky, but try telling that to the rich and the stupid.

objects.title: Demonic Lusts
objects.text: Demons come in all manner forms, foul and fair. All wish to corrupt and debase. Before, they would rape to sow misery, or seduce to gain power, but now they do so to indulge as well, and may take fairer forms to seduce and corrupt and subvert more often. Worse or not, it’s probably safer.

addons.text: Demon Prevalence: Most demons summoned are for sexual reasons. Lead by their lusts, naïve summoners are often manipulated by their ‘lovers’, spreading demonic influence throughout society.

objects.title: Breeding Evil
objects.text: When demons are destroyed, their being returns to the dark, weakened and needing to reform over time. As their numbers are limited, their efforts have turned to breeding, bringing as many demon touched into the world as they can so that their influence can grow.

addons.text: Demon Prevalence: A demon touched child being born is usually a stipulation in any contract, leading to more of them.
Demonic Lusts: While women must fear kidnapping for breeding, now men do as well, with succubi waiting, their wombs made for litters of smaller, weaker horrors.

Female: Should you be strong, they will go out of their way to add you to their livestock, though kidnap, betrayal, curse, and other foul means. Their reach extends far and you’ll always need to be weary.

objects.title: The Staging Ground
objects.text: While they have made the western point a charnel battlefield, they have gone no further, so far content with their playground. Now though, it is clear it is a place to prepare to bring destruction to the next country, and the next. If left unchecked, they may conquer the world.

addons.text: Demon Prevalence: Their agents and spies infect other countries, leaving them without surprise.
Breeding Evil: The war will need soldiers and the soldiers need training. With more focused goals, the number of livestock and offspring will grow considerably, marching with the army.

objects.title: Outer Anchor
objects.text: One cannot choose what grows in the dark, but you can choose to let it in. Now the unknowable horrors of the deep rivers are invited by cults gone mad with knowledge, who want to commune and become, drawing the horrors even to the surface world and its seas.

objects.title: Beguiling Look
objects.text: While fundamentally slithering unknowable things, many can now take a form pleasing to the mind of their witness. Shining gods, smiling parents, mind breaking abstractions, whatever gets them whatever it is they want. Knowing a person’s mind gives them a leverage you can’t imagine.

objects.title: Unknowable Desires
objects.text: The Outer Realm are drawn to the world by the whispers of minds, and now more specifically, the desires of its people. They are delicacies to feed upon, and more ecstatic to coax to life in breeding subjugations. They view the local life as meat, their sentience simplistic, but their bodies enticing.

addons.text: Outer Anchor: Sex cults, who kidnap and enslave others and subjugate their minds and bodies to their masters, who are not just mind flayers, but tentacle pits, mental parasites, and ascended outer gods.
Beguiling Look: Beauty unimagined. Irresistible. That touches, and kisses, and sucks so sweetly, conforming to your every desire. You’d go mad if you could see what was really happening.

objects.title: Firmly Rooted
objects.text: Cults once little more than shadows and whispers are now true powers, drawing many to their cause. They operate under the guise of a new celestial god, subverting rulers, sabotaging trophy seekers, and inviting more in. They are in open war with the Drow of the deep rivers.

addons.text: Beguiling Look: Many will flock to the cults cause when called, betraying all they hold dear. Only those whose will is an iron fortress will be able to resist and shatter the illusion.

Unknowable Desires: Conquest is a by-product, their goal more like… resource refinement. The chosen are bred, their offspring are bred, the corrupted becoming shepherds to the cause, while the refined are taken out of the world, to the deep, where ecstasies unknown can be dined upon. You will be the pinnacle of what they seek; you’re soul like a shining diamond.

objects.title: Close The Races
objects.text: Return to the Worldly Choices.

rows.title: The Soporatus Cult
rows.titleText:
The duty of the cults is considered sacred by its followers, yet they are still beings with desires and faults. Tradition, ritual, and understanding, can all be corrupted over time, and while the challenges posed will be writ upon the stones of the shrines and rejected by them if they are lacking, the people who you deal with may be far less judicious. 

The cult will ostensibly be on your side, as they are for any who seek the trophies, but the type of organisation they are can make you their noble hero to help, or a lamb to lead as they see fit. If made too strong, they may become your greatest enemy, being a thorn in your side every step of the way as they make you jump through hoops to please and benefit them. A weaker cult, meanwhile, may rely on you and be subservient to your cause, though they may not provide as much help in your journey. To the people and the state, they may be a near ignored nuisance or they may be the state itself in all but name, dominating the lives of those around them. Their actions and attitudes will certainly reflect on those associated with them, such as yourself.

The changes made here will be most noticeable in Dormientes, where the cult is princely located, but each of the six points will be touched by their presence. Beyond them, the cult is known only in name and rumour, if at all. For the people whose lives they touch, yourself included, the changes made here may drastically reshape the state of things, or have no effect on society at all. You’ll need to be careful.

objects.title: Sexual Connotations
objects.text: The cult has been infiltrated and corrupted by sexual deviants. Rituals now involve orgies, requests require service, and the dress code would make your nose bleed. They’re viewed as whores by all.

objects.title: Pure Practices
objects.text: The cult favours spiritual purity and abstinence, and can often be naïve of the world and its ways.  This makes them less threatening and sometimes easier to deal with, if a little stuffy.
