addons.text: Sexual Connotations: Their surface veneer is pure, while their ritual and hypocrisy are hidden behind closed doors.

objects.title: Predatory Practices
objects.text: The cult worships objects of power, and power is what they practice as a result. They will dominate those weaker than themselves, inside and outside the cult. They may be viewed as cruel as a result.

addons.text: Sexual Connotations: This adds some (more) bondage to rituals, but power is a dark thing: the cult will be much more rapey overall.

objects.title: Servants to All
objects.text: They give away everything they have: selflessness is a core tenet of their ideology. This makes them weak, but eager to please, and naturally, people love them for their acts of charity.

addons.text: Sexual Connotations: Giving away everything includes their bodies, and some of the more devout can be VERY generous.

objects.title: Political Connections
objects.text: The cult is more likely to scribe challenges that involve meddling in politics, which can make powerful enemies for you as you’re moved like a pawn in the cult’s own political games.

objects.title: Political Aspirations
objects.text: They don’t just navigate politics because they must, they do it for the power it brings. An adherent of theirs gains a powerful ally, but often becomes an enemy of all who have power to take.

objects.title: Rich
objects.text: This is an order that can hire mercenaries, bribe officials, own nobles, and purchase its interests outright. Comes from many sources: donations, services, savvy investments, and so on.

addons.text: Servants to All: They know that to improve lives, they must have resources to spend. Donations are high, and much good can be done.
Political Aspirations: They are the de facto rulers of Dormientes. They will be less inclined to see you succeed as a result.
Predatory Practices: They are more like a mob than a religion; a cancer to malignant to remove from society.

objects.title: Poor
objects.text: The cults coffers are nearly always empty, either due to charity or indifference. Don’t expect much support from them if money is involved.

addons.text: Predatory Practices: They have been left with few friends, but simply take what they need. More likely to be viewed as criminals in the six points.

objects.title: Fanatical
objects.text: While already devout, this is the bridge between lively debate and rhetoric, to trials of fire, martyrs, and merciless inquisitions. Dials everything else selected up to eleven.

objects.title: Faithless
objects.text: Few in the cult truly believe the trophies exist. They may laugh at your earnestness. Most use the cult as an excuse to achieve their ends, and will be much more focused on that than your needs.

objects.title: Magically Powerful
objects.text: The cult provides magical services, often related to dreams or even minor prophecy. Perhaps they’ll teach you, if you’re devout enough.

addons.text: Sexual Connotations: Their services also have a sexual nature, from simple fertility management to full blown sex changes, and of course all the fun toys they can conjure.
Predatory Practices: Their powers also extend to the mind, and those dominated by hypnosis or contracts can be found bound to the cult.

objects.title: Pilgrimage
objects.text: The cult’s active presence in the other countries is now zero and a priest or priestess must now be escorted personally to the shrines to get your challenge. A massive and often costly pain.

objects.title: Noble
objects.text: Their membership is considered a worthy pursuit for rich, with retirees and the spare children of nobles entered into their ranks. They expect finer things, complain more, and will probably look down on you.

objects.title: Criminal
objects.text: Their membership is a place of repentance, where criminals and prostitutes are sent to be of service. There will be little respect for them or their associates, and the organisation will be much rougher around the edges.

addons.text: Noble: A place to put the politically inconvenient. Where those discredited and disowned can find purpose. Expect the dregs of broken and vengeful nobility.
Political Aspirations: While they aspire, they are less likely to achieve, becoming more of a mob that operates behind the scenes.

objects.title: Among the People
objects.text: While usually accessible via temples, this makes them far more dispersed among towns and cities, both in housing and in duties. This can make them both harder to find and easier to talk to.

objects.title: Isolated
objects.text: The temples may be open to all, but that matters little when there is no one nearby. You’ll have to hike to them if you’re to interact; earn an audience through a wearying journey. Wise men live on mountains, after all.

rows.title: The Aesthetics of the Cult
rows.titleText:
Within the world, the cult has its own feel: a quality you think of to look upon it. More than the actual attitudes of the cult, this is the appearance it takes, and will affect the manner of its rituals, dress, and mentality of its adherents.

Can be mixed with any of each other, and the options above. You could make them a group who look sinister, yet are saints, or who are both militant and mournful in their duties.

objects.title: Sinister
objects.text: Regardless of intentions, they appear dark and up to no good, with droning chants or whispered prayers, or the eerie sound of silence. People won’t trust them easily.

addons.text: Predatory Practices: And for good reason. Scarification, marks of blood, kidnappings… This sinister air is more than just dark robes.

objects.title: Mournful
objects.text: The cult walks with a closer connection to death, managing burials, calming spirits, and honouring those who have walked the path and failed before its end.

addons.text: Magically Powerful: Masters of deaths magic, from fatal spells and necromancy, to spiritual healing and exorcisms.

objects.title: Powerful
objects.text: They appear bristling with power, be it magical, political, intellectual, or moral. People talk quietly when the cult is nearby, and if they don’t they are shushed by others.

addons.text: Predatory Practices: People fear the cult terribly. Teeth chatter when they pass, and cold sweat flows freely.

objects.title: Mystical
objects.text: They move through shadows and see sights unseen, always knowing more than they let on. Whether their wisdom comes through truth or deception, you may never know.

addons.text: Magically Powerful: Their knowledge of the future is very real and far reaching. People come from all over to attempt to pilfer their secrets.

objects.title: Militant
objects.text: A cult for warriors seeking power, and adorned to match. Ritual combat, training, and brash bravado shine in the plates of polished armour that does not remain unstained for long.

addons.text: Predatory Practices: Only the strong should survive. There will be less honour and more brutal training.
Fanatical: Quests and crusades will be common, and their haphazard reach will be surprisingly far as you’ll find heroes and corpses both with their livery.

objects.title: Close The Cult
objects.text: Return to the Worldly Choices.

rows.title: So That’s How It Is…
rows.titleText: You now understand the basics of the world you’re entering now and can think on other things. You’re interested to know more about the six points and the main country as you’ll have to decide where you’ll be arriving.

objects.title: You Know Of The World
objects.text: Select this to unlock the other section of The World In Sight, taking one step closer to your new life.

objects.title: Close Worldly Knowledge
objects.text: Return to the world in sight.

rows.title: Knowledge of the Six Points
rows.titleText:
From so far above, your eyes can see an impossible distance. With a glance, you can see the furthest reaches of a scorching desert and with a turn of your head you can see the tops of a frozen mountain. You can see within the deepest rooms of the highest fortresses and you can see the winding rivers far below the earth, and with seeing comes knowledge, both of the place it is and the place it could be.

You select each in turn, choosing what to change, and what remains...

objects.title: The Floating Fortresses
objects.text: The lofty reaches of an ancient skyward empire.

objects.title: Highmarch
objects.text: The dark shadow of the northern mountains.

objects.title: The Domain of Melliomer
objects.text: The woodland realms of the eastern reaches.

objects.title: Eardheart
objects.text: The many kingdoms of the West, beset by demons.

objects.title: The Nellacomb Desert
objects.text: A baking land of desert dunes, stretching southward.

objects.title: The Deep Rivers
objects.text: The veins of the world hidden far below it surface.

rows.title: The Ancient Floating Fortresses
rows.titleText:
You look to the place closest to you, furthest from the world, floating above it with a dreamlike air. Vast boulders of broken stone, split by questing roots and careless collisions, move as clouds on the wind, carrying vast buildings of forgotten designs and gale torn wilderness, hardy and overgrown. Simply getting here will be a challenge, but you see that others have and still do, rickety airships brutally pinned to the bluff by a cobweb of ropes.

They go on and on, sometimes clustered thickly and clinging to the tops of mountains, sometimes alone, like an outpost. The largest collection was once a capital, and before that it was a mountain, or perhaps many mountains, mined and hollowed to support a people long absent. You cannot see where it was taken from below, but you can see where it used to be bigger; some islands crashed thousands of years ago, or drifted out into the vastness of the world.

objects.title: An Ancient Empire
objects.text: Legend has it, the ruins are of an empire founded by one who claimed the trophies. They asked for knowledge, and these ruins of a vast floating kingdom are the result, their creation and home, filled with magic focused technology beyond the understanding of wizards today. Its bones draw in archaeologists from all over the world, seeking to understand how it floats and to unravel its secrets. The few that have been understood have been revolutionary.

objects.title: Stalwart Guardians
objects.text: The ancient nameless kingdom is not without some life. The old golems, ones that closely match those around the citadel in Dormientes, wonder the halls of the vast ruins, fighting a losing battle against thousands of years of decay. Some march with lumbering steps. Some stand guard and endlessly keep watch. Some are designed not to move, being deadly traps for all who would invade. They are very dangerous, and the principal reason its many secrets have stayed such.

objects.title: High Adventure
objects.text: Despite the dangers, adventures, treasure seekers, and archaeologists all hunt for powerful items, spells, and secrets throughout the ruins. They are both comrade and competition with each other, and those who make the daunting trip and survive the deadly guardians, may still fall prey to jealousy and greed. If you were to make it further than them, powerful artefacts may become yours, and secrets of magic and history that could lend you an edge.

objects.title: A Lofty Parliament
objects.text: Most of the floating islands are host to their current ‘rulers’, the harpies, who have made nests out of reach of the traps and the golems and do not care to venture the tight halls where wings are a hindrance. They require tribute, but can be one of the only ways to get around. Even if airships, magic, or the great mountaintop elevator was taken to get up there, the harpies are still worth bargaining with to avoid being harassed.

rows.title: Changes to the Floating Lands
rows.titleText: Far away from the trophies and their power, and scattered all over, changing the islands too much feels a pain to do, and you can scarcely see them all regardless. There are a handful of changes you can make though. Whether they’ll be worth it, you’re not sure.

objects.title: Tropical Islands
objects.text: While usually more like moorland, filled with hardy plants clinging on, many of the islands will now be akin to tropical paradises, their local residents following suit. Expect vines to chew through old stone and thickets to mask doorways. Time and nature will have taken bigger bites out of the ruins.

objects.title: Frozen Islands
objects.text: Before, only those few islands clinging to the tips of the northern mountains had snow. Now, with the altitude of many of them greater, shining snow and frigid ice make many of them cracked and frosty tombs, more lifeless than ever.

objects.title: Migrating Harpies
objects.text: With the moving islands now each drifting through seasons of their own, the flying residents migrate, moving to islands bearing new life and growing warmth whenever it gets cold. With the right timings, some islands will become very busy, while others will be practically empty.

objects.title: Known Quantities
objects.text: The islands and their past empire have remained a mystery for as long as they’ve been ruins. The items retrieved from within have ranged from powerful artefacts to junk and curios. Now, proper records exist, and people know what a truly worthy find is. Less mystery. More profit.

objects.title: Close The Floating Fortresses
objects.text: Return to the choices of Countries.

rows.title: The Mountains of Highmarch
rows.titleText:
Hills and valleys rise and fall, blown white with a chill wind even in their lower reaches. Wild cold is the deadliest of beasts, and its competition is fierce, both in animal life and in the dark dealings of those looking for solitude. A country home to dwarves, who’s many clans bring light and life to the shadowed reaches of the mountain stone, and where a small kingdom of humans also scrape a living, the rich ores below ground doing little to keep their bellies full. 

Little else brings others to Highmarch, being a distant and inhospitable place. Those not drawn to proud dwarven traditions and mineshaft homes instead cut ice and weather snowstorms to pass the time. They get less sunlight, becoming pale, and adopt a suspicious attitude to foreigners, who rarely bring good tidings, yet they are hardy, and to become their friend is to have a friend for life.

objects.title: Cults and Darkness
objects.text: To say there is nothing to bring people to Highmarch is a surprising truth. ‘Nothing’ is what some seek, as there is no better place to avoid easy scrutiny for dark cults, witch clans, and Demon worshipers. The grand school of necromancy is even located somewhere between the peaks, the preserving chill perfect for their work. It has given everyone from the area, save the dwarves, an ill reputation for the association with their unwanted neighbours.

objects.title: The Climate
objects.text: The cold brings with it freezing rains and impenetrable snowstorms, howling through caves whose residents howl back. Bears, giants, wolves, and monsters roam, traversing narrow crumbing paths, deep crevices of ice, glacial caves worn crystal smooth by flash floods of freezing water. Trees split for the freezing of their sap, and bodies lie unburied for the hardness of the ground.

objects.title: The People
objects.text: Little of all mentioned effects the dwarves, whose vast underground cites throb with the trapped warmth of vast furnaces, and whose mushroom farms grow richly. They trade with the humans, but the deep rivers far below allow travel without ice, though with dangers of its own. The huddled humans meanwhile, sell wood and furs, and trade a lot for such unwelcoming people.

objects.title: The Politics
objects.text: Dwarven clan struggles can occur, with whole mountains set against another, and the humans suffer the reliable chaos of their kind, but in general it is peaceful. Few wish to fight and die for frostbite incarnate. Instead, it is the various cults that cause combat, both between themselves and between the many militant orders who hunt them, whose religious reasons preclude cooperation.

rows.title: The Changing of Mountains
rows.titleText: Such a vast an pale land, beating with life beneath as the thud of pick on stone chimes faintly in your ears. A dark land, above and below, and swept with the winds of change that blow in the direction you choose.

objects.title: More Temperate
objects.text: While it grow colder the further north you go, and the tips of mountains will always put life at risk, the area as a whole is less extreme. It allows more life, both for simple locals and their less simple neighbours. A good choice for those who don’t do well in the bitter cold.

objects.title: Rich Culture
objects.text: While always the centre of the dwarven world, the surface cities have long been neglected. Not anymore. Now such kingdoms are linked to the river ways, exporting precious metals and dwarven works to the world. Its hardy people, and those like them, are no longer treated with suspicion.

addons.text: Pale Skin: People who think you one of the mountain folk will not treat you with suspicion for it.

objects.title: Dwarven Tarnished Age
objects.text: While catastrophes of ages past have left ruins, they are nothing to how it is now. The tunnels go deep. Deeper than anyone knows. Deeper than the deep rivers. Once grand cities of the golden age are now abandoned and unmapped, offering treasure for the daring, and death for the incautious.

objects.title: Volcanic Mountains
objects.text: Magma flows through stony veins. It is harnessed by the dwarves for great works, and the humans above who enjoy natural hot springs. The downside, of course, are obvious as earthquakes are more likely to bring rock falls and avalanches, and falling in lava is a fate wished on no one.

addons.text: Rich Culture: The cities now employ natural heating and are actually quite pleasant places to be. Tourism increases.

objects.title: Cultish Threat
objects.text: Witches, cults, worshipers of dark hearted gods, pursue their works in quiet isolation no longer. Now a great melting pot city of rejects is formed, their mad ideas melding and forming new power and ritual. The cults consume each other, but grow stronger for it. A new threat, and perhaps an opportunity?

objects.title: Zero Tolerance
objects.text: The human kingdom often grumbled about trouble making zealots. Now they lead the charge, eager to keep baby stealing madmen in check with a heavy hand. Cult hunting becomes more organised, but the chance for the innocent being targeted increases, including you if you act suspiciously.

addons.text: Rich Culture: Courts and refined methods reduce the number of mistakes. They also reduce the chance of escape if you happen to cast any unsanctioned spells.
Cultish Threat: It’s zero tolerance for a reason, and instead of a wild desperation, it is now driven by a focused campaigns against a defined enemy: a campaign necessary to keep them in check.

objects.title: Grand Necromancy
objects.text: Before, a quiet school tucked away, filled with unnaturally old scholars and their strange pursuits. Now, the centre of Necromancy in the known world, its university masters each having long since shrugged off their mortality. Unassailable by zealots and careless applicants both.

addons.text: Rich Culture: The cities are travelled enough to tolerate the ‘scholars’ of the school, as long as they don’t make trouble. They even trade supplies and guide students to the schools location.
Cultish Threat: The Necromancers have little to do with such armatures, though students rejected usually end up with the cults, giving rise to a kind of pathetic counter school.

Zero Tolerance: The relationship between the necromancers and the people of Highmarch is extremely adversarial. Highmarch may be outclassed, but that won’t stop them giving necromancer killing quests to those on the path of power

objects.title: Close Highmarch
objects.text: Return to the choices of Countries.

rows.title: The Great Forest Domain of Melliomer
rows.titleText:
Melliomer, god of the woodland realm, and no more fitting name could be found for the great sea of trees. From the boreal northern reaches, ever green when not dusted white, to the desert touching jungles of the far south, and between the two a wood of all kinds. Only verdant valleys, flowing rivers, cliffs and crevices, and the vast distance of its reach, separates the biomes of this one great wood. At its heart, the trees reach taller than sight, a flat ocean of green from the sky, a great basin from below, and the winding cities of elves held between.

They are not the first residence. The ruins of an old empire, more consumed than even the floating fortresses, dot the unmappable woods, and labyrinthine caves and winding pitch black canyons add to the density and verticality of a place that is truly the wild cradle of nature and raw magic. A place where beasts prowl, from small and venomous, to vast and venerable, and civilisation wages an unwinnable war against the chaotic balance of the natural world.

objects.title: The Elves
objects.text: Their great central city is an insular peaceful place of powerful magic and isolated culture, woven into the trees, yet more grand than any other. Little changes politically. Some elves are more primitive, lost to the woods, while some are more integrated, living in cities of stones by the edge. All face some form of predators. Renowned for druids and rangers, but the masters of many crafts are found among them.

objects.title: The Woods
objects.text: It’s hard to describe how challenging to navigate they are. Paths that are cut, scorched, paved, and pleaded into existence are consumed quickly, while giant winding roots, lakes and swamps, and cavernous crevices so deep they join the rivers of the Drow, make the floor uncrossable. Branch networks, and even airships are needed to reliably cross it, and certainly a compass or two.

objects.title: The Beasts
objects.text: The forest may be the Elves domain, but do not think them the only residents. Lizardmen battle minotaurs, ape-men war with goblins and ogres, while all manner of wild creatures, from great snakes and spiders to docile sloths, elks, and even spirits of nature itself weave a complex harmony. Life teams, and hunts, and easts, and ruts, and it won’t wait to face you alone, or on your terms.

objects.title: Old Threats
objects.text: Many of the ruins, some made by ancient elves and some by races unknown, now only serve as dens for beastmen and greenkin, though even they avoid the heart of such places. Magic is raw here, dripping like dew, and where it collects, wild things form, from glowing mushrooms to giant beasts. Such ruins were built on lay lines, or carry ancient magic artefacts. Few consider such treasures worth their risk.

rows.title: Uprooting The Woodland World
rows.titleText: The roots go deep, and through leaves and trees, there are places your eyes cannot see, yet there is purchase enough to shift some things, changing a forest that has not seen such influence since the times of nuts and acorns.

objects.title: More Navigable
objects.text: As wild as it is, the forest is now no longer such a massive pain to cross. Long paths criss-cross the land, maintained by the elves and even the beasts and animals, who use them for their hunting and their migrations. While few dare try, it should be possible to walk from one end to the other.

objects.title: Peaceful
objects.text: The woods have seen enough of war and bloodshed. The old magic that flows through it and the spirits long past want only for tranquillity. The odds of ambush, and evil creatures, are much reduced, because for those who disturb the peace, the woods disturb in kind.

objects.title: Lost Tribes
objects.text: The woodland realm is far more populated, with isolated tribes of humans, elves, orcs, and even Dwarves, waging primitive wars and trading primitive goods. They present an opportunity for guides or an extra chance for an ambush, for each tribe is different, and as they often move, it’ll be hard to know which are friendly.

addons.text: Peaceful: No extra ambushes, and the tribes deeper connection can help commune with the woods, and even make amends.

objects.title: Wild Spirits
objects.text: Magic and history leaves many more wisps here. Some play pranks and chime in the wind, others possess with cruel intention. Thick magic makes strange and unpredictable things happening more often, to people, plants, and animals, giving the forest a more haunted and mystical feel.

addons.text: Peaceful: Fewer hostile spirits, though the woods will now have more methods to punish those who break the peace, and those methods can be very dangerous.

objects.title: Golems of Nature
objects.text: Now, among the many beasts and peoples of the wood, you may encounter manifestations of nature. Golems of stone, ents of wood, swirling tides of water or wondering clumps of earth. They will be very difficult to overcome and are often large and protective of their region.

addons.text: Peaceful: The great beings are like lumbering mountains, placid, and can even be unknowingly ridden. Just don’t get underfoot.

objects.title: City Road
objects.text: Moves all of the cities into a great chain stretching from one side of the wood to the other, giving an easy path of civilisation to the centre and beyond. This does make the rest of the woods more wild, and the path between cities can still be a challenge, but a considerable unburdening for all.

addons.text: More Navigable: The road is easier, with paths splitting off from it, though their furthest reaches are much reduced.

objects.title: Sexual Fauna
objects.text: The vast ecology of the woodland realm is bound to have some outliers. While goblins and ogers and other greenkin still hunt for ready wombs, stranger kin with stranger lifecycles now compete with them; monsters of swamp and branch and cave below, with eggs to lay or seed to gather, and no concept of consent.

addons.text: Peaceful: The creatures use pheromones and spores over force, to confuse and arouse their prey.

objects.title: Close Melliomer
objects.text: Return to the choices of Countries.

rows.title: The Ravaged Realms of Eardheart
rows.titleText:
A once fair country, charred black and blood drowned. Where once famed for its flowers, it is now known only for its demons, a great gate to a hell unknown spilling them forth to ravage all they encounter for little more than their own amusement. Cities have fallen, countless villages swallowed, and where not burned away outright, survivors tell of terrible things: endless reasons for why the dark hoard must be stopped here.

The calls have not gone unanswered. While at first disorganised, the armies of the human centric kingdoms of Eardheart have been fighting this war for over 150 years. Most do not remember a time without war. Adding to their number, countless groups, from religious crusaders and to honourless mercenaries, fight the menace to the bitter end in battles where surrender is unconscionable. The people here could certainly use a champion, or anything to break the long standing stalemate, and among them, demon blooded can be seen, outcast painful reminders of those who endured capture and birthed the result. More can be found here than anywhere else.

objects.title: The Great Demonic War
objects.text: They attack, they cause chaos and tragedy, they are slain and sent to hell, diminished. Tear still open, they return in time. Divine casters can burn the demons more than any other, but very few have the strength to destroy them utterly, and everything from lone demons to great warbands must be met along the vast chain of fortresses that have held a wavering line longer than most have been alive.

objects.title: The Disunified Realms
objects.text: The country holds many kingdoms, with long bitter rivalries, but they all fight the same enemy. Sadly, it is an enemy of varied means, and while some of their demonic numbers rampage, others subvert, leaving the kingdoms in an odd, politically charged cold war alliance. Outwardly, they would die to protect each other, and many mean it, yet allies sometimes arrive slow, and joint ventures bear mixed results.

objects.title: The Hands That Take Arms
objects.text: A wide verity of holy (and unholy) orders operate in the country, along with armies and mercenaries. There is also the grand collage of war, where skills of martial combat and battle magic are mastered, and ample opportunity given to test them. Other countries have pledged support, but that waned after a great wall was built on its border, leaving the kingdoms within Eardheart feeling abandoned.

objects.title: The Rape of Eardheart
objects.text: No one knows how it started, but for all these years, the battles, the raping, the kidnapping and torture, have gone on and on without end. The towns and villages that are captured, whose residents could not flee in time, find nothing so gentle as death, forced into oppressive horror by their new bickering rulers, who nurture and feed off their worst impulses. Some cut deals to live, loosing soul or mind to march beside their masters.

rows.title: The Turning of the Tide
rows.titleText: In the chaos of war, things change easily. It is for this reason that changing things is harder here. To save a city, another falls. To best an army, another rises. The countries slippery nature means that permeant changes, those that will not be undone by the time you arrive, feel more limited than they should be.

objects.title: Women at Arms
objects.text: Women have learned that the side-lines can quickly become the frontlines if the frontlines fall. They make up a quarter of the kingdoms fighting armies, and their work to manage, supply, and rearm gives them genuine equal rights to men. They are viewed as critical components for total war.

addons.text: Female: Despite the dangers unique to your gender, you will be met with more respect here than many other places.

objects.title: The Remorseful
objects.text: Being born demon touched is not a choice made. What you do after is. With this, Demon Touched are orphaned and raised in the war collage, forming some of the most powerful orders fighting against their progenitors. They make powerful allies and turn tragedy into begrudging respect.

addons.text: Demon Touched: If you fight against those that caused you, people cannot help but respect it.

objects.title: The Tainted
objects.text: Demonic forces are far more locally sourced, with corrupted mortals and those born demon touched making up a large contingent of their forces. They will focus more on ritual, subversion, and assassination, though they still march to war, and still commit atrocities, more brutal for their familiarity.

addons.text: The Remorseful: The most hated of rivalries form; the heart of the war, where no quarter or mercy is given. Demon Touched against Demon Touched.
Demon Touched: People will view you with added suspicion here. Don’t expect to be included in battle plans.

Breeding Evil: Already being bread, the demon touched, corrupted, and insane are now the backbone of the demons influence in the world. Battlefields, logistics, constructions, and infiltrations are more mundane, but no less dangerous.

objects.title: Corrupted Heros
objects.text: To break the will of one is to crack the will of all who looked up to them. Those heroes who rise and inspire are rarely allowed to die if overcome in battle or kidnapped in the night, returning months or years later on the side of the enemy, broken and degenerate, but just as deadly.

addons.text: Women at Arms: More fun to corrupt and more heart breaking to see corrupted, you will face more women among the corrupted champions.
Women at Arms + Female: The moment you gain notoriety or show power, expect them to come for you hard. You may want to consider killing yourself if it looks like they’ll succeed.

objects.title: Powerful Spellcasters
objects.text: Demonic forces now utilise powerful battle magic, their heavy hitters now requiring several collage trained mages to counter and overcome. Being demons, it is often mental magic used, driving frenzy into their forces, or madness into their enemies if they cannot dominate and control them outright.

objects.title: Skilled Strategists
objects.text: The demons are no longer playing, coordinating among themselves under skilled leaders with frightening strategic acumen and considerable personal power. They will attack with well thought purpose, but it cuts both ways, adding a single point of failure: the head of the snake.

addons.text: Powerful Spellcasters: They are often one in the same. Expect their magic to gain subtlety and its use to be perfectly timed. These will be very challenging foes to deal with.

objects.title: Few Over Many
objects.text: Instead of the wide range of evil forces, power will be concentrated in far fewer foes. To destroy one is a greater victory, but a far greater challenge, as now instead of an army, you may find yourself facing an army of one.

addons.text: The Tainted: This only effects demons so their mortal forces remain numerous. If anything, the incentive to cultivate them increases with conquered territory.
Powerful Spellcasters: These monsters can now dominate whole armies, and their spells can be far more destructive.
Skilled Strategists: While they have fewer forces to maneuverer, their personal combat ability increases significantly and their wicked intellect can still destabilise kingdoms.

Powerful Spellcasters & Skilled Strategists: The demons become true lords of hell, each surly impossible for any single champion to overcome. The only chance the civilised races have is due to their distrust of each other and the games of power they play.

objects.title: Close Eardheart
objects.text: Return to the choices of Countries.

rows.title: The Endless Deserts of Nellacomb
rows.titleText:
The stretching dune sea, scorched by the lash of the suns burn, is home to more life than its inhospitality warrants. Human cities and orcish bands, wondering beasts and beast kin, even the long dried dead cling to it, forebears of an ancient society long since departed. Yes, the sweat soaked competition of existence is alive and well in the numerous city states, petty fiefdoms, bandit hideouts, and tribal enclaves.

It is a place of duality. The sands constantly shift, revealing the spires of ancient structures, and territories also move with the tribes, and the politics of the cities are more often turned by knives and poisons than old age. Yet at the same time, it has always been thus, unchanging for as long as anyone can remember. One king falls, another rises; and the merchants sell their rugs and trinkets without interruption.

objects.title: The Heat
objects.text: The first things you’ll notice and the first enemy you’ll make, yet enjoyed by scorpion, snake, and desert spider. The rarely interrupted sun bakes the sands, but also stony ground and rocky canyons, shining on the southern jungles of Melliomer to the East and upon a jewelled sea to the West, and in the South, where the deep desert hides ruins unseen for millennia.

objects.title: The Old Empire
objects.text: According to legend, a bellicose empire rose here, fighting and ultimately being destroyed by the kingdom of the floating fortresses, before they too fell into ruin. Necromancy must have been a part of their society as they still guard their tombs and temples, keeping empty sockets upon jewels and gold and keeping their greedy inheritors away with traps and terror.

objects.title: The New Sultanate
objects.text: Perhaps once outliers of the old empire, the several dozen cities remaining now answer to no one but themselves. Each has a Sultan, each has its own rules, and they range from poor lawless places to shining beacons of gold and culture. One contains Akzinianar, the great university of magic, history, and culture. Another contains Wound, a combat pit and brothel where even children are forced to take part.

objects.title: The Tribes Between
objects.text: From rich jungle to baron cliffs, tribes can be found. Some are Orcs, strong and hardy, while others are human, ever adaptable. They skirmish with each other, acting as bandits to the cities and its traders, and guides for those seeking the deep deserts paths. Minotaurs and other beast kin can also be found, and a cave that contains rare water can have anything living within it.

rows.title: Shifting the Sands
rows.titleText: Like the narrow squeeze of an hourglass against a great and endless pouring of sand, great changes feel near impossible to sort through, hot to the touch and wearing to the spirit. Squinting against light and heat, you focus on what you can change.

objects.title: Blood on the Sands
objects.text: Wars are not fought on the shifting sands, the slip of a knife being a surer path to power. Now the city Sultans wage wars against each other openly for territory, using professional soldiers, mercenaries, conscripts, criminals, tribespeople, and whatever other enterprising adventurer accepting of coin.

objects.title: Permitted Slavery
objects.text: The buying and selling of people, usually criminals, is now legal throughout Nellacomb, allowing them to be put to work dependent on their skills and station. From mines and brothels to the personal pleasures of royalty. Few like slavery, save the slave owner, as even the most selfish lament the lost chance for a job.

addons.text: Blood on the Sands: War gives a greater opportunity for enslavement, both in taking and being taken. War prisoners can be sold into lengthy terms; you could earn a profit or lose it all.

objects.title: Rampant Slavery
objects.text: Now slavery is engrained within the culture of the desert. Captives of all kinds can become slaves. Owning one is an aspired symbol of status and the buying, selling, and using of them done openly and with pride. Skill in management has grown, and with the right shackles, even the most powerful can now be tamed, owned, and used.

addons.text: Blood on the Sands: Slaves are now a key resource wars are fought for, with not just soldiers taken, but any persons who can be overcome by them. Even if you mind your own business, being in the wrong place at the wrong time can have others trying to collar you.

objects.title: Desert Fashions
objects.text: Instead of covering up, people will wear less, at least in the safe shadows of the cities. What would be considered brothel attire in any other country is quite normal in Nellacomb, and many flustered foreigners are laughed at until they wear the same. This has led to a promiscuous reputation the locals do little to dissuade.

addons.text: Permitted Slavery: Slaves wear very little, their collar all the clothes they need.
Rampant Slavery: Slaves wear basically nothing, their collar all the clothes they need. If their master wills it, they must wear a signifier that allows free use by all.

objects.title: Great Beasts
objects.text: Before, a range of relatively small things, with lion like creatures the biggest about. Now the wastes hold vast and frightening monsters: great lizards that swim though sands like water, vast vulture like birds that glide on the ever rising heat, basilisks and sand-mantas, and dragon like things. Dealing with any will be a great challenge.

addons.text: Blood on the Sands: The beasts may be captured for use in war.

objects.title: Hazardous Preservations
objects.text: Instead of dried eyeless husks buried beneath the sands, the magic that animates and binds spirit to form now preserves as well. They are near the same as the living, keeping more of the deadly skills they had in life. Only the soul is rotted to undeath, the mind slipped into endless unquestioning purpose.

addons.text: Terrifying Undead: Preservation does not heal injuries, and a headless naked person sprinting at you is definitely terrifying.
Sexual Undead: Yes, it’s all fully functional, and yes they will use it, long beyond you passing out from it. Among the least horrifying undead to be effected by this.

objects.title: Great Ruins
objects.text: The old Empire was now a truly monolithic superpower. While much of it is still gone, what remains is vast and deep, each ruin once a super structure centuries in the making, like hollowed out mountains. Exploring just one could take months, maybe years, with no guarantee of each secret passage found or treasure plundered or defence undone.

objects.title: Vast Cities
objects.text: The cities now carry their creators mark: no longer engorged outposts built-up over the long years, but vast and complex places, often towering over the landscape and stretching deep into the sands below. While populous, there are rumours that not even they have been fully explored, and that sewers and hidden ways still carry treasure and undead.

addons.text: Blood on the Sands: It is not unheard of for a whole city to be split down the middle with war, but be so vast that the lines do not move for months or even years.

objects.title: Treasure Seekers Guild
objects.text: Before, only the brave or stupid would set a course for the deep deserts and the ruined wonders of the old kingdom. Now, an official organisation, unconnected to any one city, has gathered an eclectic collection of thieves, archaeologists, mages and scholars, tribespeople and madmen, to brave the deadliest of adventures.

addons.text: Great Ruins: The guild now sets up long standing bases of operation for each ruin.
Vast Cities: Each city has a guild presence. They are among the few who know just how deep they go.

objects.title: Close The Nellacomb Desert
objects.text: Return to the choices of Countries.

rows.title: The Fathomless Flow of The Deep Rivers
rows.titleText:
Far far below all of the six points and the lands between, lies the greatest kingdom of all. Its length reaches from the far side of The Great Forest of Melliomer, to the sea caves at the end of Eardheart. From the most barren ends of the deep desert, to the foundations of the Highmarch peaks. The veins of the world, running subterranean channels in a woven maze of darkness. A place where the sun will never shine.

Despite its grim and foreboding nature, many call this place their home, the most well-known among them the Drow, whose elegant narrow boats can take travellers wherever they need to go. They don’t though, at least without cost. Below the world, trust runs thin, and the Drow must contend with more than just their treacherous selves. The windless surface of vast and flowless lakes ripple with disturbances from below, where rumours and whispers speak of a hole in the world of a different kind. Dwarves and other subterranean creatures make homes in the cold stone, and strangers from above, who would dare cross the realm of the Drow without permission or payment.

objects.title: Winding Reaches
objects.text: The tunnels are a maze; many who travel too carelessly miss the paths that join their own, finding more ways to go behind than ahead. Rivers don’t always flow in the same direction and hold strange currents and whirlpools, and while the Drow have mapped the safe ways, don’t expect them to share easily. Only the most memorable lakes or expansive cities, lit by luminescent fungus or algae, can be navigated unaided.

objects.title: The People of the Dark
objects.text: Had they their way, the Drow would hold total dominion, yet the Dwarves have sizable communities as well. Even combined they do not fill a thousandth of the paths and river ways, yet that does not keep them from coming to blows, arguing and fighting over strategic chokepoints, resources, safe passages, or perceived slights. Trade does occur in goods and service, but it is marred by narrowed eyes and unkind words.

objects.title: Things That Aren’t People
objects.text: Both Dwarf and Drow know there are things that only grow in the dark: goblins and even chittering beasts of the earth may be slain, disturbances attributed to them, yet they know so little. Ancient terrors and nightmares slither, and for all the tunnels are long, the rivers and lakes are deep, their depths and their dwellers hidden in the inky waters. They draw some from the surface below, dreams compelling them down, and where they go, few dare to venture.

objects.title: Most Dangerous of All
objects.text: Politics. Perhaps an older threat than even what lies below. To enter the matriarchal society of the Drow is to step into a hundred schemes and to be the start of a hundred more. Opportunities abound for anyone with the wits to navigate such strong currents, but most simply pay the ferrywoman nobles in what gold, jewels, power, or service is asked, keeping heads down and eyes open if they wish to reach their destination alive.

rows.title: The Currents Redirected
rows.titleText: To look upon the many paths and to see into the unseeable deep gives you the beginnings of a headache, and even from the dream you feel watched from below, as though a star being viewed by a distant world. The place feels cold and wet, and you have no desire to touch it more than is necessary.

objects.title: Infiltrated Schemers
objects.text: The Drow are now being unknowingly controlled by the creatures of the other places. In some cases, whispers in the minds of leaders, and in others, agents gained through replacement or transformation. Whatever the method, the Drow politic serve unknowable goals that are not their own.

objects.title: Powerful Influences
objects.text: Near their source, the creatures, slaves, and minions of the other place gain a considerable boost to their strange powers, tapping in to forces left behind. While away from it, they will weaken. You will know their source by its guardians, and must fight them on your terms if you’re to stand a chance.

objects.title: Drow Faith
objects.text: Before, faith was a presence in Drow society, but a tool, not a mission. Now it gains a resurgence, with old scriptures found anew and their goddess taking a more attentive role in ritual and prayer. Their leaders become priestesses and their society becomes less stable during the difficult transition.

addons.text: Infiltrated Schemers: The ‘Goddess’ isn’t what she seems, and the requirements of the faith will conveniently cause conflict with all unwilling to be controlled by the abyssal forces lurking below.

objects.title: Old Ruins
objects.text: The hole was not made unbidden. The ruins of an ancient people can now be found below, and while not so common as the ruins found above, these hold secrets of the other world, why the door was opened, and perhaps even how it may be closed. Such places hold dangers though, sacred to the cults drawn below.

addons.text: Drow Faith: The ruins align with the faith, making it easy to encourage the Drow to help uncover them. Could the Drow have faced such other worldly things before?
Infiltrated Schemers + Drow Faith: The ruins align a little too closely with the faith, who rush to protect them and close them off from enquiring eyes. Investigating them will be a challenge.

objects.title: Giant Horrors
objects.text: Before, the tunnels held more than their fair share of dangerous beasts, the worst being spiders the size of bears, or eels as long a boats. Now many of those beasts are bigger in size. Giant slugs and spiders, slimes and centipedes, obstacles too large and too dangerous to get past.

addons.text: Powerful Influences: For those deep forces that cannot claim to be native to the world, well, you’ll know them if you see them, and learn not to cross certain lakes or deep rivers.

objects.title: Goblin Capital
objects.text: Near the reaches far bellow Melliomer and stretching down to the deep waters, a vast goblin city has been founded, where most goblins come from and many captives are taken to. They spread through the caverns and passage ways to find a way up, and bring chaotic skirmishes into the dark.

addons.text: Female Goblins: Rather than war, conflict, and kidnapping, they simply become a third semi-friendly faction below, much to the chagrin of the Drow.

Evil Goblins: The chaos they bring ill suites those from the deep, leading to a strange war and hostility between the impossibly old and the ever replenishing new. Remember, the enemy of your enemy is NOT your friend.

objects.title: More Light
objects.text: While some parts of the rivers contain bioluminescent algae, mushrooms, and even animals, it is far from all and far from bright. Only Drow cities cultivate such things enough for surface dwellers to see by. Now the lights are on, and the deep rivers become a beautiful forest of lights and life.

objects.title: Merfolk
objects.text: An often overlooked element: the rivers and lakes now teem with a new and dangerous faction of merfolk. Adapted to the darkness, they inhabit the places that other worldly forces don’t, and while that means seeing them is one form of good news, their hostile nature and ghastly appearance sooths no nerves.

addons.text: More Light: Instead of adapted to the dark, they are more akin to their surface cousins in both manner and appearance. Less proud perhaps, and more passive and skittish, but helpful if traded with, and eager to cast out other worldly forces.

objects.title: Close The Deep Rivers
objects.text: Return to the choices of Countries.

rows.title: They All Look So Near, And So Far…
rows.titleText: You give each country one more glance with lasting understanding. Now you can set your mind onwards, continuing a train of thought towards the next thing to think about. Perhaps you’ll choose one of these countries for your arrival, when you’re ready for it. At least for now…

objects.title: You Know Of The Countries
objects.text: Select this to unlock the other section of The World In Sight, taking one step closer to your new life.

objects.title: Close The Countries
objects.text: Return to the world in sight.

rows.title: Lidded Eyes On Dormientes
rows.titleText:
Dormientes, the citadel. Dormientes, the city. Dormientes, the country. One in the other in the other, like nesting dolls. The citadel is like a dark black spot in your vision, as impenetrable to you here as it is for all those below, patrolled by powerful golems ready to face the impossibility of someone approaching without falling into a deep sleep. A respectful distance is all the city gives: a wall and an open space all around as the place of power is swallowed by long rejected hopefuls.

Unlike the centre, the city is changeable. Unlike the six points, the country is changeable. Both shiver beneath your fingertips, eager for change, as though restrained since the last dreamer so very long ago. To brush your fingers through its grass is to hear its purr, responsive and kind, and by instinct, you touch. Changes are immediate, not unlike smearing the wet paint of a portrait, yet disruption, no matter how careless, settles things into how they should be, and will be, and always have been, the moment you stop. It is like the fine hand of creation guides your own.

You’ll need to be careful. The prizes, and the guidance of the Soporatus Cult needed to get them, will have you coming back here. Crossing from land to land leaves this as the shortest route, and its sheer size will not make your stay quick. This is a land you may visit more than any other, and for all you effect it now, it will repay you in kind later on.

objects.title: The Land
objects.text: Such a vast place, yet clay in your hands.

objects.title: The People
objects.text: A varied mix of bodies, minds, and hazy culture.

objects.title: The Ruler
objects.text: The leaders of the realm, the good and the bad.

objects.title: The Rule
objects.text: Laws and those who enforce or avoid them.

rows.title: The Scenery of the Centre
rows.titleText:
Best to begin with the sweeping changes. You see a fairly pastoral place, with fields and woods and hills. Nothing out of the ordinary: all the plain nature of a temperate clime. You can see where the country changes naturally, blurring over great distance into hotter dryer regions to the south, and getting hillier in the north and more wooded to the east. You needn’t change a thing, but wouldn’t that be the waste of a chance? The topography could be as you choose.

Listing off the features there could be, the country seems eager to show you where they could go and how they could mix. It all makes sense, and fits by miracle. You could add any number of features: the country is big enough to accommodate all of them. Alternatively, you could select just a few. After all, the boldest pictures mix the fewest colours.

objects.title: Pastoral
objects.text: A greater emphasis on the pleasantries of the countryside.

objects.title: Rivers
objects.text: Not just streams and brooks, but a web of great arterial river ways that streak the land.

objects.title: Lakelands
objects.text: Vast lakes, big enough to hold islands of their own, and for towns of river trade to be built upon them.

objects.title: Forest
objects.text: You smear your thumb from east to west, stretching the greens of a more sensible forest.

objects.title: Meadows
objects.text: Natural fields of flowers and low lying nature. Beautiful and exposed.

objects.title: Northern Cold
objects.text: Cold from the north blows down harder, dusting more often with fallen snow and winter chill.

objects.title: Boreal
objects.text: Like Melliomers’ northern reaches: trees and plants adapted to the bitter cold.

objects.title: Glacier
objects.text: Great walls of ice and permafrost, with paths and even towns carved into them.

objects.title: Hills
objects.text: The land rolls, rising and falling to the dominion of hills and valleys.

objects.title: Mountains
objects.text: From timid hills to wild mountains. The country will be divided by towering ranges.

objects.title: Southern Heat
objects.text: Like pulling up a blanket, warm air blows up from the south, bringing the heat of an ever summer sun.

objects.title: Jungle
objects.text: More lively and wild, the forest becomes a jungle, hot and humid and teeming with life.

objects.title: Deserts
objects.text: Smearing south to north, you bring the dry heat and sandy deserts of Nellacomb to bear.

objects.title: Dry
objects.text: Warmer and more tropical temperatures lead to drier soil and hardier life.

objects.title: Rocky
objects.text: Grass and fern have less soil to grow, but rich veins can be mined by the hard of sole.

objects.title: Sea
objects.text: This turns the country into an archipelago, with the four adjacent countries their own continents and the biomes above scattered across countless islands.

addons.text: Bandits will become pirates and the beasts of the wilds will become creatures of the sea, while many trade and passenger ships hop the islands, keeping the ‘country’ a lively and dangerous place.

objects.title: Less Fractured
objects.text: Rather than a series of many islands, the control of which can be fraught, there are instead five large continents separated by the sea. This gives rise to different cultures while keeping the ability to go inland far enough that salt is not in the air.

objects.title: Flooded
objects.text: While the country is still mostly water, much of it is now fresh water that has smothered the land in lakes and rivers so vast they are indistinguishable from ocean. The waters will be shallower and cut the land apart, but the heights of the land are still connected haphazardly.

objects.title: Hard to Traverse
objects.text: Crossing from one side to the other is more of a challenge due to the unique geography.

objects.title: Venerable
objects.text: The land is holier closer to the city, with restless spirits more in need of appeasement. One shouldn’t cross without care.

objects.title: Broken
objects.text: A place of odd land formation, where one wonders what strange event could have churned the world so.

objects.title: Grandeur
objects.text: The lands of this country don’t do things by halves. From titanic waterfalls to towering cliffs, everything is bigger.

objects.title: Untamed
objects.text: Roads and bridges are no more, with dirt paths that suffer natures hunger all that is left. Untouched and untraveled.

objects.title: Close The Land
objects.text: Return to the choices of Dormientes.

rows.title: The Culture as Shared
rows.titleText:
People are more than individuals. Connecting them all is a web of shared experiences, language, and history. Looking at them now, like moats of light in the dark, you can see details and patterns in the static lull they have fallen into. The majority are human, but more than anywhere else, variety in species is alive and well, all drawn to the same promise. You see elves and dwarves and orcs. Those touched by the heavens and the hells. Even those not alive, golem forms marching to their masters orders. To pull on one is to pull on them all.

You try to gauge who they are: what kind of people they would be. It’s near impossible. Close to the blinding dark of the citadel, whose lofty doors are locked to those lacking the keys of entry; close to the changeability that lies at the heart of this place; to observe is to alter, and to think on what kind of people they would be, is to make them so. You can no more leave them undisturbed than you could walk through smoke without shifting it, or move into water without a ripple, but your passage would still leave people. To change them now is to simply shift them from the baseline of any typical culture.

And so with a thought, you know them to be a people known far and wide for their…

objects.title: Good Food
objects.text: Spices from the south, beasts from the east, sea trade and skills from the west, and their own home grown produce. The perfect recipe for a culture of food.

objects.title: Bad Food
objects.text: Salt is for nobility, and spices are considered Drow magic. A bullish people, where quantity should beat quality, and enough should be good enough.

objects.title: Friendly Locals
objects.text: People travel from all around to be near the place of power and try their luck. They are welcome company and welcome coin.

objects.title: Unfriendly Locals
objects.text: Strange folk with a standoffish attitude. People come to try for the powers that rest, and that makes newcomers fools or rivals, and rarely welcomed.

objects.title: Cultured Nature
objects.text: Music, art, poetry, theatre. Anything that delights the senses. Where there is adventure, bards of all kinds are not far behind.

objects.title: Uncouth Attitude
objects.text: Music is a tavern song, theatre is a fight, and poetry is the sound of knocked out teeth rattling across the floor. As uncultured as can be and proud of it.

objects.title: Extravagant Notions
objects.text: Always willing to go the extra mile, their cities and towns are lavishly decorated. Even the poorest house would put up wreaths and clutter their walls with what they have.

objects.title: Austere Sensibilities
objects.text: Their action, their culture, architecture are all what they needs to be to function. Even in their highest halls, uncluttered spaces are the way to go.

objects.title: Lecherousness
objects.text: They’re noted for their crassness around the people they desire. From long glances to catcalls to inappropriate touching and worse, disrespect is the start of their low effort courtship.

objects.title: Sexual Repression
objects.text: Courtship is a long process, and such people will not even begin it without going through the proper channels or making the proper considerations.

objects.title: Hedonistic Indulgence
objects.text: Be it food, fighting, or sex, the people of the country are known for their self-indulgent habits. Orgies of all kind will be held, and fun will be the point of life.

objects.title: Temperate Sensibilities
objects.text: The betterment of society is held in high regard and people will more often abstain from what is fun in favour of what is right. Generally considered a sensible people.

objects.title: Honourable Actions
objects.text: How someone competes is seen as more important than what they win, or lose. Surrender is respected, and displays of chivalry will earn you friends for life.

objects.title: Honourless Behaviour
objects.text: Losers deserve to lose and winners deserve all they can take. If you lose because you didn’t take every chance you could, you can only blame yourself.

objects.title: Prowess and Dominance
objects.text: Drawn to power, or raised in its promise, the country respects and cultivates strength of all kinds, raising skilled soldiers and statesmen.

objects.title: Failure and Fools
objects.text: Those drawn to the capital, and their descendants, have ever failed to get the power within. A culture of buried bitter resentment and defeatism.

objects.title: Loose Attire
objects.text: People wear what they like and often times that is very little. While outright nudity in certain places may still raise some eyebrows, it will rarely raise complaints.

objects.title: Reserved Dress
objects.text: Prudish adherence will have people cover themselves often for the sake of decency. Necklines and ankles will carry a forbidden provocative lure of their own.

objects.title: Strict Hierarchy
objects.text: The young obey the old, the poor obey the rich, the weak obey the strong. There is an order to these people that they culturally accept an obedience to.

objects.title: Troublemakers
objects.text: To get drunk and cause pointless destruction, or to rail against perceived injustices. The people take nothing lying down, from anyone.

objects.title: Adventurers
objects.text: The romantic notion of striking out and seeing the world is strong. As a nexus of people and trouble, the country is known for adventure, and those who seek it.

objects.title: Criminality
objects.text: Whether the law can keep up is one thing, but here there is a definite cultural draw to disrespecting the law for the benefit of one’s self.

rows.title: The Bonds Between
rows.titleText:
More than how people act alone, they can be better judged by how they act with each other. Their relationships and bonds begin with basic factors and preconceived notions, and you feel you will notice more when they judge you by what you cannot change.

Here, without a touch, the society may tick on by, too mixed and too cultured to hold any truly repugnant prejudices. Men will be men and women will be women, mostly equal but not quite, and races will grumble of each other, yet mostly stay in their lanes. But perhaps that could change? It would only take a touch…

objects.title: Male Supremacy
objects.text: It is men who take the reins of this society. They are its leaders, its soldiers and workers. Women are too delicate a flowers to subject to more than the warmth of a kitchen or a marriage bed. Occasionally, they may get uppity, and it’s down to a man to gently yet firmly remind them of their place.

addons.text: Male: You are placed head and shoulders above your female counterparts, and while life may not be easier (save for the lack of competition), it most certainly won’t be harder.

Female: You’re place is at the lower end of society and your quest will become harder in the face of sexism and assumptions of your weakness. Expect the local blacksmith to try and sell you pots and pans over swords and shields.

objects.title: Male Domination
objects.text: Men rise even higher, trampling on women to do so. It is now highly unusual for a woman to be free of the control of a man, either farther or husband. If they are then they’re seen as whores for it. Their only protection is as property whose damage must be compensated for, and the thought of one fighting would send men into apoplexy.

addons.text: Male: As a man, you will be respected and your whims will be catered for. Unwed daughters will be offered for sale, along with opportunity and education. Desperate women who have fallen through the cracks of society will be for mercy at your feet, and people are more likely to assume a competence and intellect you do not have.

Female: As a woman, you will be treated as an object, silent unless spoken to, and obedient to all the men about you. To speak out of turn would be an outrage and to defend yourself a literal crime that would put you in the stocks until your lesson is learned. Reputable jobs and education are out of the question, and while the Soporatus Cult will still support you, there will be definite opposition and hostility throughout Dormientes to the thought of a woman questing for the power.

Female + Beautiful: You will be in for a difficult time, being a prize for men to take and drape across their arm and their bed, and your opinion will not enter into it. Being fought over may seem fun to the neglected, but when it is spoiled children who would rather break their toy if they cannot keep it, it can be very dangerous.

objects.title: Female Supremacy
objects.text: Women hold the keys to governance; the decisions of the cities and villages and families have been carefully removed from the brutish emotional grasp of careless men and placed under the guidance of the fairer sex. Men still labour, their strength their utility, but should they speak up without respect they would be shushed into silence.

addons.text: Female: You are placed head and shoulders above your male counterparts. Expectations upon you may increase, and things will not simply be handed to you for your gender, but you will have significantly more privileges, and with the right coin or influence, certainly any man you may desire, as guard, servant, or something else. Birth control is significantly more advanced.

Male: Yours is the lot of the guard, the farmer, and the miner. Rarely the shopkeep, clerk, or scholar, and most certainly not where decisions are made. Legally, you’re second class, with the law always siding with women, and you will be expected to cater to them and protect them, even if they offer little respect in return.

objects.title: Female Domination
objects.text: It takes one man to impregnate multiple women, and while some backwards countries have women filled harems, here the logic is corrected in reverse: society simply doesn’t need very many men at all. A few studs with appropriate traits in brothels, the rest serving as simple docile beasts where labour of violence is needed. Rights for them are non-existent.

addons.text: Female: As a woman, this society is made for you. All the difficult and dangerous actions are taken by men, while all the task that require a brain are done by women. You will be expected lead and command, and your quest for the powers will be natural, with many women acting as your rivals.

Male: There will be fewer men about and so you will stand out unless standing your place, subservient to any woman who commands you and wishes to use you for whatever purpose they want. While this may seem like a boon to the foolish, they quickly change their mind on arrival, facing what it’s like to be disposable labour at the bottom of the totem pole. They usually escape after their first night in the stock for looking a woman in the eye, or when an unsatisfied woman talks of circumcision to make them last longer.

Male + Beautiful: You, as all men, will be directed to the right place for your use. As a very handsome man, that use will be between the legs of a woman, and you’d better be good at it. Either brothel work or private stud. The smile slips when you remember, this is not a nation of scantily clad amazons; women who needn’t compete with looks for male attentions won’t.

objects.title: Other Superiority
objects.text: Those uncategorised in the prosaic sexes are seen as a form of alchemic higher being: a combination perfected or absent from nature, carrying a strange and enticing allure that is taboo to no one. Those who wish to change may pursue magic or alchemic aid to do so, and so you will find those pursuing this goal more frequently.

addons.text: Other: As one who is viewed as the new and exciting, you will find curious partners aplenty. Respect and inquiry will grow, and your unique point of view will give your voice more weight in matters of decision, philosophy, and sexuality.

objects.title: Other Rejection
objects.text: A few freaks of nature breed uncertainty into the world, and deviants who pursue strange modification are rightly shunned. Dormientes is a country in which men are men and women are women, and anyone who doesn’t fall into those categories, despite their fetishisation by the few, are resolutely viewed as lesser.

addons.text: Other: You will face rejection from this society, though you can ‘pass’ as whatever you most resemble on the surface. To be discovered by anyone not as accepting will leave you shunned, or even hunted by those who view you as lesser, to be ‘corrected’ in body and manner, or disposed of.

objects.title: True Gender Equality
objects.text: Instead of the typical divisions between men and women, this society is barrierless in its expectations of people. About half the soldiers are women, half those at home raising children are men, and from leaders to workers to the poverty stricken homeless, diversity of gender flows freely.

objects.title: Increased Homosexuality
objects.text: As with the ancient cultures you know, homosexuality becomes the accepted norm, with a persons own gender offering fun and service without the risks of familial commitments. Not all take part, but about half of society, be they men or women, will be or have been in same sex relationships.

addons.text: Strict Hierarchy: Truly like ancient times. Masters will form sexual relationships with apprentices, novitiates will ‘honour’ their senior members, and advancement often comes with a cost of service. This can lead to abuses of power, but they are abuses many will turn a blind eye to, accepting them as the norm.
Male Supremacy: The height of manliness is to be such a man that only a man can satisfy you. Women, meanwhile, are left with the dregs, namely women and the half of men too weak to take a real man.

Female Supremacy: Being the height of beauty, it is fashionable for women to fancy each other, and those who still fancy men will at least be bisexual. The men not lucky enough to be fancied by a woman can satisfy their urges with each other.

objects.title: Additional Racism
objects.text: The races of this world may have their animosities, but in this country and for its people, some are truly held lower than others. This opens a new section to find which races are viewed as lesser here than elsewhere.

objects.title: Racial Exaltation
objects.text: Some are held with a greater respect here, due to history, myths, and the passing of great individuals. This opens a new section to find out which races are held above others and receive special leniency and treatment.

rows.title: The Tensions Between Races
rows.titleText:
There is no getting away from racisms, especially when the races are made so differently. While a mostly human country, this can make drastic changes to who is in control, from royal guard captains to small business owners. Of course, it also factors into who remains jobless in the streets, and who are forced to turn to crime or dishonourable dealings to survive, perpetuating the stigmas against them.

Naturally, any choice chosen here reduces the number of that race within the usually diverse central country, with those left having a very hard time.

objects.title: Inferior Humans
objects.text: Despite being the most populous, they are viewed as the weakest and most useless, leaving them as the chaff of society. Soldiers, prostitutes, and labourers are all they’re fit for.

addons.text: Your Race: Complex or responsible jobs will be kept out of your reach, and your fame will spread slowly outside of the human parts of town.

objects.title: Subservient Elves
objects.text: Beautiful, but fragile. In Dormientes they are viewed as weak and breakable things, desirable in a sexual sense, but unfit to be part of the strong core of a society.

addons.text: Your Race: While you may inspire the fanaticise of a quick fuck, the false smiles will quickly fade when it comes to ‘real’ work.

objects.title: Heartless Dwarves
objects.text: Viewed as unwelcoming clockwork contraptions, with greed in place of a heart, the stout folk lack the delicate touch needed for society to function. They should stick to their mountains.

addons.text: Your Race: The short jokes will make you act as bitter and angry as they assume you to be, and as one viewed as so tight fisted with money, thieves will assume you have some to take.

objects.title: Vicious Orcs
objects.text: The presence of tribes and raiders and ill history means the strength of the orcs is a misery to weather against, not to invite into a city or a home. Even the usual slums are too good for them.

addons.text: Your Race: You cannot be kept out entirely, but the inconveniences put in your way will mount up. Segregated dirt paths, animal beds, and being stopped and questioned by every guard will be the norm.

objects.title: Scheming Drow
objects.text: As fair as the elves perhaps, but half as trustworthy. Old plots leave olds scars, and while folk would be happy to bed one, they’d be less happy to sleep beside them.

addons.text: Your Race: People will view what happens to you as deserved, simply pre-empting your own betrayal of them. They will gladly take whatever they want of you, ‘civility’ the only thing holding them back.

objects.title: Celestial Heresies
objects.text: Demons have an interest in discrediting the heavenly touched, and have succeeded enough to soil the usual respect here, curing them with an unlucky and unwelcome reputation.

addons.text: Your Race: Where once viewed as beautiful and precious, people will instead question your origins and motives, assuming a trick of or against the gods, depending on their point of view. They’ll likely avoid you as a result.

objects.title: Demon Tainted
objects.text: The foulness of demons should be kept in the west, and the signs of Eardhearts problems are an unwelcome reminder of a fate that could soon be shared.

addons.text: Your Race: Viewed as cursed and an omen of worse to come, people will cross the street to avoid you, and spit at your feet if they can’t, making holy signs all the while.

objects.title: Barbaric Harpies
objects.text: The bird people have never been welcome in the cities and villages, but a recent trends of feather collecting and a high profile murder made them profitable bounties.

addons.text: Your Race: Already difficult to interact with, the city, its people, and the cult you need sanctions from, will all view you as vermin, whose plumbs could mean coins in their pockets.

objects.title: Soulless Constructs
objects.text: The rare golems were ignored before, but after some ran wild due to a novice mage, each are viewed with suspicion here.

addons.text: Your Race: People will now watch you warily in Dormientes, waiting for you to go mad, or demanding to know where your maker is. Guards may follow you, to ‘protect’ others from you, and others may try to rob or provoke you, any response of yours simply proving people right.

rows.title: The Races That Rise Above
rows.titleText:
It doesn’t take much to put others on a pedestal. A play, a story, a misstelling of history. Even a living person whose fame leaves them idolised can raise the unrelated above their previous standing. In the central country of Dormientes, this has happened with a few groups, placing them higher than perhaps they otherwise should be.

This will be reflected in the positions they will more easily find themselves in. Government and business and soldiery will place them in leadership positions due to assumed competence, while others will have to work harder to reach the same heights.

objects.title: Human Greatness
objects.text: It is only natural. Humans are the most populous race within Dormientes and thus should be its masters. An elf may live longer and a celestial may be more charismatic, but a human in command feels right.

addons.text: Your Race: This gives you advantage over other races in your dealing in the city. People will much prefer the thought of their fellow human getting the power they all seek than someone else.

objects.title: Elven Grace
objects.text: The long lived elves are both fair and wise, and easy to place on a pedestal. To give them a position as royal guard not only ensures competence, but that said competence will continue to grow and remain over centuries.

addons.text: Your Race: Expect smiles and nods and flustered confessions of admiration from people. Others will seek your advice, even if you are younger than they, and will wish to protect you, your life seen as a valuable store of knowledge.

objects.title: Dwarven Reliability
objects.text: The mountain folk are held in high esteem for their crafts and the stories of their vast underground cities. A history of strong and enduring alliance between Dormientes and the northern Dwarven clans have forged unbreakable bonds of friendship.

addons.text: Your Race: The occasional boisterous tale told over free drinks will make you out to be the hero, even if it took place several hundred years ago, and when you talk, people will listen and assume truth.

objects.title: Stalwart Orcs
objects.text: Unlike elsewhere, the Orc tribes of Dormientes earned their respect, coming to the aid of the country and its people when the Demons plaguing Eardheart first appeared. Their strength, both physically and of character, are things now held in high regard.

addons.text: Your Race: Where before, people would view you harshly, now they feel safer around you: a strong and honourable presence that can do much good should bad things begin to happen.

objects.title: Allied Drow
objects.text: Due to a few more open passages down to the Dep Rivers, the Drow have become trading partners who have surprised all by being generally honourable and trustworthy. Their work in reducing goblin numbers from belowground have been beneficial to all as well.

addons.text: Your Race: No longer will the worse be assumed of you, in Dormientes at least. Your people have bought the trust of the locals, either genuinely or as part of a plot, and it is you that stand to benefit.

objects.title: Heavenly Celestials
objects.text: The Soporatus Cult may be a significant influence in the central country, but many other cults exist and hold anyone touched by celestial influences to be divine. To be favoured by one is to be favoured by the gods, and more so than elsewhere, that favour is dearly cherished.

addons.text: Your Race: People will beg for your blessing, asking you to kiss their babies or simply favour them with a smile. The number who would do anything to breed with you, mixing their bloodline with yours, may become worrying.

objects.title: Demonic Celebrity
objects.text: A famous saga did the rounds a few years back, in taverns and playhouses, about a demon touched who slew their father, a demon lord. While only loosely based on real events, it has shown how demon touched and their infernal power can be a force for good.

addons.text: Your Race: While it may be irritating to be compared to a character of mostly fiction, simply saying you don’t like demons, or lowering yourself to mutter some famous lines, will have crowds of people smiling and cheering for you.

objects.title: Harpy Freedom
