objects.text: A quite famous adventurer recently returned from the floating fortresses, telling tales of a beautiful harpy who saved them, swooping in to pull them out of danger, and supposedly share a night of wild passion. While doubtless embellished, is has left some more willing to give the birds another chance.

addons.text: Your Race: People will be more willing to ask questions and less likely to chase you off. There may even be some romantic advances.

objects.title: Construct of Kindness
objects.text: A golem maker setup shop, and to advertise his creations, he sent them out into the city to do good and show their helpful utility. After saving two dozen people from a fire, golems are now viewed as a force for good, their reliability invaluable.

addons.text: Your Race: Rather than treating you as a machine, people will treat you more with endearment, like a local oddball with a good heart. Separate, but included.

rows.title: The Style They Choose
rows.titleText:
The most surface level change of a people is how they choose to look. Their theme may be skin deep, but it is tied to their culture and sensibilities and you will see it reflected in their architecture, their dress, their livery and banners, and even their names. Being so close to the grand fortress that houses sleep and power, the people simply reflect its style, and its outward style is one of the few things you can change about it.

You needn’t make any change at all though, keeping it unremarkable from other cities of this world.

objects.title: The Light of the Dawn
objects.text: The citadel is a hall of light, and so the city is a display of outward morality. White and gold fashions, ivory pale stones, and domes that sparkle in the sun; it may all be a reflection of clear conscience, or an insipid whitewash of the truth.

objects.title: The Dark of the Night
objects.text: The centre of Dormientes is an evil looking thing, and so the city built around it follows suit. Black is in, with grim gothic architecture that speaks of endless night nestled in dark reaches. Even in the sun it seems to stubbornly stand in defiance.

objects.title: The Natural World
objects.text: The citadel is overgrown by unsleeping nature, and the capital becomes just as remiss. Trees, bushes, moss, and weeds bring nature to the unnatural, spreading earthen smells into city streets, and the colour of flowers upon peoples commutes.

objects.title: A Barbaric Place
objects.text: Regardless of what came before, what is there now is rough: a city made by adventurers instead of masons. In the place of stout stone, there will be rough shacks and wood planks, with even the most permanent and grand structures having a temporary air.

objects.title: An Urban Centre
objects.text: Already large enough to touch each horizon from its centre, the city becomes more condensed, piling upward, its grand quarried stones scarcely supporting its own mighty weight as they squeeze dark and narrow streets between towering buildings.

objects.title: Close The People
objects.text: Return to the choices of Dormientes.

rows.title: Who Reigns over the Reins
rows.titleText:
And why does it matter? Anyone powerful enough to seek the trophies and succeed may begin to look at the rules of kingdoms as mere suggestions, its leaders quaint and antiquated, yet the leader will set the laws of the land to their will, and you will be forced to interact with them or face the consequences of refusal. They will be a surprisingly significant character in the story of your rise, and tragically enough for them, likely the villain.

Kings and Queens of Dormientes gain their sovereignty through stewardship of the citadel and its powers, being decedents of those who have claimed some small scraps of it in the past. They exist, ostensibly, to help others on the same path, yet power is a corrupting thing, and for you to gain yours, tradition dictates that they must give up theirs. It is a situation that will have them be friends and allies until you truly get close to success, and then things will get difficult, still all smiles and ceremonial gestures, yet becoming more murderous or manipulative behind the scenes.

For every key you receive you will be summoned so that honours can be placed upon you. They are honour bound by law and tradition, written by royalty, but required by you both. Refusing such a summons would be a grave crime, and an insult to the royal household, both enough to mark you for arrest or death, for who would refuse the grand gifts of tradition…

objects.title: The First Key
objects.text: Those who receive their first key are rare enough to be summoned to kneel and introduce themselves to the court. Their name will be etched into the grand mural garden of key holders and a small bounty of gold given, along with words of encouragement from a monarch. Other nobles may look to them with interest, ever looking for the capable to serve in their schemes or their household.

objects.title: The Second Key
objects.text: A grand feast is held, for rarer still are those who perform a miracle a second time. Games are held and honours given. Historically, even knighthoods, should the key holder be chivalrous enough to warrant. It is a celebration, and in some unofficial ways, an end, the great many holders of times past choosing this key to retire to a life of luxury, success, and their mark on history.

objects.title: The Third Key
objects.text: And thus the key holder is ushered into the nobility, with noble titles given, lands, people, and responsibilities. These cannot be refused and to neglect them is to let the people of said lands suffer; a cruel gambit meant to either tie you down or sully your reputation. On the other hand, who better to rule over lands on a dangerous frontier than a hero? This also places them under the summons of the ruler.

objects.title: The Forth Key
objects.text: If unmarried, they gain a noble spouse chosen by their sovereign, and greater lands and responsibilities. They are required to sire multiple children, so their noble blood and bountiful talents are not wasted, and spend a minimum time of three years on their lands to rest from their successes. The restless may be gently (or forcefully) placed under house arrest, or slowed with magic and curses. The spouse may be fair or foul, depending on the rules inclination.

objects.title: The Fifth Key
objects.text: The law demands the previous marriage be annulled, the spouse and children banished, for it is royalty that must be married into. The new spouse will be the most suitable available for children and inheritance, from widowed queen to unwed princeling, so that should the last key be claimed, the line of succession will be unbroken. As cruel as it seems, a future monarch must prove they will put the kingdom before their own blood.

objects.title: The Sixth Key
objects.text: By right, power of the kingdom is handed to the claimant of the power of the citadel. The previous noble families properties and holding transfer to the new monarch, themselves inheriting the properties and holding of the next most powerful family, and they the next, and so on, just to make sure all the nobles will suffer from this outcome and will wish to prevent it. Should everyone be unwilling or unable to stop it, the kingdom will be theirs.

rows.title: King or Queen or None
rows.titleText:
A ruler is a ruler and an antagonist is an antagonist, but here and now this is your story and the flavour is yours to choose. Their wants and needs will reflect from your choices here, colouring your inevitable interactions with them. This could leave them an ally longer, or an enemy sooner, and could make their thoughts of you murderous, envious, or lecherous.

You needn’t choose at all of course, but the tossed coin of fate can land quite unfavourably if left unruly.

addons.text: A king who is either unmarried, widowed, a boy, or mistressed to the hilt.
The husband of a queen, bound together in duty and matrimony.
A queen who could be widower, virgin, broken hearted, or a bed hopping whore.
The wife of a king, elegant assured, ruling dutifully at his side.
A council of nobles, a rule of committee. Each competes for the job of a monarch.
The council will try to uphold the traditions of old, but without a monarch to guide them, there will be descent, and more chaos the closer you get to your goal.

rows.title: The King
rows.titleText: What man would be king of a country?

objects.title: A Warrior
objects.text: One who leads from the front with forthright action; a battle leader who can hold his own.

objects.title: A Mage
objects.text: A king who rules with magic manipulation; curse and control and magic enhanced senses are his.

objects.title: A Powerful Man
objects.text: His personal abilities are significantly improved. He may even have a key or two of his own.

objects.title: A Naive Man
objects.text: Through a lack of ability, he doesn’t do as well as he should in politics. His power suffers accordingly.

objects.title: A Good Man
objects.text: Kindness is a power of its own. This is a king who would not be cruel for its own sake.

objects.title: An Evil Man
objects.text: One who finds pleasure in seeing cruelty done. His is a court of fear, where none dare speak out.

objects.title: A Just King
objects.text: A king for whom the law is sacrosanct, even unto himself. Will act as a fair judge to all.

objects.title: A Chaotic King
objects.text: The law applies to all but the king, who acts in his own interests, laying out penalty as he chooses.

objects.title: A Charismatic Man
objects.text: His charm and dignity inspires all to his civility and his cause, with a noble face straight from a bards tale

objects.title: A Disgusting Man
objects.text: Ugly in face and manner, and completely unable to inspire confidence. His is a villainous persona.

objects.title: Young
objects.text: Barely a boy, his lacking years leading to a lacking experience and childish mistakes.

objects.title: Distinguished
objects.text: A seasoned man, wise with years. He knows the business of being a king, its limits, and lack thereof.

objects.title: A Clever Man
objects.text: One who can play the game of power and schemes, outsmarting his opponents at every turn.

addons.text: A Naive Man: Book smart, but still too trusting for politics.

objects.title: A Terrible Statesman
objects.text: Though none would say it to his face, he is a fool who makes terrible decisions.

objects.title: A Lustful Noble
objects.text: A man led by his loins. Wondering eyes match wondering hands, and who he wants, he gets.

objects.title: A Madman
objects.text: Driven insane by knowledge and a curse of visions. No magic can help, but he sees things others don’t.

objects.title: Demon Touched King
objects.text: The royal family has been tainted by the touch of demons. He’ll be less well liked, succumbing to their nature.

objects.title: Undead King
objects.text: A king who has served on the throne for a long time, rarely seen in public. Wise with years and practiced competence.

objects.title: Cursed King
objects.text: The shameful secret of the crown, its wearer tainted by one of the curses. Werewolf or vampire.

objects.title: Corrupted King
objects.text: The demons have not yet marched east, but when they do they will find a ready ally, or a puppet.

objects.title: Obsession
objects.text: From first glance, the king will be obsessed with you. The obsession depends upon his personality, but he will use all his power to satisfy it.

addons.text: Queen: Be careful of her jealousy.
A Naive Man: His fascination is with your tales and bravery, not romantic or sexual.
A Good Man: He will want what is best for you, which usually involves him.
An Evil Man: He will want to hurt you, even if he loves you.
Lustful: He will want to fuck you, love you, and keep you. Once will never be enough.
Madman: He knows what you are and what you have changed, demanding you put things back.

rows.title: The Queen
rows.titleText: What woman would stand above all?

objects.title: A Martial Queen
objects.text: While perhaps unladylike, she has taken to a training of arms, winning duels both on and off the battlefield.

objects.title: A Sorceress
objects.text: Skilled in the mystic arts, from fireballs to mindreading she is a force to be reckoned with.

objects.title: A Powerful Woman
objects.text: Her personal abilities are increased significantly. So much so that she may have a key or two of her own.

objects.title: A Naïve Woman
objects.text: Sheltered and ignorant of the outside world, the queen is less effective throughout her endeavours.

objects.title: A Kind Woman
objects.text: Good to people and animals, the rigors of the dark side of rulership makes her cringe with regret.

objects.title: A Brutal Woman
objects.text: The shortest path is a straight one, and sometimes that line goes across someone’s neck. She loses no sleep from it.

objects.title: A Pious Woman
objects.text: More than merely the religious duties of her station, faith holds a key part of her life. Both its good and its bad.

objects.title: A Licentious Queen
objects.text: Impropriety is one of her drugs of choice. Free of moral restrictions, this queen does whatever and whoever she wants.

objects.title: A Young Queen
objects.text: Barely a girl, she has yet to grow into her station, making the common mistakes of youth.

objects.title: An Experienced Queen
objects.text: Matured like a fine wine, she makes no easy mistakes, playing the games of politics like an old pro.

objects.title: A Manipulative Noble
objects.text: She has the mind to pull peoples strings with ease, all to get whatever she wants. Be careful around her.

objects.title: Blunt Queen
objects.text: She knows what she wants and she’ll say it without embellishment. She has not time for subtlety.

objects.title: Abused Queen
objects.text: Much of her behaviour can be traced back to a past, either one day or many, where something terrible happened.

objects.title: Whore Queen
objects.text: In mentality rather than profession. She likes sex and engages in it often, even if she shouldn’t.

objects.title: A Cracked Mind
objects.text: She is not all there upstairs, being seen as somewhat mad. She can have moments of surprising clarity though.

objects.title: A Broken Mind
objects.text: Everything else selected pushed to the extreme degree. Her madness can be frightening to be around.

objects.title: Celestial Queen
objects.text: A woman of celestial touch, beautiful and heavenly. Whether she acts that way is another matter.

objects.title: Demonic Queen
objects.text: A woman of demonic bloodline, carrying their curse, their strength, and their ill repute.

objects.title: Cursed Queen
objects.text: The royal household, touched by one of the curses. The ill choice of vampire or werewolf.

objects.title: Corrupted Queen
objects.text: In league with demonic forces, willingly or not. When they march east they will find kneeling royalty.

objects.title: Obsession
objects.text: From first glance, the queen will be obsessed with you. The obsession depends upon her personality, but her pursuit of you is non-negotiable.

addons.text: King: A jealous husband can be a dangerous thing.
A Naïve Woman: Her fascination is with your valour and heroism, not in a sexual sense.
A Pious Woman: Your adherence to her faith will keep her up at night.
A Brutal Woman: Tide to a bed or a torturers table, you WILL give her what she wants.
Lustful: She will want you to fuck her, hard and often. Her interest is purely sexual, though more unquenchable than her usual.
Cracked: She knows what you are and what you have changed, demanding you put things back.
Broken: From the moment you meet she will gather what forces she can to ensure you never leave her sight. Obsession becomes a truly deranged single-mindedness.

rows.title: The Quirks of Royalty
rows.titleText: The royal faction, regardless of its head, will have ways of doing things that go beyond the leader, extending inexorably, to you. Their household may interfere more fiercely, or be a circus of incompetence, undercutting their institution.

objects.title: Large Spy Network
objects.text: Whispering into their ears are the goings on of the whole kingdom. Do not expect to catch them by surprise, nor escape their notice.

objects.title: Manipulative Advisors
objects.text: Pulled to and fro by special interests and greedy individuals, their plans can be more refined, even while the target on you is pulled in other directions.

objects.title: Martial Training
objects.text: Royalty comes with a martial culture, and each member of the family is trained self-defence, and self-offence.

objects.title: Treacherous Court
objects.text: The closer to royalty, the more dangerous the game becomes. Opportunity, but also, your monarch is smart enough (or lucky enough) to have survived despite it.

objects.title: The Love of the People
objects.text: Because of, or despite, their actions, the people of the city and the country love the royals. They will be far more willing to act with them, even against you.

objects.title: Pomp and Ceremony
objects.text: All nobles have it, yet for the royals it is pushed to the maximum. Breaking decorum and procedure is more serious around them, but they are constrained as well.

objects.title: Powerful Subordinates
objects.text: More than just the best royal knights, their retinues contain a plethora of ex-adventurers, assassins, magi, and other dangerously competent individuals.

objects.title: Devoted Household
objects.text: From knights to maids, the household of the royal family will be loyal to the end. Perhaps it’s magic or faith or love, the result is the same.

objects.title: Extended Family
objects.text: An array of sons, daughters, cousins, brothers, sisters etc. all now in the scene. They’ll make up some trusted (and no so trusted) nobility, and could be allies or enemies.

objects.title: Adoptive Family
objects.text: From young wards and hostages to valiant heroes written into the bloodline, there will be more members of the royal ‘family’ to deal with, perhaps including you one day.

addons.text: The court is busier than ever, but friction and scandal arise more often

objects.title: Protected Vulnerabilities
objects.text: The people (and objects) the royals care about are kept both secret and protected, leaving fewer vulnerabilities that can be exploited.

objects.title: Golem Guard
objects.text: They have on their staff some of golems of the central citadel, or close to it, cementing their base of power with unshakable unthinking loyalty.

objects.title: Undead Court
objects.text: From knights to servants to family, undead strength and resilience flows through all or many, leaving them a force to be reckoned with.

objects.title: Cursed Court
objects.text: No longer alone, the royal leader has turned or been turned by their knights, servants, and even family members to the same curse.

objects.title: Blessed Court
objects.text: The royal household has long been blessed by the outer realms. Spirits, good fortune, and friends in very high places make them a challenge to overcome.

addons.text: Corrupted King: Surrounded by the holy, the kings corruption (willing or unwilling) must be kept the strictest secret.
Corrupted Queen: Surrounded by the holy, the queens corruption (willing or unwilling) must be kept the strictest secret.
Corrupted King & Queen: The royals have both been corrupted, meaning their holy court is soon to follow. Perhaps there is time to prevent it?

objects.title: Corrupted Court
objects.text: The demonic taint has spread, through force or guile, to the whole household of the royal family. No longer will they have to hide their allegiances behind closed doors.

rows.title: The King and Queen
rows.titleText: A royal couple who rule together, in love, in venture, or at each other’s throats.

objects.title: Royal Unity
objects.text: The king and queen are a team, who’s combined efforts are far more effective than the sum of their parts. They share everything with each other.

objects.title: Dysfunctional Marriage
objects.text: They are a marriage of politics or convenience, not love. Abuse, lies, twisted manipulation; they spend their time plotting against each other.

objects.title: Sexual Dynamic
objects.text: They spend much time together in the bedroom, locked in coitus. Children are inevitable, if not already present.

addons.text: Dysfunctional: Despite it all, they still make love regularly. Mutual hate-fucking, or something more one sided.
Obsession: They will imagine you in place of their partner, which may promote jealousy or sexual curiosity from their spouse.
Shared Obsession: They will role-play situations involving you, desiring to share you together in the same bed.

objects.title: Power Couple
objects.text: The powers of the king and queen compliment each other: two halves of a VERY powerful whole.

addons.text: Dysfunctional: The halves become counterbalances that jar as badly as their motives. This keeps them in place.

objects.title: Focused Insanity
objects.text: The madness of one is focused by the other, its truth distilled to a useful concoction. One to see. The other to act. Little is left to escape their reach, no matter the distance, plan, or time.

addons.text: Both Insane: It is left up to their household to interpret and act on their ramblings. They are unlikely to do so.

rows.title: The Nobility
rows.titleText:
More than a king or queen, rulership often lands upon the landed noble. It is the noble who decides how the laws are enforced upon their lands. Nobles who push and pull upon the whims of royalty for their own ends. Nobles that spy and bicker and undermine, or act as stalwart defenders of their lessers. The royals may be the head by which the ship steers, but the noble court is the wind, and may be as changeable. 

While key or infamy are required to gain audience with a king, only competence and need are needed for a noble. If you are willing to play pawn in their games, coin and influence may become yours, or even sponsorship, your quest for the keys bringing reflected glory upon the noble at your back.

Their games may bring you in conflict with the royal faction, or other nobles, leaving their lands dangerous places for you to tread. Dealing with them will be a choice that causes complications, but avoiding their influence entirely is no choice at all.

objects.title: Noble Nobility
objects.text: Many of their number live up to the name, operating on rules of chivalry and honour. They look to the wellbeing of their people first and foremost.

objects.title: Brutal Methods
objects.text: When they strike, they strike without honour; no person or deed is off the table in terms of revenge or examples, and often, the cruelty is the point.

objects.title: Hedonistic Impulses
objects.text: Self-indulgent corruption festers in their circles as they eschew their duties of state to pursue feasts and orgies and the satiation of their wild appetites.

addons.text: Brutal Methods: Any common man or women that takes their fancy are included, whether they want to be or not. The nobles pleasure is more often tied to other people’s pain.

objects.title: Strange Behaviour
objects.text: Isolated from normality, the nobility have become nonsensical. Strange styles and habits will make them difficult and uncomfortable to deal with.

addons.text: Hedonistic Nobles: They are consumed by unusual fetishes that they incorporate in their lives. Things most find strange or even repulsive. If you have such a fetish, there will be some noble to share it with.

objects.title: Martial Expectations
objects.text: A noble is expected to lead their armies and fight beside them. Duels and military conflicts between them are more common, but many become more dangerous and capable individuals.

addons.text: Noble Nobility: They will be defenders of the realm, leaving many of the minor threats taken care of, and local forces better able to help when the going gets tough.

objects.title: Magically Trained
objects.text: The study of magic is a common practice of the elite, for daily life, combat, and intrigue. While a point of pride, their actual skill varies wildly.

addons.text: Martial Expectations: Their magic focuses more on combat arts and the path of the battle mage.

objects.title: Powerful Magic
objects.text: A Magocracy, all members of which have powerful enough magic to hold their own. They will make strong allies, or deadly enemies.

objects.title: Fighting Boredom
objects.text: Their games go beyond vying for power. Competitions between nobles become quietly official, some strange and some mundane, some with champions and some with themselves.

addons.text: Brutal Methods: The games can be quite horrific, even fatal, as the bloodier games gain the biggest interest. Naturally, these roles are often filled unwillingly by the common folk.
Hedonistic Impulses: The games will often be sexual in nature, and highly so, taking place in masked dens of pleasure and pain.
Brutality & Hedonism: A dangerous combination. Rape a sexual suffering becomes the entertainment of the nobility, where captured monsters and imprisoned peasants make a screaming pair.

objects.title: Noble Cooperation
objects.text: For all they may vie for power, they are more friends than enemies, understanding that destabilising one destabilises them all. More trust, cooperation, and far fewer knives in the night.

addons.text: Fighting Boredom: Their games, while still exclusive events, become Olympic in their grandeur and audience.

objects.title: Cut-Throat Politics
objects.text: A chosen henchman dying in the night with a dagger in their back is simply par for the course among the games they play. Their politics are vicious enough to fell even a monster slaying hero.

objects.title: Loyalty
objects.text: Despite the differences between nobles, their loyalty to their royal head is never questioned. Through tradition, fear, or genuine respect, they will answer their monarchs call, always.

objects.title: Apathy
objects.text: They do not openly defy their monarchs, but they are slow to answer, dragging their heels or questioning decisions. Perhaps you could coax them into further defiance.

objects.title: Incestuous Bloodlines
objects.text: Using magic to keep impurities out, births are often kept blood to blood, some using distant cousins, others much closer relations, and education of sex is a family matter.

objects.title: Undead Nobility
objects.text: Immortality is the pursuit of the rich, and with enough coin, anything is possible. Many have ruled their domains for generations of the living.

objects.title: Cursed Nobility
objects.text: To stand at the top is to face the malice of all below. Curses were inevitable, and for those who perpetuate them, what better targets?

addons.text: In Control: The Dormientes nobility will be the posterchild of vampiric corruption; an open secret known to all.

objects.title: Corrupted Nobles
objects.text: The forces of hell have corrupted or bribed the leadership of Dormientes, leaving the demon inclined making the decisions and leading the armies. A disastrous state should the demons move east.

objects.title: Close The Ruler
objects.text: Return to the choices of Dormientes.

rows.title: Strength of Rule
rows.titleText:
Whenever anyone declares their rule, one must ask how closely the ruled listen. Would the very moats of dust march to their will? Or perhaps even the bases commoner would spit at their feet? Power does not mean competence, competence does not mean an effective chain of command, and doing everything right does not mean that everything won’t go wrong anyway.

So how meekly do the citizens follow? How strong is the rule of the law?

If you do not choose it will be as the ruler demands, melding more closely to the reflection of their personality.

objects.title: Strong
objects.text: The law grips the throats of all who walk within the kingdom of Dormientes. Checkpoints are kept, the roads patrolled, criminality caught and stamped into the dust. A place where freedoms were exchanged for order. It is not necessarily a place of tyranny and can achieve greater feats in government projects, but neither is it a thing well enjoyed by all.

objects.title: Medium
objects.text: The rule of an even hand. Unlike selecting nothing here, this option smooths out the edges so that even the most tyrannical of rulers, both mad and evil, will adopt a live and let live approach to the common folk. This results in self-governance, with threat or guidance from above keeping the power hungry in line. In essence, moderate rule, even if ruled by the unmoderate.

objects.title: Weak
objects.text: The rule of law is lessened, its enforcers corrupt, its criminals more organised. This can mean more ways of getting things done and more paths to travel unseen, but the living cost is a predatory society where those unbound by morality cannot be bound by law, leaving misery in their wake. The law still exists, but as an undermined tool, it seems to only hurt the innocent.

objects.title: Absent
objects.text: There is scarcely a government at all. The capital perhaps, and a few surrounding territories, but anarchy reigns in all the lands between, and where order should be kept, the hands that keep it are too weak to keep violence from spilling out uncontested. Criminal gangs offer more stability, yet their tribalism with each other brings only more conflict.

addons.text: The rulers and nobility previously chosen are still present, but only around the capital and are more akin to the strongest faction leaders than sovereigns. They can still make your life difficult.

objects.title: Fractured
objects.text: Dormientes is still the centre, but the once vast country is now many different city states, vying and warring and forming shifting alliances. This means more opportunity to join the fray, nobles houses needing fighters more than ever, but it also leaves lines of contention and conflict, with tragedies sown and lives ruined wherever the lines on the latest maps meet.

addons.text: Strong: There are three great and powerful countries, locked in a war of stalemate. Most of the time it is a thing of knives and quiet sabotage, but when battle lines are drawn they stretch from horizon to horizon.

Medium: The actual citizens of each nation do not get involved in ‘the nobles business’, and are actually on good terms with each other. When war comes the people are neither targeted nor drafted, their leaders all fearing a rebellion more unified than their own mercenaries.

Weak: Like shattered glass, dozens and dozens of fiefdoms, some big and some small, war and trade with each other. The battles are smaller and the corruption more varied between locations: while some may be led by pious leaders, others will be little more than glorified crime lords.

objects.title: Distracted
objects.text: The country is in the midst of a crisis that is currently taking up much of the attentions of the ruling and working class. Wars, plagues, and disasters have a way of putting aside the usual habits. This opens up a new section, where the nature of the crisis can be chosen.

addons.text: Strong: The disasters will be greater, to match the added competence of a robust and unified government. Still solvable, in time.
Medium: The people are mostly working together to resolve the crisis, leaving their ‘leaders’ able to focus more on their own business.

Weak: The crisis will be of the lesser kind, where a competent government could mop it up quite easily, yet order has slipped so much into incompetence and self-interest that said crisis has grown worse than it ever needed to be.
Absent: This crisis likely caused the fracturing absence of a government destroyed by its magnitude, yet that means the damage is mostly done, with only the fear and fixing remaining.
Reincarnation: The distraction will begin when your 5 year plot armour wears off, so be careful.

rows.title: Types of Strength
rows.titleText:
The rule of law and the grip of the government is strong and self-assured, but such strength can come in different flavours, some more and some less oppressive. What kind of muscle backs this strength?

If you do not choose, it will simply be a strong and authoritarian government with no special qualities.

objects.title: Utopian Mandate
objects.text: Somehow, perhaps by literal divine intervention, they’ve cracked the code that all others have failed at, creating a strong and unified society through balanced order and culture. People obey the laws because they see their worth and agree perfectly with them, never even thinking to stand against them. This can be quite messed up depending on the actual laws chosen later on.

objects.title: Imposed Order
objects.text: Those in control are of different blood to those controlled. This is an order imposed by an external conqueror, either through strength of arms or skill of subversion, leaving a puppet on the throne and resentment in people’s hearts. Done by one of the six point nations, or perhaps creatures from more distant realms, either way, decent is not tolerated.

objects.title: Forced Unity
objects.text: The nations strength will have communistic overtones, giving housing and food, but rarely enough to keep warm or healthy. Expect everyone to have the same clothes, homes, and preferences, whether they like it or not, as the government foolishly strives for unity though uniformity. The nobility will become the apparatchik, whose supposedly even share is significantly greater.

objects.title: Reduced Cognition
objects.text: The populous is being kept sedated. Something in the water. Magic in the air. A culture of booze and drugs. Infiltrated dreams. People forget, growing confused and helplessly controlled. People won’t notice how bad it’s gotten, and an addict won’t care to know, as long as they can get their fix. This will somewhat affect you, though you can notice and fight against it.

rows.title: Types of Weakness
rows.titleText:
The limp wristed grip of the government is weak and flawed, rife with crime and feeble with justice, but such a sorry state can come in different flavours, each a history of a slippery slope and a tragedy of errors. What kind of ineptitude infects this nation?

If you do not choose, it will simply be a corrupt and incompetent government with no special qualities.

objects.title: Family Clans
objects.text: Blood is key, with family ties seen as the strongest rule to abide. Nepotism is expected, marriage for power a given. The outsider is shunned and distrusted and acts of incest are more commonly accepted from anyone with land to inherit. The families can be vast, their influences many, and their actions should always benefit the family over anyone outside of it.

objects.title: Subverted
objects.text: The government is not inherently weak or corrupt, but is in fact a victim of external forces, weakened and undermined at every turn. This may be from another nation, forces of the deep below, or even demons encroaching from the west. Rooted deeply, they keep Dormientes frail and ripe for invasion, stymying any effort to fix itself.

objects.title: Libertarian
objects.text: The business of selfishness takes the lead as unregulated capitalism supplants or undermines the rule of law, leaving monopolising merchants providing every basic service at an exorbitant cost and poor functionality. The rat race grips the nation, everyone kept too busy clawing their way to the top to notice they’re all stuck at the bottom.

objects.title: Fanatical Fascism
objects.text: The society is all a theatre of competence. The strong military parades daily, and everyone must know and recognise the countries strength and the enemy’s dangerous corrupting weakness. It’s a façade, masking ineptitude and cowardice with violence. Their grip will feel strong if you stand against them alone, or are one of the many out groups targeted for hatred.

rows.title: Types of Absence
rows.titleText:
Much of the country is empty of rule, but why? What caused or contributed to the end, or stopped its beginning, and what can be found in the empty space left over?
 
If you do not choose, it will simply be a place mostly bereft of the touch of law, its wilderness wilder and its societies more chaotic.

objects.title: Calm
objects.text: The more stable of the unstable. While no overall government control remains outside of the central city, small groups, like villages and communes, manage to self-govern, creating uncountable proto city states and clans that war when they need to. People live together and fight together, making their own rules, but otherwise the anarchy is kept low.

objects.title: Ruined
objects.text: Absence of order brings decay in time, but here there is only devastation. From war or disaster, or even your arrival, all that once was of the country is no more, left to the stumps of ruin. Bandits are many, but so are the voices calling for a push to reclaim the broken lands and bring order back to them. Fresh chance for the city builder.

objects.title: Contained
objects.text: The laws and societies mostly remain, but trapped in small high-walled cities and fortresses, the land outside keeping them in with its dangers. This keeps the most law and the most civilisation, but leaves the land a dangerous wild, beset by beasts, bandits, and perilous nature of all kinds. Isolated people get by as best they can.

objects.title: Wild
objects.text: The land around the citadel proves harder to tame, leaving the remnants of those who have tried. The cities and laws are rustic and wild, and the remnants of many shattered tribes rejecting of civilisation are scattered about the lands. Now that you’re here, perhaps this savage innocence can be tamed, or nurtured, or swept away in the fires of a new order.

rows.title: Distracting Disaster
rows.titleText:
What will be the nature of their calamity? Whether many have died already, or the mayhem has just begun, the country, its people, and its rule will likely survive in the long term. Scarred perhaps, and certainly traumatised, but it will survive.

One event will be a disaster on everyone’s lips, keeping the focus of those in charge until the situation is resolved. Two will be the height of misfortune, cancelling each other out or working in a disastrous union. Three will be the kind of concert that sees countries collapse, and should some madness compel you to push things that way, perhaps it can. Four and it will be a time of madness and exodus, where fatigue is high and hope is thin, and a solution to all the issues seems an impossibility, while more will be seen as apocalyptic, and will truly lead to the end without your intervention. Be careful of this and remember, the Soporatus Cult is based here; their destruction will crush any hope of reaching Dormientes centre.

objects.title: Natural Disaster
objects.text: A great earthquake or storm, drought or flood, magic surge or monster migration, or some other destructive eruption has come and swept a path throughout the kingdom. Food and resources are scarce and the dead lie in the open.  Most think things will get worse before they get better.

addons.text: Sea: The disaster will be a tsunami, sending waves big enough to sweep across many islands and cause untold destruction.

objects.title: Plague
objects.text: Disease sweeps the lands and its people, either magic resistant in nature, or faster and more deadly than healing magic can contend. It sweeps through communities, leaving only those with natural or hard won immunities. Be careful you don’t succumb as well.

objects.title: Spell Backfire
objects.text: Some spell has brought about a miserable twisting of nature. Spirits rise in rebellion, rivers run with undiscovered colours, and storms lift stones into the sky and leave them there. This can be fixed, with either time or a proper untangling of the magic, but the effects need to be worked around.

objects.title: Power Struggle
objects.text: The least destructive distraction, property wise. The old king is dead, and while the rulers you have chosen will win the race eventually, they are not there yet. Others contend for the throne, from rival houses, distant relations, and bellicose nobles, the royal world will see heads rolling before it’s done.

objects.title: Rebellion
objects.text: A faction of home grown unrest, or a manipulation of external cause, many people now rise up against the rule of law. It is doomed to fail as less than a third of the country is on board, but revolution can be a very ugly thing, and the reasons will smoulder long after it’s done.

objects.title: Undead Uprising
objects.text: Some event, from a terrible godly curse to the rise of some mad necromancer, has left a glut of undead upon the land, roaming and lingering, leaving roads dangerous and villages barricaded. A call for holy orders has been sent, and a war enacted upon the hordes of the restless.

addons.text: Terrifying Undead: Understandably, a lot more of peoples attentions are on this, and more religious orders have been called in to resolve it.
Organised Undead: Several cities, including the capital, have been sieged by the more organised waves of the dead. It is more a war than a plague.

Terrifying and Organised Undead: Religious zealots flood into the country, and extreme prejudice should burn the land free of undead in time. If you get in their way, their failure could bring about an apocalypse. Everyone operates under the same terrified cooperation; if you do not follow the rule of law, your life may be forfeit.

objects.title: Demon Invasion
objects.text: The Demons of the west have made inroads into Dormientes, bringing death and destruction, and dragging all they find into their sick world of horrific indulgences. The outer cities have fallen, and many inner cities have been gutted, their people marched into enslavement.

addons.text: Demon Prevalence: Not just from the west, but from within: many seemingly meek, magically controlled servants have broken free and are sowing chaos within cities and societies.

Breeding Evil: More of a raid for captives to be taken back west than an invasion proper. See that you and yours are not caught, and note that this will have some tragic effects for at least the next generation.

Corrupted Nobles: The head of the armies and the defenders of the people offer no resistance, causing more devastation and less distraction from your antics. They may even sabotage you if you work against the demons.

objects.title: Powerful Persons
objects.text: It takes a lot of power for a single individual to capture the attention of a nation, but these people can be living wrecking balls to the establishment. Besting them would earn you adulation. Helping them means joining the wanted posters. There are only about five, but their presence can be felt.

addons.text: Civilised Beasts: The new ruler of beasts is taking a dislike to the rules of the ‘civilised’ nation. Herds are being mustered and crude axes sharpened as this trouble maker seems compelled to start a war of beastly proportions.

They Walk Among Us: The individual is rumoured to be of the divine realm: a trickster, an adventurer, a person for whom rules mean nothing. They’re searching for someone who seeks the power, whose very arrival has reshaped the world.

Firmly Rooted: The head of a cult who has ascended from the deep rivers to spread the glorious word of a new and terrible faith. This being of dubious origins has the backing of some very powerful benefactors.

Spell Backfire: Some madman is doing this on purpose, wondering the land and bringing calamity in their wake. Perhaps they cannot control it and perhaps their death would not fix it, but something must be done.

Power Struggle: The one behind the assassination perhaps? Now someone quite powerful will also be in the running for the throne, and they will not give up, even if the matter is settled by everyone else.

Rebellion: The leader of the rebellion, charismatic, powerful, and slippery. As long as they remain, the rebellion will always return, more desperate and bitter, and you’ll be either with them or against them in their eyes.

Undead Uprising: The necromancer responsible is at its head, raising more and more and is intent to lay siege to Dormientes in a bid to claim its power. Even without the army, this lich and their minions will be hard to deal with.
Demon Invasion: A powerful demon lord is setting up shop, looking to turn a large chunk of the country into their personal playground. It would take a crusade or a miracle to see them banished.

objects.title: War With Highmarch
objects.text: There is a war with the northern lands. Either dwarves or the human kingdoms there range across the boarder, seeking territory, or vengeance for some perceived slight. Their conquest is not so destructive and unlikely to take the central region, but it is distracting.

objects.title: War With Nellacomb
objects.text: The sultans of the southern desert see weakness in the north, raiding the towns and villages of Dormientes hotter climates. The coalition that has formed is weak and divided, attacking without unified direction, but it is frustratingly varied and unpredictable, focused on loot over territory.

objects.title: War With Melliomer
objects.text: The elven nations of the eastern forests encroach with their woodland, part of a plan that spans generations of the shorter lived races. This latest slight must be answered, but the elves do not advance unless their footing is sure, and uprooting them will be quite the challenge.

objects.title: War With Eardheart
objects.text: Looking to take the great wall created by Dormientes to keep the demons at bay, the warriors of Eardheart battle to take a strategic resource for their own war machine. Conflict with their lethargic neighbour’s armies is a small price to pay to control their eastern flank.

addons.text: Demon Invasion: Perhaps they are the cause, driving their enemy into their lazy ally’s territory, so they might chase them and ‘secure’ territory from the demons. A bold plan that may result in a three way fight.

objects.title: Total War
objects.text: Rather than invasions from all, the rule of Dormientes has been swept up in an atmosphere of total war, invading its neighbours without a clear plan. While gaining easy territory through early surprise, they’ll be doomed to the crippling counter attacks deserved by all overreaching warmongers.

addons.text: This puts Dormientes on borrowed time, an alliance certain to conquer and defang the country eventually. As the cult has ties to the state, they may give you quests that contribute to the war effort, and may be crushed and scattered in the end as a result. Join the war and lead it to victory, or join the allies and barter for the cults life. Either way, you can’t sit this one out.

objects.title: Just Started
objects.text: The time of crisis is just beginning at the time of your arrival. War horns are blaring. The animals are giving their warnings. Chaos will begin as you arrive: an inauspicious omen, if anyone has the mind to notice one new face. At least with this, you will not be the only one lost and confused.

addons.text: Reincarnation: Only the rumblings of the disasters chosen begin when you are born. They are instead spread out over many years, likely reaching far into your adulthood if unattended to. They are far lesser in magnitude day to day, but the trade-off is their longevity, with every day of decades feeling like it’s only just begun.

objects.title: Just Ending
objects.text: You arrive as the time of crisis comes to a close. Wars are winding up, rubble swept away. There is much work to be done as tired people begin to put their lives together, and the rule of law is weakened by the dead, but such dark days are not to last.

addons.text: Reincarnation: Rather than waiting until your plot armour ends, it will instead begin when you arrive, meaning the time of disasters will be winding down when your story starts to begin.
Total War: The cult and kingdom survive, but only just. Their revival will be very slow, and you many not even begin your quest for the keys for many years while they recover.

rows.title: The Resulting Rule
rows.titleText: How a county is governed is not the sole arbiter of what happens within it. Laws build up over time, each a brick in the wall that would collapse with its removal, and situations that grow and change, writhing and slippery to all who would attempt to control them. Small things, in the grand scheme, yet each could define or destroy many lives.

objects.title: Criminal Magic
objects.text: Those not born of nobility are restricted from learning any form of magic, no matter their talent. Foreign magic users must be registered through a difficult process, or agree to wear limiters that cripple their magic. Those who flout the rules are beset by terrible punishments.

addons.text: Reduced cost of spells in the spell section, but the more you have, the more hated you’ll be.
Spell Backfire: This is a recent rule after the incident and magic users are being rounded up and persecuted more actively when you arrive.

objects.title: Secret Police
objects.text: The law is kept by both public authority, and private, with a state organisation that hunts down troublemakers, or suspected troublemakers, or potential troublemakers, dealing with them with extrajudicial cruelty. They are feared, and rightly so.

objects.title: Golem Guards
objects.text: Specialised golems are used to maintain the law. They are not every guard, but they do bolster their forces, helping them to stand against all but the most powerful individuals. These give the state a strong, if insensitive, hand, helping to deal with it less cooperative problems.

objects.title: Gladiators
objects.text: The honourable profession of murder for sport is alive and well, with large colosseums dedicated to the entertainment of the masses. Crimes committed for the purposes of entertainment are accepted, and even criminals may be forced to compete. A chance for you to earn coin perhaps?

objects.title: Criminal Free Use
objects.text: Legally, those convicted of a crime may be subject to sexual degradation in a public theatre. From simple nudity and humiliation, to being forced to provide sexual services to the public, the felon both pays for their crime and gives back to the people they have wronged.

addons.text: Male Supremacy: Naturally, only women are subjected to this, though men convicted of truly terrible crimes may be ‘tried as a woman’.
Female Supremacy: Naturally, only men are subjected to this, though women convicted of truly terrible crimes may be ‘tried as a man’.

Sexual Repression: The punishment is reserved for the truly heinous as it’s seen as the ultimate degradation. It is also carried out behind closed doors, even where the public is concerned, with masks or a dividing wall keeping the public anonymous.

objects.title: Free Use
objects.text: To the strong go the spoils. There is a lawful understanding that those who are in charge may use those lesser than themselves as they see fit, with the lesser party needing to submit themselves at request of the more dominant.

addons.text: Male Supremacy: All women must submit themselves sexually to any man who asks. If they are with a man who is considered their owner or guardian, said owner may refuse this request.
Female Supremacy: All men must submit themselves sexually to any woman who asks. If they are unable to perform the services requested, this may be considered a criminal offence.

Absent: The understanding is that if one is strong enough to take another person sexually then they may do so freely, regardless of sex, position, or any other factors. The used, if without strong friends, is on their own.

objects.title: Criminal Factions
objects.text: The kingdom has a significant organised crime problem, with gangs that have far more power than they should. They will be a path to getting many things deemed illegal, be it knowledge, power, or pleasure, but they will also be a dangerous force to cross, and a cancer on the common man.

addons.text: Weak: While already beset by crime for its weakness, it will now be utterly overrun, becoming essentially a mafia state. When different criminal factions come into conflict, whole armies and mercenaries may be involved.

objects.title: Bandit Clans
objects.text: The countryside is rife with bandits, who make a living ambushing travellers of all kinds. They have become their own subculture, fighting for territory, and live in their own villages and fortresses, where no rules but their own apply.

addons.text: Sea: Rather than roadside ambushes, this will be organised flotillas of pirates and other seafaring ne'er-do-well.

Weak or Absent: Having little control already of the countries wild places, this dials it up significantly. It’s not unheard of for these clans to siege and sack cities, with even Dormientes itself falling to these wild barbarians.

objects.title: Assassins Guilds
objects.text: Either in spite of the law, or with its blessing, guilds of assassins operate in the country. They can be hired to do dark deeds for coin, taking out prominent figures from the shadows. Mostly used by royals and nobles against upstarts who would threaten their power. Can be joined, if you have talent.

addons.text: They will come after you eventually, if you seek the powers. It’s recommended you have counters for poison, as well as short and long ranged attacks.
Criminal Factions: Assassins are used extensively in the power plays of criminal leaders.

objects.title: Bounty Hunters
objects.text: The task of hunting down criminals is given to the private sector. From lone freelancers to organised guilds, those who are wanted must run from those hungry for coin, who are far more relentless than guards who’re paid either way. An opportunity for a profession though?

addons.text: Criminal Factions: Hunters work carefully around those with power, and closely, picking off those who have fallen out of favour.

objects.title: Religious Rule
objects.text: The Soporatus Cult rules the people openly, the rulers selected mere figureheads attending to the nobility and the lands. Laws will be based on religious requirements, and so will the punishments, justification for all stemming from faith. They will seek to exercise their authority wherever possible.

objects.title: Lawless Soldiers
objects.text: The rule of law understands that for soldiers, the law must be suspended for them to do their duty. When mustered, the soldiers have free reign to pillage for supplies, kidnap for entertainment, torture and execute prisoners, and commit acts others may deem cruel and unusual to win.

addons.text: Honourable Actions: While many will hold to their honour, many will not, resulting in a distinct hatred of the army by the people.

objects.title: Witches
objects.text: Cabals of witches and other occultists infect the land, either sacrificing people to their patrons or using them in other dark and self-serving rituals, or as village healers and spiritualists. The small and hidden wars between practitioners is a thing no law can seem to touch.

addons.text: Criminal Magic: All the magic users of the land are driven into these hidden covens, their protections, and their requirements. Their feared natures increase with their numbers, and their conflicts become problematic for all.

objects.title: Uncontrolled Beastman
objects.text: The country has lost some ground to the beast men, who have dug in and begun raiding the races they see as weaker. Soldiers, guards, hunters, and adventures all have failed in getting rid of them, and each attempt has increased tensions.

addons.text: Many Beasts: They have taken significant swaths of land, turning them into no-go zones for the civilised races. Their raids have often needed mobilised armies to successfully turn away.

Civilised Beasts: Treating with the leaders, offering gifts, and a policy of appeasement has led to a blind eye being given to the growing threat. You may even face trouble from civilised people if you fight them as they do not wish to provoke them, even if they provoke you first.

objects.title: Orc Problem
objects.text: The country is best by orcs who hold the rules in little regard, raiding, raping, and sowing chaos where they may. This particular tribe has been a long-time foe of Dormientes, evading all attempts to quash them, though they are viewed as little more than savage bandits by their betters.

addons.text: Your Race: These guys give you a bad name.

More Accepted Orcs: There is still an ort tribe causing issues and disobeying rules, but they are more akin to gypsies that cause issues with the settlements nearby. You may be left making both friends and enemies though when either side asks for help against the other.

objects.title: Goblin Infestation
objects.text: Keeping their numbers down is a task that has been neglected, and the result is a country whose caves, dens, and abandoned places are all overrun by the prolific breeders. Many quests and bounties will be for their removal, or for the rescue of kidnapped wives and daughters.

addons.text: Evil Goblins: This is a truly miserable state of affairs for the people outside the cities, who live in a state of constant fear. Still, it also means a champion who might free the land would be lauded all the more.

Green Tide: As overrun as the rest of the world may feel at times, Dormientes lax policy leaves it as a true epicentre of the plague, with more goblins than people. It is the primary failing for the current rule

Evil Goblins & Green Tide: The true home of evil, the country will be known most for its goblins, their infection worse than any other nation of the world. High walls will be about all settlements, and only the brave and the foolish will set foot outside of them.

objects.title: Enslavement
objects.text: The rule of law allows or even encourages slavery to exist in some form. This opens up a new section where the specifics can be decided.

addons.text: Troublemakers: Whatever the laws say, slave rebellions and freedom movements are a continual chaos within the kingdom.
Temperate Sensibilities: As much as it may be accepted, there is a dislike for the practice.

rows.title: The Rules of Slavery
rows.titleText:
In the country closest to the summit of power, what pit of powerlessness should there be? What contrast would sting the eye more than the depths of enslavement: to not even own one’s own self?

But this is no world of advanced mentalities. Someone somewhere is getting enslaved, be it in the centre of power where you will walk, or a savage country far away. Perhaps by adding a touch of nightmare to the place, you could gain the power to correct it? Or perhaps you wish to stand above everyone else a little sooner? Either way, the price is the ever stalking chance to be exploited by it, and of course the suffering of others. But that’s not really a price for you to pay, now is it?

objects.title: Enchanted Weakening
objects.text: The enslaved can be fitted with collars or cuffs: binds that strip the individual of strength, both physical and magical. A punch thrown carried the impact of a child, and a spell cast, if castable at all, fizzles to sparks or subtler signs. The strength of this enchantment, and the specific detriments, can be set by the owner.

addons.text: Reincarnation or Child: Should you be born or raised a slave, such methods are not necessary until you grow too strong for comfort.
This would have the effect of stripping you of many boons, should someone slip a collar on you.

objects.title: Magical Control
objects.text: Another potency carried in bindings of a magical nature. They now control the mind, with many options on how they do so for those who use them. The more expensive can shunt thoughts about, confusing, or providing pleasurable incentives, while the cheaper merely give shocks of pain at a word or a gesture.

addons.text: Reincarnation or Child: Should you begin life as a slave, mind control is not used unless you begin rebel or lose trust.

The mental changes are not permanent, at least magically: when the collar is removed, the fog lifts, altered memories correct themselves, artificial ticks are undone, and incentives are lost. All memories remain, however, even the scarring ones, and habits learned can be hard to break.

objects.title: Only Women
objects.text: Only women may be subject to enslavement, their nature seen as demanding a firm correcting leash from time to time; otherwise, some stray from their purpose without a man in their lives to guide them. Ill-suited to hard labour, but seen as a symbol of status, and preferable in some respects to marriage and its burdens.

addons.text: Male Domination: Now, the distinction between women and slaves can only be seen outside of the kingdom. Within, all women are as communal as coin, bought and shared and used, horded by the wealthy and thrown to the poor by the generous.

Female: People are used to seeing women as slaves and things to use, and enslavement of women, including you, will be seen as a potential solution to any grievances had. This reduces respect, and increases danger for you.

Female and Male Domination: You will be enslaved by the first man who realises you are free, or at least an attempt made, and you will be viewed as a slave by default by all the men of the central kingdom. This massively drops respect there, making Dormientes a very dangerous and oppressive place for you. Disguises may work, and the cult will still work with you on your quest for the keys, albeit with thunderous condescension.

objects.title: Only Men
objects.text: Men are the gender most in need of chains and taming, and most suited to the physical labour of beasts, and so they are given both when falling astray. Be they used for brutal labour, protection, or breeding studs, the buying and selling of strong flesh among the female elite is a well-regarded pastime for the sophisticated.

addons.text: Female Domination: All men are slaves, as is right, their last scant freedoms stripped away and torn to pieces. No man may enter the country without chains, and the markets are filled with fine young men, bought and sold between their mistresses like prize winning animals.

Male: People are used to seeing men as slaves here, and enslavement of men, including you, will be seen as a potential solution to any grievances had. This reduces respect, and increases danger for you.

Male and Female Domination: You will be enslaved by the first person who realises you are free, or at least an attempt made, and you will be viewed as a slave by default by all the women of the central kingdom. This massively drops respect there, making Dormientes a very dangerous and oppressive place for you. Disguises may work, depending on your build, and the cult will still work with you on your quest for the keys, albeit with fear and suspicion.

objects.title: No Typical Slavery
objects.text: Having made the overall choice of allowing slavery (both by their law and by your prior selection), a marketplace that allows the legal buying and selling people is born. Selecting this, however, prevents such open commerce, and should be combined with another type of slavery chosen here to take its place.

addons.text: Not Light, Honourable, Criminal, or Illegal Slaveries: Slavery is legally allowed, but not technically practiced in any form. This results in some horrific yet legal workplace abuses instead.

objects.title: Light Slavery
objects.text: Slavery needn’t be all chains and whips. It is a social contract, often entered into willingly to pay off debts, gain training or education, or for protection. Forcing someone to submit is a rare and uncouth way of resolving disobedience: simply reporting a violation of signed agreement and letting the law handle it is better.

addons.text: Only Gender: Such contracts are technically open to both genders, though naturally one gets far more favourable terms than the other.
No Typical Slavery: As the primary form of slavery, slavery is more prevalent, but softer as a whole.

objects.title: Honourable Slavery
objects.text: There is an expectation that the defeated party will serve the victor that spares them. Choosing death instead is considered a great dishonour to the victor, and denying the service a great dishonour to the defeated. The law is written to take this cultural quirk into account. Given your likely strength, this is more of a boon.

addons.text: Only Gender: The rare exception as few of the lesser gender are an equal match on an honourable battlefield.

Light Slavery: Defeat now leads to the formation of a Light Slavery contract. While before, the law allowed slavery of any kind through surrender, it now offers the protections and legal obligations of the more formally written binding, negotiation of which is considered the ‘second battle’.

objects.title: Criminal Repayment
objects.text: Only those who have broken the law can be subject to slavery. While this often means slavery to the state (mines, fields etc.), slaves can still be rented for individual or business use. The relatives of the rich pay so their kin can ‘attend’ them at home, while debtors and miscreants must serve their sentence at their renter’s discretion.

addons.text: Light or Honourable Slavery: Unlike lighter forms, criminals cannot be trusted and so their slavery is of the harsher kind.

objects.title: Illegal Slavery
objects.text: Criminals buy and sell flesh beneath their rulers noses, or to their rulers directly, if they can. Slaves are usually kidnapped innocents, favouring the beautiful, useful, or strong, or simply those with no one to miss them. This black market avoids taxes and the little morality afforded to other types, leading to a particularly brutal and savage slavery hidden from view.

addons.text: Only Gender: While any may suffer a criminal act, the market wants what the market wants, and criminals aim to provide.

Light or Honourable Slavery: The restrictions of law and honour do not apply to the more brutal slavery of the criminal kind. As a result, such slavery rarely ever happens in the underworld, and when it does it is tainted with abuses.

objects.title: The Protection of Law
objects.text: The law extends even to the enslaved, and so things like murder and mutilation against them are criminal acts, be they done by their owner or not. Such crimes carry punishments reflective of the culture and severity, ranging from fines to execution. Naturally, sexual autonomy is still up to the owner’s discretion, so such crimes are not counted.

addons.text: Light Slavery: The contracts have limits on renewal dates and require evidence of a lack of coercion. They also offer greater protections and can rule out certain unsavoury requirements. Whether fully enforced or not is debatable; few slaves can afford lawyers.
Honourable Slavery: If proof that dishonourable methods were used, or the fight was thrown, the service can be ended. Further challenges can also be made to escape ones repayment.

Criminal Repayment: Criminals serving their sentence outside of a cell can no longer have their sentences extended at the word of their temporary owner, at least without cohobating testimony from a legal witness that further crimes were committed. Even then, the owner may be restricted from owning criminal slaves, to prevent further miss-management.

Illegal Slavery: While rampant within the kingdom, it is now viewed with more hatred. Expect a constant war on ‘unprotected slavery’, and stark arbitrary lines drawn in muddy waters that never the less get people killed.

objects.title: Race Specific Slavery
objects.text: Instead of a shared burden, enslavement is something carried out upon the unfavoured inferior races of the country, or at least restricted on racial grounds. Other races are precluded from the rigors of slavery, likely due to some elevated status. This opens a new section where at least once race must be selected.

rows.title: Raced Based Slavery
rows.titleText:
Must a delicate elf be a slave when hardier orcs roam free? Does human weakness demand or preclude them from slavery? Can the Drow be trusted more or less when chained? The answers to such questions lie with the people of Dormientes and the rules they abide by. The result of this is that other countries may take umbrage, looking down on a place that mistreats their kinsmen.

Each race is broken into two levels of enslavement. The first simply allows them to be enslaved, removing any special privileges that preclude their race from such a fate. The second near requires enslavement by law, those born to slaves themselves enslaved, and those free folk passing through viewed as strange, unwelcome, or dangerous, and easy prey, with plenty looking to restore the ‘natural order’ of things as they see it. 

Constructs are, by their very nature, built to serve, so they are not and cannot be, slaves. Harpies are viewed more as beasts and anyone mad enough to try and keep one would be seen at best as the owner of an exotic pet.

Illegal slavery, if chosen, can still include non-selected races, but the punishment for doing so is more severe.

objects.title: Human Slaves
objects.text: Humans can be found among the ranks of the enslaved. As the most populous race of Dormientes, this only makes sense economically.

addons.text: Your Race: You can be legally enslaved in this country.

objects.title: Humans Enslaved
objects.text: Humans are all enslaved, from birth to death. Being the most populous, this will turn the country into a slave state: an economic powerhouse of misery.

addons.text: Your Race: It is very likely that someone will try to enslave you if they discern your race, and if they are unable to, you will face considerable prejudice. The cult will still help you obtain the keys, but only in secret, and depending on their mentality, they may treat you disrespectfully, or try to sabotage your efforts.

objects.title: Elven Slaves
objects.text: Elves can be enslaved. These exotic creatures from the eastern woods go for a high price for their beauty, making fine pleasure slaves for those who can afford them.

addons.text: Your Race: You can be legally enslaved in this country.

objects.title: Elves Enslaved
objects.text: All elves who step foot in the country are hunted for the slave pens, with wars and raids bringing in any foolish enough to live too close. Relations with Melliomer suffer greatly for this.

addons.text: Your Race: It is very likely that someone will try to enslave you if they discern your race, and if they are unable to, you will face considerable prejudice. The cult will still help you obtain the keys, but only in secret, and depending on their mentality, they may treat you disrespectfully, or try to sabotage your efforts.

objects.title: Dwarven Slaves
objects.text: Dwarves can be among the collard, their stocky and strong forms a fine fit for forced labour. A race fit for the mines, many will view slavery as just another job, with worse pay.

addons.text: Your Race: You can be legally enslaved in this country.

objects.title: Dwarves Enslaved
objects.text: All dwarves are put to work by force, their strong bodies and  skilled hands seen as too valuable to waste on freedom. The dwarf clans of Highmarch view the kingdom with particular distain.

addons.text: Your Race: It is very likely that someone will try to enslave you if they discern your race, and if they are unable to, you will face considerable prejudice. The cult will still help you obtain the keys, but only in secret, and depending on their mentality, they may treat you disrespectfully, or try to sabotage your efforts.

objects.title: Orc Slaves
objects.text: As guards and labourers, and even some low rent brothels, orcs are now among those who can be enslaved, their savage natures eliciting little complaint from the other races.

addons.text: Your Race: You can be legally enslaved in this country.

objects.title: Orcs Enslaved
objects.text: All orcs require chains, not just to put them to use, but for the safety of all. Any green skinned menace, be they of great tribes or lone wonderers, will be domesticated and put to work.

addons.text: Your Race: It is very likely that someone will try to enslave you if they discern your race, and if they are unable to, you will face considerable prejudice. The cult will still help you obtain the keys, but only in secret, and depending on their mentality, they may treat you disrespectfully, or try to sabotage your efforts.

objects.title: Drow Slaves
objects.text: The scheming people from below can be enslaved. As fair as elves, and hardier, with a nature that makes them more morally acceptable to abuse; a good choice for those who break their toys.

addons.text: Your Race: You can be legally enslaved in this country.

objects.title: Drow Enslaved
objects.text: Rather than letting the spies slink freely, they are all caged on sight, to keep them from their dangerous freedom. This has left the Drow of the Deep Rivers with a vicious animosity.

addons.text: Your Race: It is very likely that someone will try to enslave you if they discern your race, and if they are unable to, you will face considerable prejudice. The cult will still help you obtain the keys, but only in secret, and depending on their mentality, they may treat you disrespectfully, or try to sabotage your efforts.

objects.title: Celestial Touched Slaves
objects.text: Even those touched by divine blood can be enslaved, rare as it may be. Their parents gave them a mortal life and so they should not be spared from mortal suffering.

addons.text: Your Race: Those of your blood can be legally enslaved in this country.

objects.title: Celestials Enslaved
objects.text: Too fair, too divine, and too rare to leave free. To look upon, or mix bloodlines with, or to see suffer, such slaves are highly prized, though Dormientes will be seen as a sacrilegious place by other countries.

addons.text: Your Race: As one blessed with divine blood, people will jockey for your enslavement, and if enslavement cannot be accommodated, they will lash out at you by other means. Disguises may help you pass, and the cult is required to help, but you may find the missions given lain with traps and waiting hunters.

objects.title: Demon Touched Slaves
objects.text: The tainted can be enslaved, as any other: it is not considered any ill omen to do so. In some respects it is a sign of equality, though their unique features can raise or lower their price considerably.

addons.text: Your Race: Those of your blood can be legally enslaved in this country.

objects.title: Demons Enslaved
objects.text: Those touched by demons must be enslaved, to prevent the taint from spreading and to control the evil influence that must surely direct them. They will often be sterilised, which leads to a predictably common use for them.

addons.text: Your Race: As one afflicted with cursed blood, people will demand your enslavement, along with your kin, and if enslavement cannot be accommodated, they will seek to banish you in exile or punish you in some way. Disguises may help you pass, and the cult is required to help, but you may find the missions given more spitefully challenging than you otherwise would.

objects.title: Harpy Pets
objects.text: Harpies are viewed as exotic animals, their ‘limited’ sentience allowing for the teaching of simple tricks. Raising them from chicks is considered best for taming, but forcefully taming the savage kind is a challenge some relish.

addons.text: Your Race: Prepare to be netted and petted as the populous will desire to see you in a cage. You’ll face considerable consternation and hostility if you try to resist, and the more your fame grows, the more collectors will settle for you pre-stuffed if they cannot ‘stuff’ you themselves.

objects.title: Constructs Outlawed
objects.text: Already a form of property, they can now not even be that, being outlawed within the central kingdom entirely. Should one be found it is likely to be forcefully deconstructed by a mob, even if owned by a foreign delegation.

addons.text: Your Race: You will be attacked if discovered to be of artificial make. Disguises will be needed, or unstoppable power, and while the cult will still work with you they are likely to out you as well, sharing the same destructive hostility as everyone else.

objects.title: Close The Rule
objects.text: Return to the choices of Dormientes.

rows.title: It Is Changed, Yet Looks As Though Always Thus…
rows.titleText:
The thoughts that reshaped the land move onward, and what was once a bed of wild ripples now settle into an untouched serenity. Your masterpiece, your dream and nightmare, and your destination. 

It needn’t be though. While you will have to go there in person to claim the power at its centre, it doesn’t have to be the point of your arrival. At least seeing it now, you are one step closer to your goal.

objects.title: You Know Of Dormientes
objects.text: Select this to unlock the other section of The World In Sight, taking one step closer to your new life.

objects.title: Close Dormientes
objects.text: Return to the world in sight.

rows.title: The First Steps of Arrival
rows.titleText:
With knowledge comes action, and you can now decide how you wish to enter this new world. The possibilities spill out before you, as dizzying as all the paths of an unwritten book; not just where, but how, and with who? Does your story start out with a family weeping a farewell, or with a bang of surprise, for you and others, or with the clink of a dungeons chains? 

It is almost painful to be so close, yet to still have so much to decide.

objects.title: The Where
objects.text: Where will your new life begin?

objects.title: The How
objects.text: What type of life awaits you?

rows.title: In What Country Will You Arrive
rows.titleText:
Between How and Where, Where is the far more important question. Where determines the people you will first encounter; the culture and threats and opportunities available; what threats you will need to overcome, either when walking in, or when living a life among, from birth or otherwise.

Just as throwing a dart, where you’re going is only what you are aiming for; each country is a massive place, and so it is only a general sense of where you’re going that you can decide. Specific locations may depend on any jobs taken later, but at the same time, you may arrive far from your job, caught up in some unexpected travel.

objects.title: Dormienties City
objects.text: The closest point to your final destination: the city built around the citadel of power. This is where dreamers and hopefuls are most changed by the choices you’ve made, and so while you will know what to expect, whether that is good or bad may depend on your past and later choices.

objects.title: Dormienties Rural
objects.text: The surrounding territories of the city state, from towns to villages to farms. Here, the race for the powers hosts its slowest members, the chief concerns of life being the troubles of the land, the harvest, and the passing of trade. Again, its other concerns are predicated on your past choices.

objects.title: Dormienties Wilderness
