objects.text: Whatever places of nature you’ve selected in the biomes, this will be your first sight of it, laid out bear without civilised folk in sight. You will be subject to the many creatures of this world, and as many of them are dangerous, this option is dangerous as well.

objects.title: Highmark Dwarves
objects.text: Deep in one of the clan strongholds is where your journey begins, where path and ceiling has been carved for the short folk. Cities and rurality often mean little in the winding tunnels, where homes and mineshafts are one in the same, but near or far, you will be among your people.

objects.title: Highmark Humans
objects.text: The human kingdom of Highmark is a place marked by cities, towns, and villages, but never very many of them. You will arrive among the standoffish people of the cold realm, and while human focused, many races can be found within.

objects.title: Highmark Wilderness
objects.text: Barren snowy mountains and dense boreal forests makes for a particularly dangerous place to be, even for those well experienced with its perils. Depending on the how, you may need to climb down a mountain as your first order of business.

objects.title: Melliomar Central
objects.text: The grand city of the elves in the heart of Melliomar. A sedate and learned place where only elves are allowed any permeant residents, with the exceptions being very rare. Despite being a city, their long lives leave most people knowing each other, to one extent or another.

objects.title: Melliomar Outskirts
objects.text: One of the towns, cities, and villages found on the outskirts of the forest. Half elven and half other in residents and culture, they tend to be a melting pot for those who wish to exploit the forest without the need to tread too deeply into its dangers.

objects.title: Melliomar Wilderness
objects.text: You’ll enter by the deep woods, where the thicket and canopy can lead deep in to darkness, where the lights of civilisation are unknown and unwanted. Tribes and caravans and explorers are the only bearers of that light, their presence either masked in camouflage or marked in overgrown wrecks.

objects.title: Peaceful Eardheart
objects.text: Your arrival will be in a peaceful part of Eardheart, where the demons have not yet touched. Such places are still in war, their produce and people sent to the front, so peaceful may be a misnomer. Of all the other places of Eardheart though, these are the safest, still holding some of its past beauty.

objects.title: Disputed Eardheart
objects.text: These are the towns, villages, cities, and wild areas, for whom raids and sieges by demons are a fact of life. Heavily militarised, those who don’t chip in are on their own, yet for all the callous math and cruel reality, there is honour and comradery here, where politics are often pushed aside for survival.

objects.title: Eardhearts Taken Territory
objects.text: Perhaps the worst parts of this whole world, and certainly the six points; here the demons run rampant, their ‘law’ a cruel misery for all trapped within. While mostly wilderness and ruins, there are conquered cities and villages where people are concentrated and the more ‘civilised’ demons rule.

objects.title: Lawful Nellacomb
objects.text: Of the many desert cities, you will arrive in one where the rule of law is upheld by a ruler of mostly respectable character. This will be a typical city, with the usual corruption and the standard incompetence’s, but where people are not actively preyed upon out of necessity.

objects.title: Lawless Nellacomb
objects.text: One of the many desert cities that resembles more of a grand bandit camp. That is not to say there is no law, but the law there is is the law of the strong, where the king or sultan always gets what they want, and those on the bottom are ground into the sand.

objects.title: Nellacomb Tribes
objects.text: Between the good cities and the bad, the vast desert stretches, and while arriving there would be a slow suicide, there are tribes and travellers that call such spaces home. Often more brutal than even the lawless places, these wastes can give rise to the hardiest of peoples.

objects.title: Deep River Drow
objects.text: The territories of the Drow: various insular subterranean cities, villages, and outposts that dot their hostile passages. While subject to the dangers of Drow society, they are far safer than the uncharted caves or the winding rivers and their chaotic flows. The only ones allowed are Drow, or those passing through.

addons.text: Not Drow: You’ll be unable to stay, yet with passage unpaid, leaving will be fraught as well.

objects.title: Deep River Dwarves
objects.text: The only other competition for civilisation aside for the Drow are either Dwarves or the mad. Dwarven civilisation in the Deep Rivers is small, and more mixed than their mountain clans, their focus on survival over inner rivalry in the more damp and chaotic realms.

objects.title: Lost in the Deep Rivers
objects.text: In the endless winding tunnels of the Deep Rivers, it is easy to get lost, and often a death sentence as well. While you may happen upon the Drow or the Dwarves, it is more likely to fall prey to or be a part of the mad followers of the things slipping through the deep places. Perhaps they’ll know the way out?

objects.title: The Floating Islands
objects.text: Here there are only outlets of minor civilisation: adventuring companies and isolated landing areas: no civilised races make a home here. Constructs roam, and harpies make their nests, and either could find themselves upon an island. This could be a very challenging start if you have no way down.

objects.title: Close the Where
objects.text: Return to the choice of arrival.

rows.title: The Three Roads Before You
rows.titleText: Before anything, you’ll need to confirm the path you’ll take to enter this world.

objects.title: As a Stranger
objects.text: Yours is a path without connection to anyone, choosing to simply appear one day, unbound. It is the cleanest approach, where everything you will have, in friends, family, and self, shall be made by the hands of your new life and the life you’ll live. It is perhaps the loneliest choice, and the hardest, with many trials for you to overcome, but you will remain the most ‘you’, uncoloured by the world.

objects.title: As a Resident
objects.text: Yours is a path well worn, forging a life and a space for yourself before inhabiting it. This is the established story, where your past can be written to inform your future, giving more choice as to the character you will be. As with the world, this is a reshaping of reality: the person whose life you create, their family, their friends, would not exist without your effort to make them so.

objects.title: As a New-Born
objects.text: Your choice is already made, as you cannot enter a world without age, save through being born on your first day. As a blank slate of a person, your family situation is more important than your own blank past. This is the story of the environment you grow up in, be it palace or slave pit, as you’ll have little choice but to endure it for the many years of your early development.

rows.title: The Path of the Stranger
rows.titleText:
This story begins innocuously enough, simply stepping out from the shadows and into the world. Perhaps it will be walking from the mouth of an alley unnoticed, or stepping from between two trees of a wood. Either way, you will simply find yourself in the world you have looked upon.

This entrance needn’t be quiet though. With a few changes, your arrival could be a thing marked in the history books, all before your tale has cause to be told. You could smooth out the edges of this rough transition as well, or lay a groundwork that may persist long after your presence is established.

Beware that while you will enter the world with all your chosen abilities, disorientation and a lack of practice can leave you quite vulnerable in the early moments of your new existence.

objects.title: Know the Words
objects.text: A simple thing when born or raised, but the language of this world is a fresh unknown to you. With this, the knowledge of the common tongue, as well as the basic written scripts, will be added to your lexicon, and the frustrations of learning will be much reduced for it.

objects.title: Know the World
objects.text: Without this, the broad details of the world still linger: names, places, cultures, peoples, and quirks, but the minutia is unknown. With it, common laws, the local currencies, customs, slang, and known dangers of the world are given, like the contents of a guide book written by an average resident.

objects.title: Clothes
objects.text: The most basic requirement: dignity. Instead of arriving in your birthday suit, you will be given clothes that match the location of your arrival, allowing you to blend in with any local, at least in fashion. They will always be plain and practical, but cut well and fit to your form.

objects.title: Money
objects.text: A pouch full of coins can usually sooth even the roughest cultural misunderstanding, and being able to pay for your first meal will certainly make a favourable impression. What each coin is worth may be a mystery, but combined, the purse should see a savvy traveller fed and sheltered for a week.

objects.title: Isolated Location
objects.text: Instead of a calm and normal location, the place you appear will be isolated. This may mean an empty forest, and old barn, or even an abandoned slum area of a city. There will be no-one around, but there may still be dangers in beasts and terrain, and so no-one to help you.

objects.title: Crowded Location
objects.text: Rather than a quiet place where one can innocuously appear, you will arrive in a place bustling with people. This may be a city centre, a village fare, or even the camp of merchant caravan in the wilderness. Questions will be asked if someone sees, and you’ll find no time or place to gather yourself.

objects.title: Ill Omens
objects.text: People will be aware of your coming, seeing signs in spoiled milk, diseased or fleeing animals, and an unease shivering through their bones. There will be a strong assumption that something foul and evil is coming, and depending on where you arrive, they’re unlikely to stop and ask.

addons.text: Isolated Location: There may be no one around, but seers and augers of all kinds will send those capable to investigate, to destroy whatever ‘evil’ can be found. See that they don’t see you.
Crowded Location: There will be guards, spells, and levelled spears ready and pointing at where you’re going to arrive. Be prepared for a fight on arrival.

objects.title: Good Omens
objects.text: People will know something comes. Flowers bloom, the sick are healed, and there is an air of anticipation, like something great is about to happen. When you arrive, people will assume divinity, if not in you then in your purpose. You will be welcomed with open arms.

addons.text: Isolated Location: Even isolated, there will be people, drawn to the feeling of something good. The crowd will be much smaller, but the smiles just as genuine.
Crowded Location: There will be festivities and celebrations galore to welcome your arrival. Be prepared for a feast, and lots of excited questions!

objects.title: Violent Arrival
objects.text: You arrive within a battle: a dangerous place, especially for your first few moments in this world. You best think quick on your feet, otherwise your journey could end before it’s begun. The fight itself depends on the location, from street riot to army camp to ambush at the roadside.

addons.text: Isolated Location: Fewer people, less chaos, and easier for people to see that you’re not on their side.
Crowded Location: A truly pitched and chaotic battle with shifting lines of engagement over a wide area. Good luck.
Ill Omens: The fight is likely between those drawn to evil and those compelled to fight it.

objects.title: Sexual Arrival
objects.text: You arrive in the middle of an orgy, your first taste of this world a clashing of bodies and sexes. You may join in, testing your new body, or watch from the side-line, or simply try to leave with as little awkwardness as possible. The participants will be too distracted with each other to notice either way.

addons.text: Isolated Location: Fewer people, so more like a two or threesome. Don’t expect them to ask you to join.

Crowded Location: A large amount of people and a large amount of sex. That said, such situations are not common; while it could be a busy brothel in a city, it is more likely to be non-consensual elsewhere, like a successful bandit raid or slave pit.
Good Omens: The good vibes of your arrival will cause the orgy. You will be invited in graciously and strongly associated with sex and the divine.

Violent Arrival: The combination makes for a scene of sexual violence, guaranteeing the greeting of a violent rape. Intercede in whatever way your feelings take you, or don’t, but there will be those involved who will assume you are part of it, one way or the other.

objects.title: Appear with a Bang
objects.text: This will cause a chaotic magical eruption at your entrance, tearing soil from the ground and flesh from bones for the few violent seconds the maelstrom appears. If there are people, they will think this an attack, if there are not, they will investigate the noise. You will not be injured from this.

addons.text: Isolated Location: Fortunately, no one will be hurt by your arrival, but a commotion will still be caused.
Crowded Location: Your arrival will be a catastrophe. Investigations will be done, vengeance sworn, and each of the many buried dead will be a bounty on your head.

Good Omens: Those drawn to the promise of goodness and wonder will be shattered into blood and chunks, their day of hope turned into a day of calamity. A truly awful combination, that will leave you heralded as a monster.

objects.title: Hunted
objects.text: There will be those who know of your arrival the moment that it occurs, through prophecy or foresight. Many will not care, the event miss-seen as insignificant, but enemies you didn’t know you had will send bounty hunters and assassins after you, and the mystery of their identity to unravel.

rows.title: An Assumed Identity
rows.titleText:
This is a story that is just begun, its first page giving presence and scene and introduction to its main character and their background. Like all characters created by thought, they do not exist until written, and so as you write yourself and your past life, the story of each scar and wrinkle, friend and foe, success and failure and choice made, the future takes on its own life, writing itself as you prepare to read through it for the first time.

While choosing these early details of your character, you’re creating the life your story will blossom from, but it is important to remember that this is not really you. Like an actor playing a role, whether they are like you or radically different will help determine how easy it is to step into their shoes. The opening moments of their tale may also set the tone for some time to come, and both who and what you start with will last far longer than its first scene. 

Finally, it is worth remembering that this will be, for all intent and purpose, a normal life. The boons that will later be specific to you will not have been carried by this person up until you take the part, and have played it for a while. Their relationships, property, and prior conversations will bear this in mind, and many may think you mad if you mention a quest for the keys, assuming you have no hope of success. After the first few days, any abnormal abilities you’ve chosen, good and bad, will begin to manifest, growing quickly until you have them all in a week. This will leave you quite vulnerable in the early days of arrival.

So like everyone else, you’ll have to be careful who you choose to be.

objects.title: A Close Match
objects.text: The life created has a personality near identical to the one you have now. Friends and family won’t notice any change; not to your favourite foods, colours, hobbies, the way you walk; even your speech patterns and names are similar, the language barrier crossed with fluid success.

objects.title: A Poor Match
objects.text: The people around you will grow concerned, if not outright suspicious, as all of ‘your’ preferences change, and not slightly: the person you ‘should’ be will be a person opposite to you, in taste, opinion, attitude, and thought, and the friends and family you’ll inherit will reflect this.

objects.title: Full Knowledge
objects.text: Basic knowledge is already given, like the language, culture, and the local currencies, but the social details of the life made are hazy: like an ill thought out impression. With this, knowledge of yourself, your friends, and your family, are delivered in memory, separate, but accessible, like a well-read book.

addons.text: The skills of this new life, such as its profession, are not given, but the opportunity to pick them up later on will be available.

objects.title: Becoming Them
objects.text: The knowledge of this new life and the time it has lived no longer remains separate, spilling into your mind as real as your own memories. While you’ll be able to adopt their role far more easily, you’ll be forever changed, having lived two lives, unsure as to which one was ‘real’.

addons.text: You will also pickup any skills they have, from accounting to assassination, allowing you to save points later on.

A Close Match: The life you’re assuming, its wants, its personality and experiences, are already so similar that you will scarcely notice this, nor be changed by it. Only by choosing a job or social class radically different from your own will there be any noticeable repercussions or existential crisis.

A Poor Match: A good way to go insane: so different are your personalities that your mind may crack, but it will not be a permanent thing; even the most discordant colours mix with time. You will be left different though. Perhaps with enough wisdom, you could keep the best of both sides?

objects.title: Day Off
objects.text: The person who you will be has a day off on the day that you arrive, or at least much reduced in terms of expectations and workload. This quiet day would be perfect to acclimatise yourself to your world: to inspect your new self with its own eyes and make plans for the future.

objects.title: Eventful Day
objects.text: You arrive as your new self on some momentous day. All eyes will be on you and how you behave, but at the same time, the stress, trauma, or overwhelming joy of the event, may go some ways in explaining your change of personality, or your answer of the call to adventure.

addons.text: A Poor Match: To help, your arrival will occur just after a head wound, allowing excuses for your change in personality or not knowing all you should. Suspicion will be replaced with concern, so long as you have people who care about you in your life, but your ignorance may be exploited instead.

objects.title: No Trouble
objects.text: Everyone has issues to solve: agreements made, appointments to keep. Not your new life. Through free and easy attitude or problem solving mastery, there are no outstanding issues in their otherwise uneventful life. They say the perfect protagonist is a blank slate. Well here it is.

objects.title: Considerable Trouble
objects.text: Be it blackmail, debts, eviction, or threats, this person has issues going on in their life that they would otherwise struggle to solve. This may be your new life, but without robust intervention, it will soon fall apart. Running away is an option, but the consequences may catch up to you eventually.

objects.title: Addicted Personality
objects.text: Your new life will be involved with an addictive drug. Technically, as your body is new and this life a realised fiction, you’re not addicted physically, but you will have friends and associates who expect you to be, and life geared around managing your addiction. Your class and reputation take a hit.

addons.text: Your chosen class and job effects the drug type, from a poor slave controlled by addiction, to a great mage hooked on a rare source of power.

Becoming Them: While still not physically addicted, you gain the mental compulsions, memories, and arguments that lead to taking the drug in the first place. They make a compelling case to take some more.

objects.title: True Addiction
objects.text: Now your body and mind will truly become addicted to the drug, to the point of significant and even fatal withdrawal if trying to give it up. With enough will, you can ween yourself off it, and you only have the addiction to begin, not the damage or the tolerance.

addons.text: The drug can be refined into multiple forms, and can be either an ‘upper’ or a ‘downer’. Whichever you take will satisfy the addiction, and whichever you have been taking is up to you, along with the form, be it snorted as powder, drunk, smoked, consumed, chewed, or even injected.

objects.title: No Family
objects.text: More often a burden than a boon, and a chain tying you down and keeping you from your destiny. This will hide the later family section, guaranteeing you be an orphan. After all, what good protagonist is tied down by worried parents or nagging siblings?

addons.text: Construct: This is the typical state of a constructed being, and so no points are given from selecting it, but it does mean you are no longer associated with your original creator, having been lost or sold off.

objects.title: No Friends
objects.text: This removes all friends and close relationships, leaving you alone and isolated when you first arrive. On the one hand, this leaves you free to make your own friends, and truer for it, and reduces the number of people confused by how you act, but also, acclimatising will be more difficult as you must go it alone.

addons.text: A Poor Match: As your new life’s ‘friends’ would undoubtedly be people you hate, removing them is quite a blessing.

No Family: A true nobody, known only to colleagues or by sight. While this may seem the path of the stranger, you still start with an established space in the world, with a job, a history, and a place to stay. You’ll still be known, just without friends, which may mean your new life has issues in their personality, or just works nights.

objects.title: Awkward Arrival
objects.text: The moment you arrive and begin your story will be a moment of monumental embarrassment. Where most would wish for their life to end, yours will begin, and whatever the situation, be it parental infidelity, accidental nudity, or literally pissing yourself, will be tailored to your misery.

objects.title: Difficult Arrival
objects.text: The moment you arrive, you are running, and will be where you shouldn’t. Be it by crime, ignorance, or foolishness, if you are caught where you are, or with what you have, or who you’re with, you will be in great trouble, perhaps being arrested or attacked. It won’t be fatal, but it will definitely be bad.

addons.text: Awkward Arrival: Not only are you where you shouldn’t be, you are likely there naked, or in some other scenario which will ruin you if caught.
Considerable Trouble: You arrive on the day when all the problems of your new life come to a head and things truly begin to fall apart.

objects.title: Dangerous Arrival
objects.text: From the moment of arrival, you will be in a dangerous situation, surrounded by beasts, brigands, or unstable footing. You will have to be careful and act with diligence to survive, or at least not act rashly. There may be others with you, whose lives are also in danger.

addons.text: Difficult Arrival: This takes place in the territory of your aggressors, with help far away. They can take their time, and numbers will be even more on their side.

objects.title: Sexual Arrival
objects.text: The moment you assume your new life will be one engaged in something sexual. It may not be all the way, but you and another will be naked and both raring to go. It may be disorientating to arrive with someone pressing their genitals to your lips, but what better way to explore your new body?

addons.text: Not a Virgin: Never mind things just getting started; you will be actively getting fucked when you arrive.
A Poor Match: Your partner is very unlikely to match your physical preferences, or even sexuality.
Addicted Personality: It is quite likely to be your dealer, exploiting you in some way.
True Addiction: It is almost certainly your dealer or their friends, exploiting you in some way. You will also be actively high, adding to the disorientation.
Awkward Arrival: A fumbling first encounter, with all the embarrassment and lacking skill that can be expected.
Difficult Arrival: An act of infidelity, where being caught will not just ruin your own life.

Dangerous Arrival: The sexual situation will be non-consensual, with you as the victim. Knife to your throat and a moment from death, do as they say and you’ll live, even if you wish you didn’t after. There may be multiple partners, multiple times, and even multiple species and would take some sizable starting boons to escape unscathed.

rows.title: A New Life Made
rows.titleText:
To emerge into this world as near everyone else within it has: through the natural process of birth. This path may be more natural, but it’s a slow start, as all lives are, with many things your developed mind and personality may consider humiliations. Still, a cleaner slate you cannot find, nor a better way to become as one with your destination.

While you may be born anew and your soul and spirit made pure (enough), the world you will be born into will be one of sin and life. Your family and you environment and even the nature of your birth will be marks upon you that you will grow up with and carry into adulthood, and what you leave behind can be as important as who you will become.

As with the other methods of arrival, there is a slight delay of a week before your chosen abilities manifest, but as a baby, protected by plot armour, you will hardly need them anyway.

objects.title: Emotional Reset
objects.text: Lose the burden of all that earned maturity. Controlling your emotions is a thing for adults, though not something mastered by all of them; you’ll get it back, in time, re-earning them after the screaming rage of childhood and the wild swings of a few teenage years.

objects.title: Forget the Dream
objects.text: The choices you have made here, like the warmth of the womb, will be forgotten, fading quickly in the light of a new worlds day. You’ll still remember who you were, but the why and how of your arrival, your choices, and even knowledge gained of your new world, will be utterly unknown to you.

objects.title: Forgotten Life
objects.text: A new born, by definition, cannot have amnesia, yet for you the memory of who you were will be gone. Your thoughts, your preferences, and everything that makes you who you are, will remain, but the memory of another world, another life, will not so much as haunt your dreams.

addons.text: Emotional Reset: With memory and maturity gone, this results in a total reset of the self: a true reincarnation. You’ll be free to develop as your environment demands, but unless you’ve changed your mental landscape already, the unshakable parts of you will remain, nature not entirely removed from nurture.
No Emotional Reset: You will be a textbook case of what people would describe as ‘an old soul’.

objects.title: A Slow Return
objects.text: Any memory loss taken before reincarnation will return over time. Flashes of a lost past will begin in dreams at two, and the rest will have returned by four, or when your plot armour would otherwise wear off. Being a baby is a lot easier to take when you know of nothing else.

objects.title: Skip Ahead
objects.text: Being born is no doubt a miserable and painful experience, and the time after little better. With this, such things can be skipped, waking up in your new world and new body a year after birth. You’ll still be weak, but the worst will be past, and you’ll be all set to ask a million questions.

objects.title: From Conception
objects.text: Not a sight most would wish to see, yet you could go back further, floating as an unseen ghost, appearing the day your new parents bumped hips and made you. Not only does this mean being sure of your father and circumstance, but also getting a feel and understanding of the world and your situation as a spectator.

addons.text: While you will be a ‘ghost’, moving through walls or observing from on high, you will not be undead, nor will you be able to effect the world around you in any way. You will be an observer only; one that cannot stray more than half a mile from your mother throughout the time of your gestation. You don’t need to sleep, but can ‘not concentrate’, allowing time to skip forward chaotically.

objects.title: Growing With Power
objects.text: Any abilities chosen previously or later on that a baby wouldn’t have (e.g. strength, skill, or magic) will be completely absent until plot armour is removed. You’ll likely be considered quite unremarkable, for better and for worse, but it should keep you from any accidents, save those normal for a baby.

addons.text: Skip Ahead: As you’ll be starting your life closer to this time anyway, your power is delayed as well, only kicking in several years after your arrival.

objects.title: Unarmoured Arrival
objects.text: The plot armour carried until reaching four years old (comparative to humans) is gone. While you’ll definitely be born, everything for the years after is a roll of the dice; neglectful parents, accidents, disease, and worse, could all kill you, but ‘Could’ isn’t ‘will’; you’ll have the same odds as any other in your environment.

addons.text: Growing With Power: There will still be a delay, making you far more vulnerable.

objects.title: Inauspicious Birth
objects.text: Relates to bad omens, disfavoured star signs, birth marks of cursed symbols, and even elements of your family, such as a religious group or marital status you’re born into. This may tie in with any unusual body choices, and give even your peers something to look down on you for.

objects.title: Auspicious Birth
objects.text: A child destined for great things, born at a conflux of events and signs. It may be limited to just your parents religion, but it nevertheless gives an air of prophesy about you, particularly to the superstitious. You may find more opportunities open to you later because of this.

objects.title: Unwanted Birth
objects.text: Your arrival was unplanned, and may even disrupt existing plans for your parents. This can relate to your gender or appearance, and while in some cases this can be a pleasant surprise, or something people can come around to, it can lead to some animosity from those who must make sacrifices to accommodate.

addons.text: Inauspicious Birth: Tied to bad timing and a bad situation, your birth is marred in tragedy. Perhaps your new life took your mothers through complications, or your conception was due to rape or infidelity. Either way, you are an unwelcome reminder for any who know your origins.

Auspicious Birth: Your parents may not like your prophecy. It may be to destroy what they hold dear, or require your sacrifice, or simply be the wrong fit for you based on your race, culture, or gender. Even if they agree, it can be hard to celebrate the chosen one if born of rape or incest or both.

objects.title: Blessed Birth
objects.text: Yours was a birth worthy of much celebration. Perhaps your parents had been trying for some time, perhaps it gives the opportunity for a better life for others, or perhaps the stars were simply in the right places. You will be raised as a most welcome child.

addons.text: Inauspicious Birth: Regardless of the cause; regardless of the time; your family loves and welcomes your arrival. Perhaps infidelity gave a trying couple a chance, or you’re born to godless heathens who care not for common signs. Even omens of destruction can be welcome if raised among those who crave it.
Auspicious Birth: Born at both the right time and the right place, you are doubly blessed, with parents who will do all they can to see you fulfil your divine destiny.

objects.title: Normalisation
objects.text: Without this, you will be born as you’ll become, usually matching traits with one or more parent. If you are a human and you’ve given yourself wings, one of your parents likely have wings. This removes that chance. Any unusual choice of appearance will be delayed until puberty, giving you a ‘normal’ childhood.

objects.title: Orphan
objects.text: Shortly after birth, you will be abandoned, left to be raised at an orphanage. This will hide the later family section and parental employment, giving you a new life forever separated from its part. After all, what good protagonist is tied down by worried parents or nagging siblings?

objects.title: Adopted
objects.text: Your new parents or parent are on hand soon after birth. Perhaps they are friends of your real parents, now past, or even their enemies, adopting you after slaying them. Expect them to be clearly different from you in race and origin. The family section now applies to them.

objects.title: Raised Strange
objects.text: Rather than one or more traditional parents, you are raised by something unusual. Sprits, animals, angels, demons, or other unusual supernatural elements, or perhaps organisations, such as knightly orders, academies, cults, guilds, or other community efforts. Your choice, within reason, but remember that ‘raised’ is not ‘joined’ nor ‘taught everything they know’.

rows.title: Your Family
rows.titleText: They say there is nothing more important than family, but anyone who thinks beyond the words of fools knows they can be as much a burden as a wonder. While you usually have no choice as to who you are born to, here you can set some things yourself, tying yourself by blood to stalwart protectors, miserable parasites, or somehow, through the strangeness of family, both at the same time.

objects.title: Family of Solidary
objects.text: A bond stronger than any guild, cost, or coat of arms: your family is a tightly bound and fiercely loyal group, looking after each other at every turn. An attack on one is an attack on all, and you will be expected to not turn your back on family, ever. They will help you achieve your dream, expecting only the same in return.

objects.title: Dysfunctional Family
objects.text: Ever at each other’s throats, yours is a family of caustic connections, full of betrayal and ill-mannered maladjusted adult children. Blood is the only thing holding the family together, and to these social monsters, the only thing worse to them than staying is trying to leave.

addons.text: Family of Solidary: No one destroys your family but yourselves! This turns your group into a fiercely dysfunctional mess that rallies around each other in times of crisis, flicking from screaming matches to dying for each other depending on their opponent.

objects.title: Loving
objects.text: You will be part of a loving family, where the bonds between its members are stronger than most, and marked with a willingness to sacrifice one’s self for each other’s happiness. Time spent with each other is paramount, and you will always have someone to talk to when you need it.

addons.text: Family of Solidary: You are part of a family that both cares for each other’s wellbeing and is unified enough to make that wellbeing a reality. Such families tend to go far, or at least weather adversity well.

Dysfunctional Family: Love and hate are two sides of the same coin. While your family loves each other dearly, conflicting personalities and interests can lead to explosive shouting matches and even physical altercations. A shame, as deep down, they only want to see each other happy.

objects.title: Neglectful
objects.text: The true opposite of love, your family doesn’t really care about you, your wellbeing, or your happiness, each member too self-absorbed to do so. They’re less likely to interact with you unless you can do something for them, leaving you with a drive to solve your own problems.

addons.text: Family of Solidary: As important as family is to them, it is more as a tool to use than anything to love. Nurture, to them, means to shape someone into who you want them to be, and so while they will make sure you have a place in their unified family, they care little for who you are as a person.

Dysfunctional Family: A family that doesn’t care about its members and constantly bickers and undermines each other, is a family set to ruin: a poisonous environment to survive and leave rather than fix. Your family will try to undermine your goals more than anyone, even later in life.
Reincarnation: They will care for you enough for you to survive, but offer little love beyond that. Depending on their status, they may have someone else to look after you, like a nanny.

objects.title: Good Heritage
objects.text: A family known for its honour, both past and present, and for having famous people within it. Others will come to your family for help, and offer help in kind, but a reputation leaves something to live up to, and something to fail should you go your own way.

objects.title: Bad Heritage
objects.text: A dishonoured group, marred with controversy and ill repute. Others may shun you and your family, even if its sins are long in the past, and may assume your efforts are something to fight against, even if seemingly benign. Yours will be an inheritance of reparation and apology, or unrepentant recidivism.

addons.text: Good Heritage: A heritage of good and bad. Hero’s to some and villains to others. You’ll find allies in unexpected places, and the same for enemies, your lineage mired in controversy.

objects.title: Big Family
objects.text: You have so many aunts and uncles, cousins, grandparents, relatives by marriage and relatives lost, it can be hard to keep track of them. This does mean that wherever you go, some family connection isn’t far away, but that also means your family can be difficult to escape from, with eyes in every country.

objects.title: Small Family
objects.text: Through death or other irreconcilable differences, your family stands alone. No distant aunts, no mysterious grandparents, not even a cousin twice removed, at least that you will ever meet or know. This just leaves any parents or siblings you have, and they are all the more precious for it.

objects.title: Parentless
objects.text: Raised by older siblings who had to raise themselves, or aunts and uncles, or grandparents. The bonds between family will be more raw, both for good or ill, as a difficult situation can lead to either deep affection or rampant abuses. Whether they are dead or just left is up to you.

addons.text: Reincarnation: Your mother will die shortly after you are born, or even during your birth.
Small Family: If you also have no siblings, partners, or children, you gain one or two relatives, such as an old uncle or grandfather.

objects.title: Siblings
objects.text: Do you have brothers and sisters? While annoying, with their bothersome antics, they can often be the most loyal and steadfast. They can also hurt you more than most. It feels like this shouldn’t be a choice, for if you choose to have them or not, regret will surely follow.

addons.text: As a Resident: You must also choose your place in the packing order. Are you the oldest, a middle child, or the youngest of the bunch?
Reincarnation: You will be the youngest sibling among this number.

objects.title: Twins
objects.text: You have a sibling that you shared a womb with, growing at the same time and bound with an unbreakable bond. They are not you though, lacking any boons or banes you take: it is inevitable you will go separate ways. You have a choice of identical or dizygotic twins, the latter being either brother or sister. This number is in addition to the Siblings chosen.

addons.text: As a Resident: Your twin will know who ‘you’ should be more than anyone, and will be the most supporting and the most suspicious of any change.
Reincarnation: They will be born at the same time as you and raised together, though they will be a normal child without your memories or powers

objects.title: Partner
objects.text: You have a spouse living with you. While not necessarily married, it is mostly likely, as your family would wish you to conform to the strictures of a typical marriage. This may be months or decades in, depending on your age, but may not match your preference depending on the choice ‘you’ had.

addons.text: Loving: They far more closely conform to your sexuality and preferences as you have family backing you up. While not perfect, they are safe and plain and loving.

Neglectful or A Poor Match: It is more likely to an unhappy relationship for you as it will have been arraigned to benefit others in the family or be for someone else. Don’t expect a good match on your preference for age, personality, appearance, sexuality, or any other metric.

objects.title: Children
objects.text: You have children of your own already. They will be yours by adoption or apprenticeship, your own body being newly made and virginal. They will look to you for guidance and protection, but that leaves you hurting more when they grow up and go their own way. A burden and blessing both.

addons.text: Not a Virgin: They will instead be your children by blood.

objects.title: Pregnant
objects.text: Your belly shows a slight bulge: the first sign of your pregnancy. The father may be a spouse, a boyfriend, or a relationship more tragic in origin. All that matters is that you have a new life growing inside of you, and that your family is going to grow by one (or more) new members.

addons.text: No Fertility: This is going to be the only chance you have.

objects.title: Arranged Marriage
objects.text: Your future is decided for you, with a partner picked out already. As this was done by someone else, your preferences do not factor into it. It may be with someone as unhappy with the forced match as you or with one of the ones who set it up. The ceremony will be in a few months or when you’re of age.

addons.text: Reincarnation: Barely born and already your life is planned out for you. Common among political marriages, it means the date is a long way away, but also means your future partner will likely be quite a bit older than you, with their minimum age the same as yours.

Older Age: A late marriage, perhaps due to a widowing or a life lived with other concerns. Like most arraigned marriages, there is still an element of forming alliances, only now it is more likely you are being paired with a younger half to look after. Otherwise, it could just be that you have very meddlesome and pitying friends who have set you up.
Gay or Asexual: As this was setup for you, your desires are not a factor. Expect a future relationship with someone who likely wants to have sex with you far more than you do with them.
Eventful Day: Today is the day, the wedding is about to begin! Can you remember your vows? You place? The proper dances? Perhaps it would be better to ask, can you can escape in time?

Partner: Your partner will not be married to you, becoming either a temporary love affair being broken up by the arrangement, a past partner you’re trying to get away from, or perhaps most obviously, the person you’re soon to be married to, testing the waters before tying the knot.

objects.title: Strict Plans
objects.text: While other families may be content to let children be children, yours aren’t. They have your life planned out in detail: a single cog in a complex machine. Straying from the path laid out for you will put you at heavy odds with your family, while following it would benefit them, and you (according to them).

addons.text: Arranged Marriage: The marriage is an important part of their plan, where it may cause all kinds of chaos to walk away from it.

objects.title: Addicts
objects.text: A curse plagues your family: a weakness to something that doesn’t let go. Perhaps it’s alcohol, or drugs, or gambling, fighting or even risky adventure, but it is clear that many have been consumed by this dragon of the mind. Your life will have the shadow of this as well, but you needn’t let it get hold.

addons.text: Addicted Personality: There addiction will be yours, its substance chemical, its source a clear thing.
Family of Solidary: The addition may be a temporary thing: a sickness that has infected your family. The bond you all have may be enough to shake it off and help each other out of the pit you’re in.

Dysfunctional Family: The addiction is causing your family to fall apart: a vicious cycle, where the addiction makes them worse, causing them to do more of the same to cope with each other, even sabotaging each other efforts to overcome it.

objects.title: Skilled
objects.text: Your family holds a trade or set of skills they have cultivated. They may be great cooks or combatants, skilled leaders or learned types, tradesmen or known for their charisma. Whatever it is, they will be able to teach it to you, and indeed, as you are family, will force you to learn it.

objects.title: Criminal Family
objects.text: Your family has links into organised crime, which can be a blessing or a bane. Depending on the class chosen, they may be thugs, bruisers, and pimp owned prostitutes, or they may be the heads of a criminal empire. What is clear is that they have no respect for the law.

addons.text: Dysfunctional or Neglectful: Your families criminal enterprises are often self-destructive, each willing to sacrifice the other to achieve more power for themselves. Expect to be used as a pawn, or trampled underfoot.

Solidarity or Loving: Your families criminal enterprises will be of great benefit; they will never turn you in or betray you outright, and will offer you shelter and protection from both the law and other criminals with a fierce conviction.

objects.title: Fated
objects.text: Your family has a task bestowed upon it. Perhaps it’s a secret to hide, or knowledge to keep alive, or a vengeance, a quest, an oath, sworn so fiercely as to be inherited by blood. Your family will be directed, as one, towards this task, and expect you to hold to it as well.

addons.text: Strict Plans: The plans made for you are all directed towards the end goal of your family, be it marrying you to the perfect person to deliver the killing blow, sending you to be trained as a warrior, or sequestering you away so secrets given survive in safety.

rows.title: Your Status
rows.titleText:
From the highest highs to the lowest lows, yours is a quest of power in a world of power. Where should you begin? The bottom, where slaves and whores eek a living? The top, where nobles and even the rulers you’ve seen previous can be found? Or, of course, somewhere in the vast stretch between? 

This will affect the kind of job you’ll be doing, or will be known to have been doing, and be relative to it. It will also effect any family connections and social circles you inherit. It will not change your appearance though, which may otherwise bring comment from typically fat nobles or typically thin slaves, wondering why their college looks the odd way you do, but this will be chalked up to the blood of your birth, and accepted easily as you’ve always been thus.

Depending on the country you start out in, both your mobility and your standards of life may differ also. A slave in Melliomer will be held by criminals due to the acts illegality, and a royal in the cut throat games of Nellacomb may live a more dangerous life than a guardsman. Both are more liable to change than the lot of a farmer or fisherman, but none are a brand for life.

rows.title: Your Family Status
rows.titleText:
No one is born alone, and your families’ situation will determine if you are swaddled in silks or in rags, and raised among tutors, traders, or traitors. It will be a mark carried throughout your life; even after gaining or losing it all, scents of perfume, sewers, or streets will cling to you in the noses of those you encounter, so long as they know the environment in which you were raised.

This will affect the kind of job your parents will be doing, both being of the same class, along with any family connections and social circles that could come to help you later in life. Your appearance, while still developing towards the body you have set for yourself, may face minor changes: more or less food can effect development, and a hard life can lead to harder eyes, just as scars of the flesh can be gained and carried onward. You will be resistant to such influences in a general sense, until your development is done.

objects.title: Bottom Rung
objects.text: Slaves, prostitutes, prisoners, beggars, and criminals. Anyone who could be considered ‘dishonest’ by profession. This is the class of the low life and the vagabond, rejecting or rejected by society at large, and as a result, will be a position of much stigma and suffering.

objects.title: Lower Class
objects.text: The heart and lifeblood of any country, performing the labours required for often little pay, and certainly less than it’s worth. Farmers, labourers, and soldiers; while skilled, they are not so skilled that they cannot be replaced, and punitive measures may be used to keep them from any big ideas.

objects.title: Middle Class
objects.text: This covers those who are otherwise powerless against the elites, but who have gained or been given a modicum of power. Scholars, clerks, skilled tradesmen and diligent merchants, guard captains and army officers, and any other position that manages and drives a society.

objects.title: Upper Class
objects.text: Not quite rulers, but low and mid-level nobility, or high level merchants. A station of wealth, usually just out of the limelight: a country noble, or a part of a business family, or a gossiping courtier decorating the halls of a palace. A space for competition, yet bereft of the usual hardships.

objects.title: Ruling Class
objects.text: The royal family, or at least related by blood or marriage. This includes high level nobles, and technically anyone in line for the throne, even if a great many places removed from it. They’ll have met any royal in charge of the country, and have both a courtly manner and noble prospects.

addons.text: Belonging among royals does not make your royal; such things depend on the profession chosen below. Even so, it is a valued and respected position as even servants may be the spares of lesser nobility, and the input of the harem can direct a nation as much as a royal advisor.

objects.title: Classless
objects.text: Those who live outside of society completely, not just in rejection by it, but often in opposition to it. Bandits and brigands, witches and cultists, travellers and tribes people; when the king calls, these people can ignore, or shout back in insult, and may be feared or admired for it.

objects.title: Moving Up
objects.text: With more money and more power than is usual for your class, you’re on the edge of moving upward. It would take a jump to shift classes, but with significant effort (a marriage, an investment, or patronage, along with countering those who’d keep you down) it is possible.

addons.text: Ruling Class: Depending on your choice of profession, this could mean either being in line for the throne yourself if a ruler, or being given special commendation for services rendered and being the head of the palace staff for something like a servant.

objects.title: Moving Down
objects.text: With a steady loss of money and power, you’re on the edge of being moved down the social hierarchy. This could be due to a long decline or a recent catastrophe. Hanging on by finger tips, it would take only a push, and with gravities trickery you may fall further than merely the class below.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: You are less than even the most undesirable in society, and so you will be marked for elimination. Part of a religion being stamped out, or an ethnic group being quietly subject to genocide, or a political dissident. Not even criminals want anything to do with you, if they find out.

objects.title: Criminally Contingent
objects.text: Your position is contingent upon criminal ties, who have bolstered you up or kept you supressed. They require payment and have control in your life, and removing these ties will cause a shift in your position toward the lower class.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: Overcoming your criminal connection will elevate your status.

Upper or Ruling Class: Being caught or turning against your allies in low places will result in rumour and dishonour from your peers, but you’ll be protected from a true fall from grace if noble. If you are a servant, then they made you, and can break you if you don’t do as they say.

rows.title: Your Profession
rows.titleText:
This will be the work your new life has been doing up until this point. Depending on how close of a match they are to you and how much knowledge of their life you have chosen to have, the labours of this position may come easily, or may be a complete mystery. Its marks on your body will be minimal, muscle memory present, but little more. This may mark you as a little strange depending on your choice and location: a pasty skinned farmer who labours in the sun of the Nellacomb desert would be a rare thing, explained perhaps by a recent migration.

Remember, you’re not just choosing a job: here you are choosing your colleagues, your friends, the early source of your food and shelter, your education, your freedom, and more. If and when you choose to declare your change in goal, toward the power and the keys you will need, your choice here may determine how people react. It may be the difference between someone saddles up your horse and joining you, or if you are laughed at, beaten, and chained in a cell. Later, it may decide if a king treats you with respect, uses you in an anecdote, or asks if you still bed people for coin.

If you do not choose any, you will have a random job for your class, or none at all, so be careful.

rows.title: Your Families Profession
rows.titleText:
This will be the main bread winner of the family. While there may be multiple parents, or no parents, along with other family members, the chief source of income is selected below. This means that if your parents are cobblers, both will be, unless otherwise specified, or one will be while the other assists or raises children. In some cases, like whore or prisoner, it is more likely to be a single parent operation that raises you.

Additional professions may be required by locations and will not be listed. Residents of Melliomer, for example, are near all skilled woodsmen by necessity, and even the peasants of Eardheart are taught to hold pike and be soldiers for when the demons come. Each job in each place has its own flavour.

If you do not choose any, they will have a random job, or many, hoping from one to the other, or none at all, so be careful.

objects.title: Unemployed
objects.text: No tethers or ties, nor job of any kind. This can be a momentary setback, a devastating upheaval of life, or simply the path of the carefree vagrant, spouse, or lordling. It is a fraught place to be in any case, and will require some hard work before becoming self-sufficient.

addons.text: Partner: You are the house spouse of your partner, looking after them and their property. You may not consider this unemployed when faced with the cooking, cleaning, and general management involved.

Bottom Rung: This leaves you poor, homeless, and often begging on the street, or stealing, or doing whatever it takes to get by day by day. For your new life, it may be the new state of things, or it may have been that way since living as a homeless urchin.

Lower Class: Your life is in a precarious position, currently between labouring jobs due to sickness or termination. Today’s meal may be safe, with a roof over your head, but that may not last for long as your savings will dry up soon.

Middle Class: You’re in a temporary place, caused by bad business or bad luck. It’s possible to survive for a while, lining up another opportunity, but it can be a downward path if you don’t get moving soon.

Upper or Ruling Class: You’ve lived a life of leisure, your responsibilities and skills limited while others handle things. Living out of someone else’s purse has put you in their pocket, and if you object to their requests, you’ll find being cut off to be devastating.

Classless: You’re a wild-person, living among the woods and hills, off the land, alone. While technically subject to a ruler, it doesn’t count if neither road nor tax collector can reach whatever hand built hovel or lean-to you live in.

Bottom Rung: Born to a family that is poor, homeless, and often begging on the street, or steeling, or doing whatever it takes to get by day by day. It may be just you and your mother, or a whole family of urchins, but such sorry states don’t last long; there are too many people waiting to take make things worse.

Lower Class: Your family is in a precarious position as its primary breadwinner is currently between labouring jobs due to sickness or firing. The timing couldn’t be worse for a new baby, which may force your family into accepting more dangerous or demeaning work to survive.

Middle Class: Your family is in a bad, but temporary place, caused by unfortunate business decisions or poor luck. With a new baby, it could be a precursor to things getting worse, but is most likely just a bump in the road.

Upper or Ruling Class: Your parents are supported by another, living a life of leisure out of someone else’s purse. This puts them in their pocket, so they may do anything requested of them to keep the status quo.
Classless: You’re of a wild family, living among the woods and hills, directly off the land. This can leave you raised in a dangerous wild, poor in friends and education.

objects.title: Slave
objects.text: Bound in chains, a slave to a master. Their job is to do as they’re told, be it cleaning, mining, fucking, farming, entertaining, or anything else their master wishes. If slavery is not legal at your location then it will be an illegal form, held hidden by uncaring criminals, but don’t expect rescue.

addons.text: Not a Virgin: You will have been repeatedly used as a sex slave, and may be being used for such as you arrive.
A Virgin: Sex will not have been a duty before, being new, preserved for sale, or undesirable for such things, but as someone recently sold to a new master, that is likely to change soon.

Bottom Rung: You’ll be the lowest of slaves, working in filth and feted hardship, cleaning out the pens, being fodder for the frontlines, or a faceless rear shared by soldiers and commoners. The lowest of the low, and the cheapest life can get.

Lower Class: You’ll be a typical slave, wearing rags, but valued enough to be bought and sold. You’ll be used as a labourer, whore, or other back breaking pursuit that befit your body, but your value gives you a modicum of protection; after all, few will wantonly throw money away just to break you.

Middle Class: You’ll be used in shops and front facing roles, or as cook, craftsman, or entertainer. Your new life will possess some skill that’s uncommon among slaves, like reading and writing, and so you’ll fetch a high price for your rarity, and may be treated moderately well.

Upper Class: You’ll be slave to a noble, cleaning and servicing their households. This means you were chosen for loyalty, beauty, lineage, or exceptional skill, and are trained to fit their role, doing your duties with poise and timeliness. Marks of discipline are rarely seen, at least openly.

Classless: You’re owned by a cult or by bandits. Such slaves are very roughly treated and often not longed for this world, but as you’re not long into your capture, you’ll begin with only minor injuries. You’ll get many more before they’re done with you.

Bottom Rung: Your family, such as it is, are the lowest and most disposable of slaves, working in filth and rancid hardship. Subject to rape, beatings, and outright murder, it is likely only your mother is with you, your father either dead or one of the owners of her leash. You’ll likely inherit the position.

Lower Class: Your family are typical rag wearing slaves, valued enough to be bought and sold. Used as labourers, whores, and other back breaking pursuits, they’re required to live together in work camps and can sometimes form tight and secretive communities.

Middle Class: Used in shops and front facing roles, or as cooks, craftsman, or entertainers. Your family, or at least mother, likely possesses rare skills, like reading and writing, fetching a high price as a result. They can be treated alright, but a new baby may lower their value.

Upper Class: Born to slaves used by the nobility for servicing their households. Chosen for loyalty, beauty, lineage, or exceptional skill, some slave families are bound in entirety, their noble owners breeding them over generations, like race horses. You’ll be trained to fit the role you were born for.

Classless: Slaves of a cult, tribe, or bandit clan. Your family may be very roughly treated, with some not longed for this world, while your parents were either caught with you, or you came after, fathered by a captor, either for fun, ritual, or both. You’re more likely to join your captors as you grow.

objects.title: Prisoner
objects.text: Chains, cuffs, or collar, pillory stocks or the simple restraint of bars; justice doesn’t touch people equally, and you are no exception. Whether the crimes are real or baseless accusation, the jailor the state or some other group, your lot is that of captivity, your freedom taken before you even arrive.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: Thrown into a pit, your fate deemed too worthless to remember, yours is a sentence for life, specifically the rest of yours. Your past crime or error must have been terrible, or your enemies powerful, to face such a terrible fate. Breaking out is your only hope.

Lower Class: A typical member of the criminal class, your stay is long enough to be considered your profession, mixed in with the general population who are near all of the same ilk. Perhaps the judge was having a bad day, or your recidivism knows no limits, but your sentence stretches on for years.

Middle Class: Having done something truly foolish, or gotten on the wrong side of a noble patron, your life has been upturned, your stay being harder than most. Perhaps your life’s old profession will be of some use to the other inmates.

Upper Class: Those of the upper crust rarely face prison, either escaping with token punishment or with execution. You must have really messed up, or become politically toxic, but being nobility, you’ll find nicer accommodations waiting for you, such as house arrest.

Ruling Class: A truly strange situation, though not impossible. Locked away due to the threat you pose, yet not killed due to some fondness or kinship? The trophy of conquest, kept to privately mock and gawk upon, or use in some scheme of politics? Your cell may be fine or not, but your lineage remains.

Bottom Rung: Your mother thrown into a pit, dodging execution in favour of worse fair; hers is a sentence for life, rendered for her crime or her station. Born in her cell, carried through sentencing or fathered by guard or inmate, you are an anomaly. Perhaps you’ll be raised behind bars, or orphaned once weaned.

Lower Class: Your family are criminals, your mothers sentence long and accepted. Born among the general population, you’ll be raised behind bars until her sentence is done, or fall into a worse or better fate once weaned and taken from her, depending on the vindictiveness of her captors.

Middle Class: Born in a cell, you’ll live with your mother before being taken away and given to your family outside if they petition for it. As your mother is no hardened criminal, she may be abused by others, and yourself taken and raised elsewhere. It will be a messy and distressing situation for all.

Upper Class: Any noble or wealthy person imprisoned will face nice accommodation; likely house arrest with their partner; a situation that can naturally bring about new life. It does mean being born into a family that is undergoing a crisis though, but perhaps the bad times aren’t to last.

Ruling Class: A royal baby being imprisoned is a thing of stores, but so long as a royal woman can be held captive, it can be so. Perhaps your mother is a political prisoner of another nation, a traitor, or a shameful family secret (and you as well, by extension). Don’t expect the throne any time soon.

objects.title: Insane
objects.text: Your new life begins with a broken mind, the usual moorings of reality having been stripped away in some form or another. At least that is the story. Many behaviours can be considered insane, from those that genuinely are, to simply speaking a truth against society or those in power.

addons.text: Becoming Them: While your ‘insanity’ may stem from unpalatable notions, it is more likely from genuine madness. Becoming one with that madness, your confusion will be multiplied, your inherited mental problems lessened, but not absent.
Classless: Not held by any state, except a state of madness. Yours is the ‘profession’ of a wondering madman: a profit or seer or just plain crazy, spreading your ramblings to any who would listen.

Prisoner: Rather than a prisoner of law, conquest, or politics, you are a prisoner of your own mind, and also prison. Locked in a madhouse, there is no sentence to serve; you are there to keep others safe from your insanity. Escape will be hard, and being believed and taken seriously by any who know will be even harder.

Classless: Your family will have the ‘profession’ of a wondering madman: a profit or seer or just plain crazy. They either drag their family behind them, or are followed willingly, the same malediction shared in blood.

Prisoner: Born in a madhouse, your madness may be assumed. Depending on the flavour of insanity your mother holds, you may be taken away, or kept in her arms to keep her calm, but it’s unlikely you’ll shake the inauspicious start, and may inherit some wild notions.

objects.title: Criminal
objects.text: A criminal by trade, hardened, professional, and unrepentant: a life dependent on ill-gotten income. Be it thieving, beating, breaking, murdering, either for someone else or as a freelance agent of illegality, the law your enemy, but you needn’t sacrifice your moral compass.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: You’re a two-bit thief, a freelancer, and not a very successful one, taking any dishonest opportunity you can. Working alone means you have more than the law to fear; gangs and rivals will not take kindly to competition on their territory.

Lower Class: You operate in domain of the working thug, employed to do the dirty work of gangs, subject to their protection and their cut. The work may be violent, or it may be as peaceable as relaying messages, or keeping watch, or moving stolen goods. The law will still get you, if it can.

Middle Class: Your new life operates in the world of the professional criminal, where skilled thieves, lock breakers, and seductive distracting charms are used. Your business is a thing contracted by bigger fish, though you can earn a good amount for a nights dishonest work.

Upper Class: Your life is a part of the higher echelons of criminality, where gang leaders work their schemes, corrupting nobles, officials, and even royalty to their cause. As wealth flows up, you’ll begin rich and powerful, but with higher heights come deadlier falls.

Classless: A poacher or similar outlaw, you care not for any restrictions placed upon your activities, not seeing yourself as the subject of a ruler or bound by their laws. Despite yours life’s perceptions, it will still go badly for you if caught.

Bottom Rung: Your family are two-bit thieves, freelancing beneath the notice of larger and more organised gangs. Begging, mugging, pickpocketing, and generally making a nuisance of themselves, they survive on the edge, with guard or gang ready to cut them down.

Lower Class: Your kin support themselves through employment to a gang, among other means, acting as thugs and muscle and performing other simple criminal activity. They’ve likely been in and out of prison, and are part of inter-gang rivalries that may see your family cut short from time to time.

Middle Class: The primary bread-winner of the family is a professional criminal, where skilled thieves, lock breakers, and confidence men work. They can earn good money through bad jobs, but must stay aware of threats and rivals to protect themselves.

Upper Class: You’re born into the higher echelons of criminal life, one or more of your parents or guardians gang leaders that may operate or oversee large criminal organisations. It is a dangerous business, for them and their family, but lucrative also.
Classless: Born into poaching, trespassing, and generally disregarding the distant rules of law. Your families trade may be their undoing, if they’re ever caught.

objects.title: Prostitute
objects.text: A lady of the night, or a man. Either way, they’re on the receiving end of others sexual appetites, selling their body to whoever has the coin to afford it. This is a freelance position, if inclined to name it generously, and so the risks and rewards, the highs and the lows, are theirs to manage.

addons.text: Not a Virgin: You’re quite the pro, your new life and body having engaged in many carnal acts for coin.

A Virgin: Hands and mouth may have been used, but otherwise you’re new at this, your inexperience perhaps a commodity. One that can be sold only once. The money to do so may be changing hands as you arrive.

Bottom Rung: You walk the streets, barely clothed, servicing beggars, drunks, and the dregs of the lower classes. Whether against alley wall or gutter channel, you don’t care, as long as whoever it is pays you this time. A profession of utter desperation.

Lower Class: As a street walking whore, you’re a somewhat respected member of the local lowlife community. The work is still servicing others on your knees, and the disrespect can hit hard, but a collection of regulars leads to a stable income and you’ll have a small (though shared) home to run your business out of.

Middle Class: This is the position some would call a ‘professional’, as skilled as any other tradesman in your bracket. You often work in your client’s homes, or servicing parties as the entertainment. Personality, decorum, and privacy justify your higher prices.

Upper Class: Yours are the rare pleasures of a courtesan, and courting the upper crust can command significant rewards for satisfying their odd requests and pivotal privacy. You’ll be highly sought after, perhaps even marrying an old and widowed noble, or retiring early with considerable wealth.

Bottom Rung: Your mother walked the streets, servicing beggars, drunks, and the dregs of the lower classes with little protection and for even less coin. Your birth likely stems from such a desperate soul-crushing profession, and you’ll start life as a burden on a person who has nothing.

Lower Class: Being born to a street walking whore can have some negative connotations later in life, especially if your other parent isn’t in the picture. Next to your crib, your primary caregiver’s bed will spend its days and nights rocking, their regulars perhaps stopping to decide if your features match their own.

Middle Class: You’re looked after by someone of skill, their trade simply the pleasure of others. They will get by on looks and personality, being invited out to parties and houses to satisfy customers, which may leave you raising yourself for the most part.

Upper Class: Child of a courtesan, your other parent may be a member of the upper crust. Not that you or they will know. Your guardian raises you in an environment purchased by their skills and charm, and may even be mistress to a noble, wealthy enough to retire early.

objects.title: Brothel Whore
objects.text: Unlike an honest prostitute, this is a profession in service to another: an employee to a madam or a pimp. As the largest cut of the profits is always taken, such people do not rise as high, but with a roof and bed provided for their work, they cannot fall as far either.

addons.text: Not a Virgin: The brothel business is your business, and you have a lot of regulars who know your every inch quite intimately.
A Virgin: A new hire, though soft hands and a willing mouth may have carried you a few days. Your first time is right around the corner, perhaps auctioned to an eager customer the night you arrive.

Bottom Rung: You’re working in a low rent slum brothel, where the loose walls display loose bottoms, or holes where a quick suck of relief lies on the other side. Looks do not count for much here, and the pay has an equally unpleasant countenance. Most places similar use slaves instead.

Lower Class: You work in a typical brothel, where workers and clients are paired and a good time is has by one of them. Clients are many, their requests pedestrian and unflinching, but the bordello air is often lively, with all kinds of entertainment given.

Middle Class: Your life begins employed at a higher class brothel, where a decent living can almost be earned. It (and you) caters to a noble clientele, whose needs are often more exotic, their tastes more refined, and their secrets better kept secret. Tips can be well worth pursuing here.

Upper Class: Rather than a worker, you’re an owner and business person, taking the profits of many into your own pockets. You don’t have to take part, but the staff work for you and/or customer is always right. Yours will be a high class establishment with powerful clients, if you’ve broken into the upper crust.

Bottom Rung: Your mother works in a low rent slum brothel, and evidently your father uses one. Loose walls display loose rears, where looks do not count for much, and the pay has an equally unpleasant countenance. Long degrading hours at work bring home only pennies

Lower Class: The family bread-winner works at a typical brothel, where workers and clients are paired and a good time is has by one of them. The hours are long, and little love is left for family by the end of them.

Middle Class: You’ll be born into an ok living, the one who raises you working in a brothel where nobles gather. You’ll be far more encouraged to follow the family trade and work there as you grow up, considering the good money involved.

Upper Class: Your parents still work at a brothel, but now as the owners. They may raise you up to run the family business, either starting at (or as) the bottom, or at the top. It’s just as likely they’ll pay for a good education for you when you’re older, to keep you out of such sordid affairs.

objects.title: Drug Den
objects.text: Not just a typical whore house, it is now a den of both legal and illegal narcotics. It is a much more predatory business as often the drugs are used to control the workers. Still, servicing clients has never been easier than when you’re flying higher than the floating islands.

addons.text: Addicted Personality: This is both the cause and the fuel for your addiction, the cost of the drug taken from your pay, often leaving you taking very little home, if you go home at all.

Bottom or Lower Class: You will be forced to take the drug as part of your employment and a means to control you. The moment it looks like you’re trying to quit, you get a double dose to keep you down. If you’re not already addicted, you soon will be.

Middle Class: You’ll party with your noble patrons, taking whatever they take. You’ll likely become addicted to several substances in time, if you’re not already, but the addiction won’t be used to control you outright. It’ll just be a happy coincidence that you wish to stay for long hours every night.

Upper Class: You’re the owner of the drug den. This gives you the ability to manage your addition quite easily if you have one. Noble patrons may request you party with them, even paying you to join, but your staff will be unreliable addicts that require more oversight and behind the scenes will be more miserable and exploitative as well.
Addicts: Understandably, this profession is the source of your family’s addition, and the anchor that keeps it unmoved.

Bottom or Lower Class: The one working will be forced to take the drug as part of their employment as a means to control them. The moment it looks like they’re trying to quit, they’ll get a double dose. If they’re not addicted now, they will be, and you will steadily lose them to their job.

Middle Class: Your brothel working parent will be addicted to several substances, and parties as well, becoming unreliable and degrading over time. They won’t be controlled using drugs, but it will control them, and they’ll be difficult to save.

Upper Class: Your parent(s) are the owners of a drug den. Now, crime and drug management add to their burdens, leaving your whole family, yourself included, more likely to become addicts and criminals, if not already. If they care about you, they’ll use their wealth to send you away to private schools.

objects.title: Miner
objects.text: A rock breaker, digging through the ground in search of precious metals, shining stones, or crystals of great value. It a dirty and dangerous job, favoured by the squat dwarves, but practiced by all races to some extent. In this world, the ground can hold more hidden dangers than cave-ins and poison gas.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: You’ll be a worker in a dangerous mine, or the dangerous part of a normal mine. Considered expendable, your job will be to squeeze into the narrow hard to reach spaces, scouting ore veins or mining where others won’t. It’s a job for the exploited or enslaved.
Lower Class: A typical miner, working in teams to dig out and reinforce safe shafts. Back breaking for sure, but the pay is enough to survive on and the profession has a pride to it.
Middle Class: A supervisor of a mine and its workers. You won’t have to break your back, but you’ll still have to go down and inspect the work of others, dealing with their problems and discoveries.

Bottom Rung: The primary earner of your family is a miner who is being exploited for one reason or another, being sent down dangerous and narrow cracks to mine where others won’t. One day, they won’t return, and the rest of the family will face hard times.

Lower Class: The primary earner of your family is a miner, working deep in some pit. Mining families are close, banding together when all too common accidents happen. You’ll grow up around dirty and hardy people who typically look out for each other.
Middle Class: One or more parents will be a mine supervisor, or even owner, going down and managing workers, and dealing with their extracted goods.

objects.title: Labourer
objects.text: A humble worker, doing what they are told, be it moving sacks and boxes, operating simple machines, constructing, destructing, or repetitive hand work. The pay is rarely good and the treatment often unfair: a broad category of sweaty and backbreaking labour.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: You’ll be turning the wheels of mills and work houses, or fetching and carrying under close supervision.
