This is little more than slavery, with token pay that’s barely enough to drown half your sorrows, let alone save up for a better life. A thing for immigrants or fugitives to scrape by with.

Lower Class: The bedrock of the economic workforce, yours will be a typical job of a common quality, utterly unremarkable in its normalness. Perhaps a bricklayer, an apprentice craftsman, a lumberjack, dockworker, gardener, tanner, basket weaver, you name it.

Middle Class: Either young, pursuing apprenticeships and day-labour to make your parents proud, or a craftsman fallen on hard times, needing a little extra, or an old hand, having worked enough honest days to wind down with simpler work.

Bottom Rung: Your parents are the lesser of the lower class, performing truly gruelling work for very little pay. It’s hardly enough to get by, especially with a new arrival, but as long as nothing unexpected happens, they should keep their heads above water.

Lower Class: You are raised by the epitome of the working class, be they bricklayers, apprentices, lumberjacks, dockworkers, gardeners, tanners, basket weavers, stone cutters, fishermen, basically any number of things. You’ll be raised as an honest hardworking person by example.

Middle Class: Your parents will be either young, pursuing apprenticeships and day-labour to help with the new arrival, or craftsman fallen on hard times, doing grunt work for a little extra while they get their affairs in order.

objects.title: Villager
objects.text: A labourer with a rural twist, such as a farmer or hunter. Your life awaits you in the quiet countryside, where everyone knows your name and looks out for each other, but education and prospects are often non-existent. In this world, with its monsters and hazards, it can also be very dangerous.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: In simple village life, class is shared, rising and falling within seasons of prosperity. You will be a villager of a poor and shunned village, disfavoured by your lord and prey to surrounding dangers.

Lower Class: You’ll be a typical farmer or village person. Among the peasants, everyone helps each other out, and often shares in the rewards, their many early mornings earning more time for festivals and days of joy.

Middle Class: Everyone on a farm works, even the owner. In fact, especially the owner, if a farm gets big enough to need to hire hands. People can be lazier than livestock, as you’ll soon find out, but greater rewards will be yours for it.

Bottom Rung: In simple village life, class is shared, rising and falling within seasons of prosperity. You will be born into a poor and shunned village, disfavoured by your lord and prey to surrounding dangers.

Lower Class: Your parents will be typical farmer or village people. Among the peasants, everyone helps each other out, and often shares in the rewards. Expect to be raised by the whole village, each of whom will think you’ll be there until the day you die, like them.

Middle Class: As owners of a farm, your parents will work hard, and so will you, as soon as you can stand. The farm will be big enough to hire hands, who bring stores and skills from outside the village.

Classless: You live on an isolated farm, growing enough to sustain yourself, and distant enough to be beholden to nobody. It may be lonely, and dangerous, but as long as you remain quiet and isolated, no start will give you as many long and empty days to acclimatise to your new world, in theory.

Classless: You’re born on an isolated farm, your parents growing enough to sustain yourselves, distant enough to be beholden to nobody. It may be lonely, and dangerous, but it’s often slow and uneventful.

objects.title: Service Staff
objects.text: No matter the world, the jobs that require serving customers can be filled with joy and misery both, though mostly the latter. Barmaids, waiters, shop assistants, low level servants: any position that requires wearing a smile for people you want to strangle.

addons.text: Lower Class: Rushed off your feet on the tavern floor, you cater to drunks, both hungry and thirsty, weathering their disrespect and unfettered advances. High or low class, the establishment rarely matters, the position viewed as disposable and cheap, despite the skill needed.

Middle Class: Yours will be the role of a hired shopkeeper or tradespersons assistant, dealing with customers, negotiating, bartering, soothing the impatient. Rarely the owner, but trusted enough not to scare off the buyers.

Upper Class: A servant in a noble household. While your own quarters may be cramped, you are surrounded by luxuries envied by others and hold a decorum that takes years to master. Professional servants can climb high, and retire early, and are seen as the enviable upper class of service roles.
Lower Class: Your parents will do tavern work, tending bars and waiting tables. It’s low pay and demeaning, leaving them constantly tired, but it puts food on the table.

Middle Class: Your parents will have good work behind a sales counter, dealing with customers at either face values, or by negotiating and bartering. It leaves them very socially adept, and able to keep their cool when angry.

Upper Class: You will be raised by servant in a noble household. This is usually an inherited position, the tasks and loyalty of servants of such a station needing cultivation. You’ll even have something of an education, though it will focus on courtly manners (for servants) and poise.

objects.title: Gambler
objects.text: A true rogue’s profession, seeing high highs and low lows as they place bets on cards, duels, drinking games, sporting events, and anything else that money can reasonably be put on. They won’t have much in the way of savings, or a plan, but why have either when you can just win it big tomorrow?

addons.text: Bottom Rung: Essentially unemployed, but while that would only leave you homeless and penniless, as a gambling addict, you now also have significant debts and enemies looking to squeeze money out of you by whatever means available.

Lower Class: You’re a wastrel, drinking and gambling your days away, moving from tavern to tavern. Your winnings get you a bed and food and a spot in the next game, but it’s a life that leaves you constantly on the back foot.

Middle Class: You’re a suave party goer and professional gambler, whose quick hands and wits make sure you never go hungry. Gambling houses and the criminals who own them may hate you, and you’re not exactly saving for retirement, but you wear fine clothes and eat good meals daily.

Upper Class: A fool and his money are easily parted, and rich friends lead you to rich winnings. Fine horses and houses, connections and invitations, gold and livelihoods, are all mixed in the pot of your games, and as you’ve been winning, you have an unusually mixed bag of high worth winnings to work with.

Bottom Rung: Your parents are essentially unemployed: hopeless gambling addicts looking for their next fix. As they have significant debts and enemies, they may be driven to desperation; it could even be that new-born-you are gambled away in time, or taken by the sharks to punish them.

Lower Class: Born to wastrels that drink and gamble to mixed success. On the one hand, their winnings get you food and a roof, and them a spot in the next game, but it’s a life that leaves your family constantly on the back foot.

Middle Class: Born to suave party going professionals, whose quick hands and wits make sure your family never goes hungry. Gambling houses hate them, and they’re always on the move, but they always manage to come out on top somehow, and may teach you their grift as you grow.

Upper Class: Your parents are sharks who swim in noble waters, playing the part and parting them from their money with enough ease to pull off being nobility themselves. It’s partly a con, but always a gamble, and with allsorts in the pot, you’ll be raised in a strange and ever changing environment.

objects.title: Soldier
objects.text: The life of a warrior in service to a kingdom, accepting coin for kills and wrapping various levels of honour into the act. The tasks differ with class, from guarding kings to digging privies, and the training may be anything from a duelling mastery to being told to run if you see the enemy.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: The place of a peasant levy, drafted and moved to the front as disposable fodder, or a deserter, having already made the smart move to run from your duties. If you run you’ll be hunted down. If you stay you’ll likely die. At least that is the choice facing your life before you step into it.

Lower Class: A typical foot soldier. Whether young and in training or a seasoned veteran, all are the same in pay and prestige, except among the battle brothers that make up your line. You march where you’re told and you fight when you’re told, and there’s not much more to it than that.

Middle Class: An officer, usually risen from the ranks and limited for it. Your task is to keep others in line, meeting out punishments and leading charges. It’s a tough job, but better pay and higher honours are yours if you can survive.

Upper Class: Usually of the nobility, if only in a distant way: illegitimates and bastards given a paid for rank and told to fetch honour and glory as commanders on the field. Some may become noble guards in lesser households, ready to become the vanguard in their lieges’ military efforts.

Ruling Class: A soldier of royalty, the best of the best, either serving in their private honour guard or as protectors to the royals themselves. Some see this as a cushy position, high pay and no work, but the latter couldn’t be further from the truth, as parades and ceremonies are the least of the threats you’ll face.

Bottom Rung: Your guardian is a peasant levy: fodder, standing at the front and taking the first charge, and usually not by choice. You may be born on the battle field, or to a camp follower while your other parent fights and probably dies.

Lower Class: Born to a foot soldier, either by a follower at camp or a woman on the battlefield. Companies of soldiers look out for each other, so if your parent dies, you may end up being raised by the company, dragged from battle to battle with the various followers that accompany armies.

Middle Class: The child of an officer, usually risen from the ranks and limited for it. You may either be raised in a good home, one parent rarely seen thanks to their deployment, or it may be that you’re parents both march with the army, with you with them, exposed to the family trade.

Upper Class: The child of a lesser noble: some illegitimate bastard given a rank paid for by your grandparents. Perhaps they even earned it. It’s unlikely you’ll be accompanying your parent, being raised away from them, but being the child of a military family brings with it a certain honour.

Ruling Class: The child of one of the highest soldiers in the land, honour guard to royals and the vanguard of battles. You’ll be raised in safety, but proud military history will bring with it expectations. Expect to be trained by them near from birth.

objects.title: Mercenary
objects.text: One who kills for money, without the honour, stability, or protection of one who serves a ruler directly. This leaves the profit better but the work dirtier, and few will ransom a mercenary, or give one a fair trial. Being disposable can leave many acting as glorified bandits, predatory within and without.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: An unpromising recruit, there just to catch arrows and fill the ranks, or a camp follower, doing chores and warming beds for protection. In either case, you’re likely paid more in food than coin, trapped in a prison rules environment where you’re at the bottom.

Lower Class: A typical merc, doing damage for coin, going wherever the leader says, which is wherever the company is paid. Unprotected by the rules of law, they are not bound by them either, giving their short lives an opportunity for cruel fun their employers turn a blind eye to, or encourage.

Middle Class: A company leader, taking coin and leading barely tamed bandits. This means starting out with a band of troops that are yours to lead and develop, their work and character what you make of it. They may be the rare chivalrous type, or the most monstrously rapacious.

Bottom Rung: Born to an unpromising recruit, or a camp follower, doing chores and warming beds for protection. Your family will be paid more in food than coin, trapped in a prison rules environment where you’re all at the bottom, but hey, if/when they die, you may become the company mascot.

Lower Class: Born to a typical merc, doing damage for coin. Each company has its own attitude; you may be born to the sweetheart of an honourable monster hunter, or to the latest company conquest dragged along for entertainment. You’ll be considered child to the band, and raised to join it.

Middle Class: Born to a company leader, managing a sizable band. Each company has its own reputation, and so you may be born to the leaders swooning sweetheart, or to their latest cruel conquest. You’ll be taught the trade and groomed to take over.

objects.title: Guardsman
objects.text: Unlike a soldier, the guardsman’s responsibility is not on the distant battlefields, but the streets of cities and the roads between them. There are many ranks and duties, but keeping order is the concern of all of them, at least where corruption hasn’t soured that concern to selfishness.

addons.text: Lower Class: From prison guard, to gate guard, to patrolling road guard; yours is a tiring routine of searching cargo for smuggled goods, keeping drunks in line, and telling people you’re ‘looking into’ whatever troubles they have. Occasionally exciting, and wide open for the accepting of bribes.

Middle Class: Guards with brains, also known as a captain or detective. You’ll be either managing other guards or investigating crimes, or perhaps doing paper work behind a desk. It leaves your finger on the pulse and your duties more dynamic.

Upper Class: Royal or noble guards, better paid and better equipped. You’ll be tasked with keeping your employer in power, punishing traitors, putting down revolts, and guarding much cushier and richer areas. You’ll act as the trusted muscle of the wealthy elite.

Lower Class: From prison guard, to gate guard, to patrolling road guard. Good, honest work, most of the time; if your guardian begins to bring home more money, you’ll know they’re on the take. If they don’t, you may find them taken out for being too honest, depending on your location.

Middle Class: The primary bread-winner of the family will be a captain or detective in the guard, solving murders or leading troops. Lots of opportunity for corruption and enemies, but also good pay and respect if done right.

Upper Class: You’ll be born to the guards of nobles, patrolling their castles and punishing those who would challenge their employers power. They’re much better paid, to prevent bribes, and you’ll be raised in an environment of greater opportunities for it.

objects.title: Craftsman
objects.text: A skilled and honest tradesman, be it a candle maker, bookbinder, alchemist, or chef; anything that needs years of training and experience to claim expertise. The choice is yours, and while you may be inclined to pick a blacksmith or alchemist for the adventure, never underestimate the usefulness of a shoemaker.

addons.text: Upper Class: Some tradesmen rise to the top with their expertise, becoming castle architects, royal chefs, of tradesman’s guild leaders. You may be well known for your skills, becoming the best whatever-you-do in wherever-you-are.

Upper Class: Some tradesmen rise to the top with their expertise, becoming castle architects, royal chefs, of tradesman’s guild leaders. Your parents trade will be known far and wide, and have more money and prestige.

Middle Class: A modest living in a respectable trade. You may even be more involved in the community, owning your own business and speaking your mind about it. More time and more money also means more friends, regulars, and colleagues; a greater chance of a busy life.

Middle Class: Born to parents working a respectable trade. You’ll either be raised to pursue the same business, or they may be inclined to send you to a school or tutor to bring new skills into the family. Either way, it is usually a very secure and uneventful life.

objects.title: Merchant
objects.text: One who sells, from dealing with coppers out of rickety travelling stall, up to handshake deals over the finest meals. The business of business is their business, and whatever they’re selling doesn’t matter near as much as whose buying.

addons.text: Lower Class: Low cost goods sold for low cost profit, usually on street corners. Pies, meats, trinkets, fabrics, tools; you buy from the people who make them and sell to the people who need them. You’ll never get rich, but it’s mostly honest work.

Middle Class: Owning a shop on a good high traffic street, where you can sell your wares to whoever is interested. The wares themselves are your choice, be it be it gold and jewels, housewares, adventuring supplies, slaves, even food and alcohol, your ‘shop’ a tavern instead.
Upper Class: Five thousands swords, and seven thousand pikes, completed in three years time? You’ll get it done. Your business is in bulk and your buyers are as rich as you’ve become.

Lower Class: Your parents scrape by with low cost goods sold for low cost profit, decorating street corners with their pies, meats, trinkets, fabrics, tools, toys, and whatever else they’ve got their hands on. Expect them to teach you the secrets of selling, though they may not be worth much.

Middle Class: You’ll grow up in a shop on a good high traffic street, where gold and jewels, house wears, adventuring supplies, slaves, or even food and alcohol, your ‘shop’ a tavern instead, are sold. Expect to be raised as quite the little sales assistant.

Upper Class: Your parents or guardians sell big, rubbing shoulders with those who can afford it. They may even be more wealthy than some nobles, but won’t expect the world to hand them anything, so expect the best in terms of education and opportunity growing up.

objects.title: Bureaucrat
objects.text: A paper pushing, desk riding, middle managing, administrator. Every kingdom must have its fair share of pedantic clerks and civil servants in order to function, keeping grain silos filled, ensuring treaties are upheld, and counting heads for the purpose of taxation. A dull job, but safe and reliable.

addons.text: Middle Class: The quintessential white collar job, in the middle of every metric. People will think you boring, and the notion of you going off on a quest to gain the power of Dormientes will be beyond insane: a truly knee slapping absurdity.

Upper Class: A steward of nobility, your papers and your efforts ensure the smooth running of a country, or a good chunk of it. You may also be called to perform the duties of a diplomat, leaving you better travelled than the average quill pusher.

Middle Class: Your parents will be the most boring of bureaucrat workers: accountants for an uninteresting business, or some sub-committee chair for the road maintenance commission. That they could birth anyone destined for greatness will be a most humorous jest.

Upper Class: Your parents will be steward to a noble, their work important and the punishment for failure considerable. High stress, but high reward, and you’ll be raised with connections in high places.

objects.title: Academy Student
objects.text: Resident at a place of learning, walking the path of the scholar. Such may be a fresh faced student, studying for a year or more before venturing into the world, or a veteran sage and teacher, whose studies never end. Your location will also play a part, each place with its own schools and masteries.

addons.text: Dormienties: A place where people study the citadel and its powers, working closely with the cult.
Highmark Dwarves: A place where people study the workings of the earth, the forges fires, and enchanted metals.
Highmark Human: There are few places to study in Highmark, but many religious orders and witch hunting crusaders are open to students.
Highmark Wilderness: The great academy for necromancy up in the mountains, or the lesser studies of the local cultists.
Melliomar: A place attracting rangers, woodsmen, and druids, but have schools of all kinds thanks to its many skilled elven residents.

Eardheart: The Grand Collage of War is Eardhearts primary teacher, second only to the battlefield itself. Fighting excellence, in body and magic, are studied there, and students are required to take the fight to the enemy.
Nellacomb: Akzinianar, the great university of the desert. It is not just magic of all kinds studied here, but history and culture as well, to a significant degree.
Deep River Drow: The Drow have many places of study, being isolated and diverse. None are more infamous than their unnamed academy of stealth, where spies and thieves and assassins learn their craft.
Deep River Dwarves: The Dwarves of the rivers have few academies, but their pathfinders guild teach the much values skill of knowing where you are, which is vital below.

Lost in the Deep Rivers: There are dark places where knowledge lurks, and if you call no other place home, here is where you may find the whispers of dark forces, and scholars driven mad for listening to them.

The Floating Islands: The academy of exploration and mapping of the floating islands is a small yet dedicated collective. While others loot, they study, focusing on the history and making incremental gains in understanding.

Middle Class: You’re student of middling parents, sent in to learn more about the world to help with your career, or perhaps a bookworm scholar being carried by a recognised natural talent. Either way, you’re being sponsored, and results are expected.

Upper Class: You’re a noble by birth, probably a spare, sent to garner the prestige of having offspring attending a prestigious academy. If not that then you’re a teacher who has risen to a position of academic excellence, your knowledge sought by many.

Ruling Class: You’re a member of royalty by birth, but probably a distant spare, sent to garner the prestige of having offspring attending a prestigious academy and to keep you out of the way. After all, when the royal cannot be spared, the teachers are usually brought to them.

Classless: You’re apprentice to one of the wild people, scholars of old magic and forgotten ways, learning their craft and their wisdom. This may mean being student to a witch, a travelling wiseman, or one ostracised for their wicked ways, like a necromancer or demonologist. Your choice of who. As one of their few or only students, their attention will be focused more on you, for better or worse.

Middle Class: A child can be a disruptive force to a student, whether carried by them or harboured by a local dalliance. At least one parent will be intelligent enough for study though, and that bodes well for you. If you don’t disrupt their efforts, your first few years may be spent listening to lectures.
Upper Class: Your parent or guardian will be a teacher at their academy, and so you will be raised by an educator with a good income, and little tolerance for unruly children.

Ruling Class: Born to a royal or upper noble, yet at a place of learning? There may be an element of scandal to your arrival, or the interruption of ‘royal duties’ to make you. You’ll still be royal, but your parent attending an academy must mean they are hardly in line for the throne.

Classless: You will be raised by one of the wild people: scholars of old magic and forgotten ways. By blood or by adoption, it matters not; they’ll be student to a witch, or a travelling wiseman, or one ostracised for their wicked ways, like a necromancer or demonologist. Your choice of who. You’ll be raised in the shadow of their teachings.

objects.title: Adventurer
objects.text: The lines between an assassin, a mercenary, a scout, a thief, and a dozen other professions, are tenuous at best. Perhaps it is all of them put together that make the job unique. Who knows. In these lands, they often quest for the keys, but also take guild work of all kinds.

addons.text: Lower Class: You’re a hopeful, looking to escape the drudgery of normal life. Unskilled, ill equipped, and under prepared; people like you are a common sight upon the long road of a hero’s journey, usually appearing as empty skulls and other forlorn warnings.

Middle Class: Yours is the life of a working adventurer, hunting beasts, putting down undead, goblins, and bandits. A job of many tasks, and you’ll have become proficient enough to solve some and survive the rest, more or less.

Upper Class: You’re a famous adventurer, whose quests have earned you some renown and fortune already. No key’s, but people will believe they can’t be far away if you stick to the path you’re on, and so you may be invited to parties, and be the subject of lesser tales and gossips.

Classless: An adventurer in spirit, but a chaotic path, you’re not tied down by any job or guild. This would be the bard that dabbles in everything, moving from village to village, impressing with trick and song, or the vagrant who can take their hand to any going job.

Lower Class: Your parents are among the hopefuls, looking to escape the drudgery of their lives. Unskilled, ill equipped, under prepared, and now with a baby on the way, a hopeful journey may soon meet crushing reality. Still, if they live to raise you, expect their dream to live on as well.

Middle Class: Born to a working adventurer, hunting beasts, putting down undead, goblins, and bandits. It’s a job that requires skill, and as a family profession, you’ll be expected to learn with them.

Upper Class: Child of a famous adventurer, perhaps now settling down to retirement and an easy life. They’ll likely even have a key, or even two, and nothing would make them prouder than you following in their footsteps.

Classless: Born to an adventurer in spirit, if not profession. Perhaps a child will slow down their wondering for a time, unless they take you with them, showing you the way to survive in the wild, by odd job and sure skill. The start of an eclectic education.

objects.title: Gladiator
objects.text: A champion of the arena, if gladiatorial combat is legal. A combatant of underground fight matches if not. The crowd, who is there to see blood and spectacle, care little either way. This can be a very dangerous path without the skills to back it up; more gladiators died than ever rose to the top.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: Fodder for the pits, at best you will be one of a dozen thrown against an opponent you cannot hope to beat. Usually a criminal being punished, but not doomed to die; it’s your humiliation and debasement before a crowed people are there for. If it’s an event run by criminals instead, that show, that debasement, has no limits.

Lower Class: You’re a competitor, either just getting started or with a history of losing long enough to have gained no ground, becoming a reliable extra. Gladiatorial arenas are full of such hopefuls, who have not risen past the starting line.

Middle Class: Gladiators are just another trade after all, and knowing ones trade enough to be considered competent opens new doors. Locals will know your name, and you’ll have earned enough to be considered a moderate success.

Upper Class: You’re a rich and famous gladiator, who may be touring the country you are in or making some further notoriety for yourself. Expect to have some dedicated fans and followers who cheer you on every match.

Bottom Rung: Born to a low life pit fodder, usually a criminal, thrown against opponents they cannot beat to warm up the crowed. Not necessarily doomed to die, they are the clowns and entertainers, beaten, humiliated, and debased before the crowed. If it’s run by criminals, there’s no limits; perhaps your conception was even part of the show?

Lower Class: Child of a competitor, either just getting started, or stuck with a history of losing. Gladiatorial arenas are full of such hopefuls, who have not risen past the starting line, but they can still teach you a trick or two.

Middle Class: You’re supported by a gladiator parent, and one competent enough for people to have heard of. They’ll have something to teach their child, and you may inherit a name that can open some doors later on.

Upper Class: You’ll be child to a rich and famous gladiator, touring the world or perhaps retired with their winnings. Theirs will be a far reaching reputation, and they’ll certainly be able to teach you some tricks.

objects.title: Assassin
objects.text: A knife in the dark, a slip of poison in the bedroom, some convoluted trap, or just beating someone to death. As long as the person they’re hired to kill is dead, the mission is a success and the pay can line their pockets. Whether freelance or part of a guild, their methods are their own.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: You are an ‘assassin’ as much as a knife or poison is: a disposable tool owned by the actual expert, used through threat without your choice, until you dull or break. Perhaps it’s doing the deed, or tempting the target with your body. Your ‘cut’ is a pittance and your risk is sky high.
Lower Class: You’re more a thug than an assassin. Some criminal pays you to kill someone, you stab them in an alley, you collect your pay. It is murder without subtlety and the pay reflects that.

Middle Class: More of a skilled assailant, you know the craft of breaking and entering, slipping poison and knife and fulfilling more esoteric requirements. Infiltration and seduction play more of a role.

Upper Class: A master assassin, whose incredible skills are matched by an incredible pay. Few, if any, know both your profession and your personal life, yet even the most difficult to kill know the name you work by, living in fear of the day you come to call. A difficult reputation to live up to.

Bottom Rung: You’ll be raised not by an assassin, but by their tool: someone used through coercion until breaking. Perhaps they’ll be the lookout, or informant, or a method of sexual entrapment. Perhaps the assassin is your other parent, but they do not care for you, nor for the one who does.

Lower Class: More a thug than an assassin. Some criminal pays your guardian to kill someone, so they stab them in an alley, then collect the pay. It is murder without subtlety and the pay reflects that. They can teach you, but if they can look you in the eye while doing so, you may not want them to.

Middle Class: Born to more of a skilled assailant; one who knows the craft of stealth, seduction, and the slip of poison or knife. Able to fulfilling more esoteric requests, they’ll be paid more than a thug, and may teach you their craft if they don’t want you as far away from it as possible.

Upper Class: You’re the child of a master assassin, whose incredible skills are matched by an incredible pay. Few, if any, can link the mysterious wealth of your household with your protector, but if they are inclined, they may share their secrets and techniques with their next generation.

objects.title: Harem Member
objects.text: Someone who’s placed, by their own will or someone else’s, into the power of a powerful person, to be used as they see fit. This is usually in a sexual sense, being the comfort or decoration on someone’s arm, but there is neither security nor monogamy in it: their position is contingent upon their master’s whims.

addons.text: Not a Virgin: Your position is most assuredly a sexual one, your use having been repeated many times by your controlling benefactor.
A Virgin: You’re there to look pretty mostly, and perhaps to kiss and touch. The taking of your sweetest prize is sure to happen soon.

Lower Class: You’re the sweet to a gang or bandit leader, or any who would be high among the lows. You’ll be seen with your hands on their arm or your head in their lap, but lose favour with them and you be a favour shared with their friends.

Middle Class: One of the many lovers of your sugar-other. On their arm at parties and their bed at night, willing to do anything, even feign affection, to have your rent paid for you. Jealousy can only flow one way, though you may make friends and fun with the ‘others’ you share them with.

Upper Class: You’re a plaything owned and housed by the wealthy elite, given fine foods and shown the finest toys; one of many that your wealthy possessor enjoys spending time with. You’ll be constantly fighting for their affection though, to stay relevant in their heart and mind. Otherwise, the streets are never far away.

Lower Class: Your parent is the property of a gang or bandit leader; any who would be high among the lows. Your other parent is likely in charge, but bastard children to property leaves little love or protection inherited. So long as the lesser parent plays their part, food, shelter, and perhaps a job will be yours.

Middle Class: Your parent is one of many hangers on to someone else; perhaps affair to someone rich. With you, a new born bastard arrived, you could be leverage for and easy life, though little love from your wealthier parent. Perhaps they will look out for you as well, but perhaps not.

Upper Class: You’re a harem child, your parent one of many to serve and service their wealthy master. You may grow up with a place in their household, or be kicked out should your parent get too old. In the former case, a limited education and a job will be given. Hopefully not the same that birthed you.

objects.title: Societal Trophy
objects.text: The role of some can be to play no role at all: to be an ornament of a person that decorates society while contributing nothing to it directly. From hostages and conquered kings, to spare royals and nobles, beauties, and guests too valuable to let go. Free from Work, but caged for the privilege.

addons.text: Older Age: Caught by a degeneration of the mind, you’re being looked after as a venerable elder entering into what may be your final years. Letting you wonder off won’t be allowed, and giving you responsibilities will be seen as irresponsible. A quest for the power may have you seen as a Don Quixote type.

Bottom Rung or Classless: You’re a prisoner, whose punishment is outweighed by people seeing you’re alive. Perhaps you are the child of a hated enemy, or a conquered bandit leader, a failed traitor or heinous criminal, or just a figurehead to be torn down. Expect to be paraded about, pelted with all sorts by angry crowds, but at least fed, and probably clothed.

Upper Class: You’re a trophy of nobility, and will be given the highest respect and the most lavish of accommodations, invited to all the parties to be shown off. Perhaps it’s as a beauty on the arm of another, or a ward or ignorant hostage, or someone famous: the latest fad or gossip story.

Ruling Class: You’re perhaps the royal of another kingdom, usurped by some illegitimate claimant, and kept so their claim can be used as an excuse for war. A political tool at best, whose opinions are far less valuable than their simple presence. Can be quite dangerous, and very restrictive.

Bottom Rung or Classless: The child of a prisoner, whose punishment is outweighed by people seeing them alive. A hated enemy, or a conquered bandit leader, a failed traitor or heinous criminal, or just a figurehead to be torn down. Perhaps you are a result of their brutal public punishment, but you’ll certainly share in their ignominy, and be born into an uncertain future.

Upper Class: A trophy of nobility, raised with respect and lavish accommodations, born to perhaps a beauty on the arm of another, or a ward, or an ignorant hostage, or someone famous. Or perhaps your oddities have left you for study: a freak to be shown off or pitied.

Ruling Class: You’re born as royal of another conquered kingdom, usurped by some illegitimate claimant, and kept so your family claim can be pushed as an excuse for war. How much of your family remains is up to you, the likelihood of your ascension to be decided later. Can be a dangerous and restrictive fate.

objects.title: Noble
objects.text: The elite of society, who manage its various territories, peoples, and goals. As rich aristocrats, it’s inevitable that that majority see to their own gains before other people’s problems. While they may be the kind to engage in dangerous politics, you’ll nevertheless start out rich and powerful.

addons.text: Upper Class: You’re either a city noble, managing estates and businesses from a town house manner, or a country noble, overseeing the mines, farms, and other taxable productions on your land. Both must play the courts, though both get further by joining an existing power block of aristocrats.

Ruling Class: You’re not a royal, but you’re among those pushing to be. The nobles of the inner circle, the powerful houses, whose vast holdings may get them to the big seat through foul means over fair. When they move in court, others are swept along, and loosing step may leave you behind, or be outright fatal.

Upper Class: Born to either a city noble, managing estates and businesses from a town house manner, or a country noble, overseeing the mines, farms, and other taxable productions on their land. You’ll get a robust education and many opportunities, being safe and looked after.

Ruling Class: Born to a noble family of the inner circles of power; they jockey for the big seat, through foul means over fair. Many plans will be placed on you, both for your perceived gain and your destruction, but you’ll get a flawless education and a powerful role to play.

objects.title: Royalty
objects.text: Above mere nobles, they carry blood ties of inheritance and a right to rule. While all nobles have some claim and may even inherit should a few hundred people die, royals are separated by only a few dozen places: a family made up of siblings, cousins, parents and children, whose bickering can have deadly consequences.

addons.text: Upper Class: You’re among the lowest of the high, perhaps a distant cousin to the king or queen. You’re one whose power has been successfully limited, so much that, while you hold the royal name, you’re unlikely to ever inherit. That leaves you as good marriage material for lesser royal alliances.

Ruling Class: You're a part of the royal family, but not directly in line for the throne. Perhaps if a dozen people were to die, it could happen. Otherwise, as a spare, you’re mostly used to secure high value alliances through marriage, act as a diplomat, or bring prestige to the family in other ways.

Upper Class: Born to the lowest of the highest, a distant cousin to the king or queen whose family connections leave you born into tremendous wealth and power. They’ll be more eyes on you than a typical noble, and plans for your marriage when you’re older, but your name will give great weight to your every action.

Ruling Class: A part of the royal family, but not directly in line for the throne. Perhaps a nephew to the king, or a ward, or a legitimised bastard. Should perhaps a few dozen die, you could inherit, but until then you’ll be raised in the royal household, with all the burdens and opportunities that brings.

objects.title: Royal Heir
objects.text: A prince or princess, the child of kings and queens and in line for the throne. There may be others before you if you have older siblings, but as a child of a monarch, your life will be more valued and perhaps more restricted than any other, putting you in a position harder to break out of than any prison.

addons.text: Dormienties Location: As a scion of Dormienties royalty, you will likely be the child of the King and/or Queen chosen previously.
As a Resident: You may be a prince or princess, or even the king or queen if the position is free.
As a New-born: You’ll be born a prince or princess. Expect some celebration of your arrival.

objects.title: Cultist
objects.text: One of the hoard that worships forces bigger than themselves. It is the work of the religious, be they moderate or zealous, and as there are many religions within this world, it could be an official faith, or a subversive cabal. Unless otherwise stated, this is most likely to be a Soporatus Cult member.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: You’re a zealot who has nothing but the rags on their back, preaching at street corners until your voice is hoarse. Even in a world where gods are real, it is rare for such deities to answer such uncomfortable fanaticism; any voices that do speak in your head are not to be trusted.

Lower Class: You’re an initiate member of a faith, working in groups while adhering to their tenants. These are usually the poor, feigning piety to get a meal and shelter, and so the work they are given is often difficult and demeaning. Stick with it and you could rise in time.

Middle Class: You’re a risen member of a faith, ministering to congregations and managing the day to day affairs of the religion. Perhaps a priest or priestess, working in a city, village temple, or isolated monastery.

Upper Class: You’re a leader within the faith, guiding others in a position of respect and holding power over other members. Perhaps you’re even held up as an idol of reverence, a symbol of the tenants of your faith. Powerful adherents may deal with you directly for their prayers.

Classless: You’re of the more sinister cultists. From witches thralls and demon worshipers, to the mind slaves of dark outer beings, these religious adherents are usually far more fanatical, expendable, and unthinking than other faiths. Your choice as to what power holds your leash.

Bottom Rung: Born to a zealot who has nothing but the rags on their back, preaching at street corners until their voice is hoarse. Perhaps they truly do hear voices. Perhaps they don’t come from their god. Either way, expect to be raised with some warped beliefs.

Lower Class: Born to an initiate member of a faith. These are usually the poor, feigning piety to get a meal and shelter, and when pregnant, they are usually runaways or prostitutes. You’ll be raised in a poor temple, raised to abide by the gods who gave you succour.

Middle Class: Not all religions are celibate, but if the one you’re born to is, expect the cause to be tragic. Child of a priest, priestess, or both, working in a city, village temple, or isolated monastery; expect to be raised in a very religious household, and taught how to abide by divine teachings.

Upper Class: Not all religions are celibate; if the one you’re born to is, expect the cause to have been unwanted. Born to a temple leader or an idol of reverence: a symbol of their tenants. You’ll gain their reflected glory, and may be seen as holy yourself. Their political connections will be inherited as well.

Classless: Born to a more sinister cultist, be it a witches thrall, or demon worshiper, or the mind slave of a dark outer being. Perhaps conceived or born through ritual, you’ll have a perceived or real connection to whatever power you are raised under, surrounded by some truly disturbed people.

objects.title: Witch
objects.text: Mostly, but not exclusively women, it is a job of magic and natural arts, ranging from a less creditable alchemist and midwife, to a member of a witches cult casting outlawed magic over bones and sacrifices. Generally, anyone with self-taught, home grown, or inefficient magic is a witch.

addons.text: Bottom Rung: You’re an apostate witch of society, presumed to be with magic you cannot be trusted to wield. While this means being hunted and killed, there are more opportunities to find work among criminals, though the danger is always at your heels.

Lower Class: You’re a ‘witch’, brewing potions, making charms, telling the future, and warding off curses. Your ‘solutions’ work for most of your customers, as long as they’re superstitious and ignorant. Your mutterings and dried grasses have little actual magic behind them though.

Middle Class: You’re a working witch, from a self-taught family. This can be good work depending on your skills and reputation, from healing embarrassing illnesses and brewing contraceptives, to undoing curses and prophesising the future.

Classless: You’re a wild witch, possibly part of a coven or cult. These are the feared kind, and while some are good, travelling and blessing crops for coin or shelter, others kidnap, kill, and curse, sacrificing others to increase their own power.

Bottom Rung: Born to an apostate witch of society, with magic they cannot be trusted to wield. You may be seen as tainted as well, both marked for death, but there are opportunities to find work among criminals. You may be raised by someone who can show you a trick or two, should they live.

Lower Class: You’re born to a ‘witch’, who brews potions, makes charms, tell the future, and ward off curses. It won’t take long for you to figure out they don’t work, but as long as the con continues, you’ll have food and shelter. When it doesn’t, you may have to move, and quickly.

Middle Class: Born into a family of working witches, their craft can be good work depending on their skills, brewing potions and curing curses, either for real or relying on deception. Depending on gender or family traditions, they may teach you what they know.

Classless: Born to a wild witch, possibly part of a coven or cult. These are the feared kind, and while some are good, others kidnap and kill, sacrificing others to increase their own power. You may have been conceived in ritual, born with a purpose, and may be raised in the shadow of their forbidden magic’s.

objects.title: Tribesman
objects.text: Part of a classless society, where every member helps with the work that needs doing, no matter what it is. They usually travel in large groups, and can be hostile, being viewed as stupid, or simply more in tune with the natural world, but definitely freer. Orc society is a lot of this.

objects.title: Shaman
objects.text: Essentially a magical tribesman, but the power they possess varies. Some can change the weather, while others only brew potions. The duties they have go beyond magic, memorising stories and legends, tending to the spiritual needs of the tribe, and administrating rituals and ceremonies.

objects.title: Bandit
objects.text: Criminals that work outside of cities, flaunting their violence and greed to the open wilds of nature. Due to the hostility of the wilderness, these brigands are considered a class of their own, made up of those cut off from society, and often quickly culled to their stronger members.

objects.title: Traveller
objects.text: Gypsies, in another sense: folk who adhere to their own small civilisation and take it with them wherever they go. More accepted than tribals, but not by much, they can arrive outside cities and trade for weeks, until they grow bored or are chased off. A romantic lifestyle, but dangerous.

objects.title: Close the How
objects.text: Return to the choice of arrival.

rows.title: The Where is set, the How is decided…
rows.titleText:
Like a being caught in a whirlpool, you feel drawn toward your new life, falling endlessly down toward it, yet getting no clearer. There is still work to do, but now at least you feel you can do that work, safe in the knowledge of the changeable things that will change no further.

What is your next step? Well, if your new life has taught you anything, it is that there is no certainty, and so you will next need to prepare yourself, either gathering energies to soften the blows sustained elsewhere, or to reap the rewards of miseries chosen.

objects.title: Your Destination is Decided
objects.text:
Select this to unlock the other section of The World In Sight, taking one step closer to your new life.

Requires a location be chosen, along with one of the three arrival types.

objects.title: Close Arrival
objects.text: Return to the world in sight.

rows.title: The Great Blessings of the Self-made
rows.titleText:
As before, in the raw dream, as now; pursuing bliss and wonder and all that you seek brings barriers to progress, blinding and destabilising. Change, the force of the lucid dreamer, can only change so much before waking, and you shudder to think what would happen here, should you grow too unbalanced in your final steps.

And yet, what is the point of a dream without fulfilling some fantasy? Outside of the potential joys, you will need power to get power, and the boons you can give yourself here will be the difference between success and failure in that regard.

You think for a dizzying moment, all the ways you could grant yourself power enough to succeed, and comfort enough to smooth your ride before doing so.

objects.title: Increasing Stats
objects.text: The most basic and most influential of changes.

objects.title: Gifts
objects.text: Blessings born with your body, innate and natural.

objects.title: Immunities
objects.text: Armour to protect yourself within a hostile world.

objects.title: Talents
objects.text: Natural proficiency. Fertile soil for skills unlearned.

objects.title: Knowledge
objects.text: Information, skill, comprehension given, years unspent.

objects.title: Experiences
objects.text: Events not yet happened, placed upon your path.

rows.title: Increasing Your Stats
rows.titleText:
To reduce a person down to a mathematical formula is just a useful abstraction. It is one with which you can examine yourself without subtlety or pretext, and tweak your abilities in the most general, and thus most balanced, sense. Without them, increasing your strength in specific may leave your own punches breaking your arms, but working in aggregate will keep your bodies balance, from lightning punches to steel abdominals to the thunder of your blinking eyelids.

You consider the categories for this, first in body and then in mind. As one number, one scale, is no better than another, you place 5 as the average available for a typical human. With a new body and an unfettered mind, starting yourself off as that average seems fair. You can always nudge some up and some down to compensate, either here or through intensive training, which can shift your points up by a couple depending on the effort. The stats below are simply the baseline.

Once chosen, these will be hard to change, but possible. Magic and potion can give temporary dexterity, for example, and hard training can give it in a longer lasting form. You’ll naturally shift to your base though, over time, like a genetic pre-disposition, but truly permanent changes can be granted through the rare blessings of powerful outer realm beings. Also, unfortunately, this extends to permanent debuffs, like curses, as well, which are very difficult to remove.

objects.title: Added Strength
objects.text: The physical strength of the body. If endurance is what your body can take of the world, strength is how much you can physically effect the world around you. A world of armoured men and armoured beasts, and where might so often makes right. This is vital for any physical combatant to achieve victory.

addons.text: Strength 1 or less - Your very body is too heavy to lift, your arms and legs too weak to rise and effect the world. You have all the strength of someone dying from a wasting illness, limiting your ability to do even the most basic tasks of looking after yourself.

Strength 2 - Your physical strength is no longer an adorable nuisance, now being very low, inhibiting your ability to do basic tasks, like opening doors or picking up objects. You will be completely at the mercy of anyone who gets close to you.

Strength 3 - You are weak. Fighting physically against all but the most wispy of opponents will be laughable, along with opening heavy doors or doing manual labour. You will crumple under many of the burdens others carry.
Strength 4 - You’re below the average that could be expected of you, needing help to lift heavy things, and generally being a bit of a weakling.
Strength 5 - The average strength for your race, build, and gender. Unremarkable to most in the same weight class.
Strength 6 - You have an above average physical strength, same as that possessed by someone who works a physical job day to day, only yours is a natural baseline.
Strength 7 - You have high strength, same as that of a warrior, whose life relies on being stronger than their opponent.

Strength 8 - A powerfully high strength, same as someone who trains regularly or takes few breaks from some very demanding labour. Opponents that train to wear heavy armour and weald large blunt weapons must reach this kind of strength.

Strength 9 - The few mortals who would reach this strength would be those who obsess with it and dedicate much of their time to its development, even at the expense of other things, like skills or tactics. Strongmen who can lift others over their heads, or throw great weights long distances in competition with each other.

Strength 10 - The strongest a mortal can reach through work, and a new record for your kind. This is the strength that crushes others, giving bare hands an easy killing force. Lifting the weight of a fully laden horse will surely bring about gasps of amazement from watchers, just as cleaving through steel will bring cries of despair from your foes.

Strength 11 to 13 - Beyond mortal strength: the ability to tear a man limb from limb with your bear hands. Your fists become sledgehammers and your weapons strike like booming thunder, and the thickest armour feels as light as winter clothes.

Strength 14 to 16 - You can shatter stone and rend steel with a fist, throwing whole groups of men terminal distances. Yours is a strength used to wrestle great beasts, leap cities, and hurl great boulders; it will bring fame and fear, even unto demons and the beings of the outer realms.

Strength 17 to 19 - Your steps can shatter the ground and cross continents in leaps. A sweep of your hand could cut a man in half, and no weight, not even a mountain, could keep you pinned. It is a strength that divine beings fear, able to shatter even immaterial forms, your stronger blows distorting reality itself.

Strength >20 - The strength of a god. Technically, you can never land a strike against another at full strength, for the shockwave of one punch would burn air and flesh and break apart matter before it can even travel through it. Such strength should not exist within anything as delicate as reality.

Endurance 6 or less: Powerful strength may still damage a weak body, as a strong punch will not break your arm, but the steel you shatter with it may. Only strong weapons can carry your strength safely, and unless they are reinforced, perhaps only once.

Endurance 8 or less: Powerful strength may still damage a weak body, as a strong punch will not break your arm, but the steel you shatter with it may. Only strong weapons can carry your strength safely, and unless they are reinforced, perhaps only once.

Endurance 10 or less: Powerful strength may still damage a weak body, as a strong punch will not break your arm, but the steel you shatter with it may. Only strong weapons can carry your strength safely, and unless they are reinforced, perhaps only once.

objects.title: Added Dexterity
objects.text: The ability to move with precision and speed; a vital trait for any ranger, bowman, or lightly armoured combatant. Also governs your flexibility and general kinaesthetic intellect, required for acrobatics, dancing, stealth, and deft action of any kind. It doesn’t give you skills like lock picking, but you’ll be able to learn them much more easily.

addons.text: Dexterity 1 or less - Your dexterity is as nil as a quadruple amputee. Perhaps that is the case, or perhaps your body is so unresponsive that you need others to feed you. Walking won’t be happening, but you could still live wheeled around by carers, who would need to do even the simplest tasks for you.
Dexterity 2 - Your lack of bodily mobility has a noticeable impact upon your life, slowing even the most simple of tasks that now require multiple attempts to perform.
Dexterity 3 - You’re undexterous, with hands that shake where precision is needed and two left feet that see each other as bitter enemies. Your body is saddled with stiff and awkward movement.
Dexterity 4 - Below average dexterity. Expect to be considered somewhat clumsy, being more inclined to fall or drop things.
Dexterity 5 - An average dexterity that lets you walk normally, without falling on your face.
Dexterity 6 - Above average dexterity. You’ll rarely trip and have a natural quickness and grace to your movements.
Dexterity 7 - You’re a very dextrous person, able to move quickly and accurately. This is a level reached by professional assassins, pickpockets, and anyone who works hard to have their work unseen.
Dexterity 8 - Yours is the level of great acrobats and contortionists, street runners and famous archers. Your hands move so quickly, it can be hard for the average eye to follow them.

Dexterity 9 - Your moves are incredibly fluid, lending themselves to close combat very well. In terms of finesse, there are few who could match you, let alone beat you, and if they try you can slip, run, or sneak away without fear of being caught.

Dexterity 10 - Yours is truly a cat like agility. Natural: a grace and fluidity that cannot be trained, only born with. Double if not triple jointed, able to escape near any bonds, fast and skilled. A blur, a shadow, and a beauty in your movements.

Dexterity 11 to 13 - Beyond mortal limits, you have a grace that you can use from which even eyes cannot hold onto, the sights of people slipping away, their minds rejecting the style and poise of which you’re capable. Your natural skills leave you able to strike any object with any weapon, and able to dodge any targeted strikes in turn.

Dexterity 14 to 16 - Should you pick something up, your body will work out how to use it before your brain does. The unnatural understanding of your physical abilities leaves anything a weapon, becoming an extension of your will the moment you touch it. You can dodge the undogable, like wide spells and far reaching curses.

Dexterity 17 to 19 - You’re able to move so smoothly that some would doubt you moved at all, slipping through light and shadow with such ability that you can travel further than you move, leaving you a dizzyingly untrackable opponent.

Dexterity >20 - You can move with such grace that mortal (and many immortal) eyes simply cannot see you, even standing before them. Your speed is without equal, not just in the blur of your hands, but in the way you travel, an acrobatic through space and time.

Perception 6 or less: The art of reacting and striking and slipping through necessitates a good perception of the world. Without this, your perfect movements are more likely to hit a brick wall, figuratively and literally, and while you can react quickly to it, you’re more often leaping before you look.

Perception 8 or less: The art of reacting and striking and slipping through necessitates a good perception of the world. Without this, your perfect movements are more likely to hit a brick wall, figuratively and literally, and while you can react quickly to it, you’re more often leaping before you look.

Perception 10 or less: The art of reacting and striking and slipping through necessitates a good perception of the world. Without this, your perfect movements are more likely to hit a brick wall, figuratively and literally, and while you can react quickly to it, you’re more often leaping before you look.

objects.title: Added Endurance
objects.text: The robustness of the body and its ability to endure all thrown against it. This covers not just physical blows, but the ravishes of disease, age, and spirit. It carries reserves of energy against fatigue, and governs the recovery over time. A defensive skill, working only on yourself, at least outside of races and drinking competitions.

addons.text: Endurance 1 or less - Your own body barely has the strength to go on. A slight breeze could be the end of you, and all your vital organs seem on the brink of rebellion in the face of their terrible working conditions. You’d need a skilled healer just to keep you from dropping dead.

Endurance 2 - You’ll need a healer on standby to keep going, patching you up every time your paper skin gets cut, or you glass bones break, or a sickness most would shrug off lays you out. This is the life of the fragile invalid who can scarcely leave their bed.

Endurance 3 - Your bodies health is not great, leaving you fatigued long before the day is done, and wheezing after only moderate exercise. Illness is not uncommon, though semi-regular ministrations from a healer should keep you going.
Endurance 4 - Your endurance is below average, leaving you out of breath more quickly, and more susceptible to catching minor illnesses, like common colds.
Endurance 5 - An average amount of endurance. You can run, jump, and swim as well as anyone who does not do those things often.
Endurance 6 - Your endurance is above average, letting you run further, last longer, and shrug off minor sicknesses faster, should you even catch them at all.
Endurance 7 - You have a robust immune system, seeming to never get sick, and you can stay in combat as long as a full trained and seasoned warrior. A picture of health and fitness.

Endurance 8 - Your body is more than fit; it is hardy. Your bones are stronger, your muscles denser. A fall that may shatter another would leave you only bruised and bloody, and you could fight for hours, even while carrying a great weight of armour or a significant wound. Cuts heal quickly, and rarely leave a scar.

Endurance 9 - A blow that would lay another out may scarcely stagger you, and a feat that would leave another paralysed with exhaustion may hardly raise your breath. Few ever train their bodies to this extent as few need to, nor have the hours to sink into such a pursuit. For you it is a baseline.

Endurance 10 - The pinnacle of mortal endurance. When people tell tales of those who survive impossible odds, pushing themselves beyond, if only for a moment, it is this peak they reach, coming down through only death or salvation. It is here you live, able to endure more than the worst any could be expected to.

Endurance 11 to 13 - An endurance beyond mortal limits. Blades do not cut deeply; great wounds for another would be flesh wounds to you, and glancing blows leave barely a mark. You require less sleep, and always have some reserve of energy, no matter how tired you get. You’re not outright immune to disease, but can develop an immunity soon after catching, no matter what it is.

Endurance 14 to 16 - You can watch your wounds knit themselves closed, such is your healing, and you never run out of blood. You could be cut in half and so long as your brain is intact, you could grow yourself back in time. You do not get tired, or exhausted, and sleep is optional for you. Your body even shrugs off magical curses.

Endurance 17 to 19 - You do not age past your prime, and it takes only seconds to regrow whole limbs, leaving you frightfully difficult to kill. Food and water become semi-optional, needing very little to keep going at your very best, and even the worst diseases and poisons have no effect on you at all.

Endurance >20 - Immortality, of body at least. You could be reduced to dust and still return, yet there is very little that could render you so. Your skin is impenetrable, your bones unbreakable. Beware though, as your mind and will may not be so robust, and without strength against all imprisonment, this immortal life may become a terrible curse.

Will 6 or less: While you can take the hits, you still feel the pain. A lack of will may leave you unable to stand or emotionally bear an attack that you can take physically, leaving long term trauma and scars on the mind.

Will 8 or less: While you can take the hits, you still feel the pain. A lack of will may leave you unable to stand or emotionally bear an attack that you can take physically, leaving long term trauma and scars on the mind.

Will 10 or less: While you can take the hits, you still feel the pain. A lack of will may leave you unable to stand or emotionally bear an attack that you can take physically, leaving long term trauma and scars on the mind.

objects.title: Added Perception
objects.text: More than mere sight and sound, perception is the interpretation of sensory information. It not only sharpens the senses, but lets you know how people feel and what’s coming next. It requires intelligence and wisdom to know why, but without either, you’ll be able to predict things and react to them without knowing the exact reason.

addons.text: Perception 1 or less - Functionally blind, deaf, and numb to the world, you’ll be at the mercy of everyone and everything around you, unable to predict anything that may come next.

Perception 2 - Your senses are generally dulled, or some are missing altogether. Anything unplanned will catch you unguarded, and both puzzles and mysteries will always be lacking some pieces, left unseen or unconnected in your periphery.

Perception 3 - With very little perception, from your perspective, most things just happen. Perhaps you can work out the cause afterward, but not in the moment, where ambush, unusual behaviour, and strange decision will come and go without you picking up any nuance.
Perception 4 - You have below average perception, leaving you surprised more often than most and able to miss details more easily.
Perception 5 - An average sense of perception. You notice things with your senses as well as anyone.
Perception 6 - You have above average perception. People will compliment you when you see or pickup on things that they missed.

Perception 7 - You’re very perceptive, carrying the skills of a detective or ranger. Tracking people and animals comes more easily, as well as picking up on small social cues most miss. Seeing lies or feints in attacks comes more easily as well.

Perception 8 - The studying of body language leave people as open books, their stoic thoughts and feeling as apparent as if they were laughing or crying. Your accuracy with ranged weapons is significantly improved as well.

Perception 9 - Adductive or deductive, your reasoning gets a tremendous boost, leaving you able to look about a scene and work out what happened, with each minor detail telling a story. In combat or game, you’re near untrickable, and it would take a master of stealth to hide from your sight.

Perception 10 - Your perceptions are at the limit of what can be considered perceptions, and while some may be able to reach such a height, most will think your abilities supernatural. From a glance at the clouds, you can tell the weather for the week, from the smell of food, you can tell who baked it, and from the sound of a step, you can tell if someone is left or right handed.

Perception 11 to 13 - Your senses become super-natural, enabling you to sense any attack before it happens. You can tell when something is about to go down before anyone, even the instigators know, and in combat, all the weaknesses of a typical opponent is revealed to you, from supernatural weaknesses to old wounds and trick knees.

Perception 14 to 16 - Your senses reach through reality, picking up on the spiritual realms and creeping outer forces. Concentrations of magical power are laid bare, and things hidden by walls or magical means are as clear to you as if they were laid out at your feet.

Perception 17 to 19 - Your perceptions reach through time, letting you see the past through its remnants, the histories of everything laid out to your mind, traceable from the present to its creation. Even the future can be compiled, echoing faintly back with confusing mirrored lines of distorted possibilities. With a strong enough mind or will, you could use this to shape events.

Perception >20 - Your senses are, without doubt, divine in their abilities. You can see beyond the horizon, hear words forming in peoples minds, smell the flowers that are yet seeds, and taste events a thousand years past. The meddling of the gods is clear to you, both in their schemes and in the creation of the world, their fingerprints as clear as oily residue. All of it flows easily, and can be ignored, but others may seek to use, or silence, such powerful abilities.

Intelligence 6 or less: Knowing what to look for and what to filter out, along with processing all the information your get, requires a mind that can keep up. Without this, you can still perceive the same, and react to it, but your mind may crack if you try to understand it.

Intelligence 8 or less: Knowing what to look for and what to filter out, along with processing all the information your get, requires a mind that can keep up. Without this, you can still perceive the same, and react to it, but your mind may crack if you try to understand it.

Intelligence 10 or less: Knowing what to look for and what to filter out, along with processing all the information your get, requires a mind that can keep up. Without this, you can still perceive the same, and react to it, but your mind may crack if you try to understand it.

objects.title: Added Charisma
objects.text: Physical beauty can leave others desiring you, and strength of will or arms can make them listen, but Charisma can make them respect you, and follow you, fighting and dying for your cause. The first rulers of Dormientes claimed their keys and their sliver of the power by leading armies on their quests. Perhaps you could do the same.

addons.text: Charisma 1 or less - You cannot communicate even basic ideas with others, your every word and gesture, or even your very existence being seen as an insult, and the result will be an outward hostility from everyone around you, turning you into a pariah, no matter what you do.

Charisma 2 - Making friends will be very difficult, if not impossible. You manner will be unfixably ‘off’ or even unnerving, and people will not trust you for it, even doing the opposite of what you ask in fear of your ulterior motives.

Charisma 3 - The charisma of a wall flower. Prepare to be ignored or dismissed if you try to initiate a conversation, requiring hostility and insult to be heard, your stammering presence treated as an irritation. You can still earn respect through action, making friendships and ‘being the quiet one’ or ‘good in small doses’, but keeping it monosyllabic should keep people from your throat or treating you as disposable.
Charisma 4 - Below average charisma, you’ll struggle to convince anyone of your point of view, but can do so with time and effort.
Charisma 5 - An average charisma, able to interact with others and negotiate for what you want within reason.
Charisma 6 - Above average charisma, allowing you to smoothly interact with others and be a much more personable person.

Charisma 7 - Buying and selling goods will become much easier and more profitable for you as you take on a salesman’s charm, and the traits of a leader will have others looking to you for direction. Your skills at song, story, and dance will be much easier to cultivate, should you choose.

Charisma 8 - Talking others into doing things for you, be it fighting for you or joining you in bed, will be quite easy. You have the effortless oratory of a captivating public speaker, and the unshakable outward confidence of someone utterly correct.

Charisma 9 - The rare charm that leads to celebrity status; others are drawn to your magnetism. Expect to be invited to a lot of parties, with the wealthy elite paying you for your presence. You have the stance of a hero, and the gravitas of a king.

Charisma 10 - Your presence is a sun that all bask in, your words, your stance, your smile, all the thing of champions, yet all within the realms of possibility. Just from talking to people, they will assume your greatness, and it will take very little to form armies and have songs sung about you.

Charisma 11 to 13 - Entering into the magic charms of faye creatures, your words more irresistible, your suggestions seen as automatically correct, even if absurd. This is not mind control, but something far more dangerous, and far harder to guard against. Persuasion.

Charisma 14 to 16 - When you speak, others listen, be they friend or foe. Your words cut to their hearts, breaking their will or fortifying their resolve, and even heavenly or infernal beings may smile and stop and listen, caught in your presence like a ship in a whirlpool.

Charisma 17 to 19 - Enemies, be they man or beast, may throw down their weapons and kneel before you, such is the authority you emanate. Your words are right, following them is good, and even divinity may be captivated by the radiance of your personality.

Charisma >20 - You are the epitome of persuasion. Your stories could convince gods to cry and demons to repent. Your suggestions could make birds dig and fish fly. Even stone faced reality may bend to accommodate you, made unsure of itself by the glow of your smile, or desperate to correct the crease of your frown.

Will 6 or less: Without a strong conviction, words are just words. As compelling as they are, lacking the ability to stand in the face of resolute opposition will make convincing people to change their minds much harder.

Will 8 or less: Without a strong conviction, words are just words. As compelling as they are, lacking the ability to stand in the face of resolute opposition will make convincing people to change their minds much harder.

Will 10 or less: Without a strong conviction, words are just words. As compelling as they are, lacking the ability to stand in the face of resolute opposition will make convincing people to change their minds much harder.

objects.title: Added Intelligence
objects.text: Your mind is perhaps your strongest weapon, yet be careful. Without the hands to wield it, be they the convictions of those who follow you or your own strength elsewhere, it is no more than a thought in a jar; a sharp sword collecting dust. There is nothing worse than knowing the answer and being powerless to enact it.

addons.text: Intelligence 1 or less - You have no mind and suffer the blissful ignorance of the drooling vegetable.
Intelligence 2 - You are, at best, clinically retarded, with a mind that goes no further in complex thought than that of a young child.

Intelligence 3 - You are what epitomises a stupid person, using crude, brutish, and ineffectual solutions to your problems. Perhaps you can power through, but it’ll be harder going than it should be, and you won’t know why.
Intelligence 4 - The slower side of average. A depressing number of people are here so at least you will not be alone.
Intelligence 5 - The mind of an average person, no faster, no slower. Your thoughts flow with a typical agility.
Intelligence 6 - The quicker side of average. More flexible in thought than most, but still ‘normal’ in mind. People may comment upon the reliability of your memory, or the danger of your quick wit.
Intelligence 7 - You are a typical smart person, taking to complex subjects like engineering and strategy, and recalling things not actively committed to memory with ease.

Intelligence 8 - You are considered very intelligent. Subjects like genetics, advanced magical theorem, and grand strategy, come easily to you, as long as they capture your interest. Very often, you’ll reliably be the smartest person in the room.

Intelligence 9 - You are in the highest percentiles of intelligence, where great inventors, composers, theorists, and wizards lie. Such people are dotted throughout history, their impressive passing usually noted.

Intelligence 10 - Your mind is at the maximum limit of human intellect: the new smartest. Like any record, one would hope it will be beaten soon enough, and perhaps it will, but for now, you can guarantee being the smarted mortal in the world not backed by external forces. Your memory will be flawless and your speed of thought unmatched by any peers.

Intelligence 11 to 13 - Were you a character in a book, your intellect rises to the point of being unrealistic, with many Machiavellian schemes coming quickly and easily. This means you have surpassed mortal limits, and plenty of immortals as well, but to some of the true intellects out there, you’re still just a child.

Intelligence 14 to 16 - Your mind is considered powerful, even among powerful minds. Creatures drawn to intelligence, who live in the high arenas of mind, be they divine gods, scheming demons, or hungering mind flayers, will come to you to sample your intellect, though conversation or less savoury means, and use it for their own ends if they can.

Intelligence 17 to 19 - You reach the kind of intellectual heights where games against gods of mind can be played, should you get their attention. You may not win, but you can give them a run for their money. As for the mortal word, stupid and violent as it is, you’ll be as safe as a genius among monsters; your mind will be beyond mortal comprehension, and the problems of people will seem trivial to solve.

Intelligence >20 - There are horrifying creatures of the deepest deep, whose simplest thoughts are like planets teeming with life and whose memories stretch beyond the earliest dawn of time. To them, who are able to look into the beating heart of the universe and make it flinch, your mind is an unknowable terrifying horror, utterly beyond their comprehension.

Wisdom 6 or less: Without the understanding of other people’s point of view, you’ll be unable to relate to others properly, struggling to understand their more limited perspective. You’re also more likely to be less grounded, getting lost in thought more easily.

Wisdom 8 or less: Without the understanding of other people’s point of view, you’ll be unable to relate to others properly, struggling to understand their more limited perspective. You’re also more likely to be less grounded, getting lost in thought more easily.

Wisdom 10 or less: Without the understanding of other people’s point of view, you’ll be unable to relate to others properly, struggling to understand their more limited perspective. You’re also more likely to be less grounded, getting lost in thought more easily.

objects.title: Added Wisdom
objects.text: If intelligence is the tool, wisdom is the hand that wealds it. Wisdom helps you empathise with others, keeping you ‘normal’ and able to relate to them, despite your fame, intellect, will, or perceptions. It helps you understand yourself and thus get the best of yourself. It helps you speak in a relatable manner when leading or negotiating with others, and generally helps any pursuit.

addons.text: Wisdom 1 or less - The world is incomprehensible to you, it’s people like aliens, its laws and rules senseless mazes where logic doesn’t even begin to apply. There are undead with more empathy, blind people with more foresight, and dying people with less fear.

Wisdom 2 - You’re in your own little world most of the time, distracted by things that matter very little, to the point of being blind to much around you. Problems are rarely solved, plans are never made, and you may need someone to make sure you remember to eat from time to time.

Wisdom 3 - A complete scatter brain, always late, always distracted, and unable to conceive of why that would upset other people unless they explain it to you. Understanding the basics of Ki is impossible.
